This surah is Madani.

{1} Almighty God opened this surah with a command to fear Him (taqwa), an exhortation to worship Him, and a command to maintain ties of kinship (silat al-arham) along with an exhortation to do so. He also explained the motivating reason behind each of these. The reason that obliges taqwa is that He is your Lord, {who created you} and provided for you and nurtured you with His great blessings, among which is your creation {from a single soul} and His making {from it its mate} so that it would be suited to it, so that it would find rest in her, the blessing would be completed by this, and joy would be attained through it. Likewise, among the motivations that call you to His taqwa is that you ask by Him and glorify Him, to the extent that when you wish to fulfil your needs and aims, you invoke Him in your request, so that whoever wants something from another says: "I ask you by God to do such-and-such a thing," because of his knowledge of the glorification of God that is in his heart, which calls for not rejecting one who asks by God. So just as you have glorified Him in this way, so you should glorify Him by worshipping Him and fearing Him. Likewise, the statement that He is Watchful (raqib), i.e., that He observes the servants in their movements and stillnesses, their secret and open affairs, and all their conditions, watching over them in them, which requires that they watch over themselves before Him and feel intense shame before Him by adhering to His taqwa. And in the statement that He created them from a single soul, and that He scattered them throughout the regions of the earth while they return to one origin, [there is a lesson] so that some of them would show compassion toward others and soften toward one another.

He joined the command to fear Him with the command to be dutiful to the ties of kinship and the prohibition of severing them, in order to affirm this right, and that just as it is obligatory to uphold the right of God, so too it is obligatory to uphold the rights of created beings, especially the nearest of them, indeed upholding their rights is part of the right of God which God has commanded. Reflect on how He opened this surah with the command to taqwa, the maintaining of ties of kinship, and spouses in general; then afterwards He detailed these matters in the most complete detail from the beginning of the surah to its end, as though it is built upon these mentioned matters, elaborating what was stated in summary and clarifying what was left ambiguous.

In His saying {and created from it its mate}: there is an indication of the need to observe the rights of husbands and wives and to fulfil them, because wives are created from husbands; so between them and their wives there is the closest kinship, the strongest connection, and the most secure bond.

And His exalted saying:

{2} This is the first of the rights of creation that He enjoins in this surah, namely the orphans, who have lost their fathers who used to sustain them, and who are young and weak, unable to manage their own affairs. So the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate (al-Ra'uf al-Rahim), commands His servants to deal kindly with them, not to approach their wealth except in the best manner, and to give them their wealth—when they reach maturity and become of sound judgment (rushd)—complete and unreduced. And He commands them not to substitute the bad (al-khabith), which is the eating of the orphan's wealth without right, {for the good (al-tayyib)}, which is the lawful that involves no sin or accountability. {And do not consume their wealth along with your own wealth}; that is, together with your own wealth. This is a warning about the ugliness of consuming their wealth in this manner, when a person has been made independent by the provision God has granted him in his own property. Whoever dares to do this has committed {a great sin (hawban kabiran)}; that is, a tremendous wrong and a grave burden.

Among the forms of substituting the bad for the good is that the guardian takes the precious part of the orphan's property and puts in its place the base part of his own property.

In this verse is the establishment of guardianship over the orphan, because the necessary consequence of handing over the orphan's property to him is the establishment of the authority of the one who hands it over over that property. It also contains the command to improve the orphan's property, because the completion of handing it over is to preserve it and to manage it in a way that improves and grows it, and not to expose it to dangers and risks.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 3–4:

{3} That is: "And if you fear that you will not be just towards the orphan girls [who are] under your guardianship and care, and you fear that you will not fulfil their rights because you do not love them, then turn to others and marry {what seems good to you of women}"; i.e., those whom your choice has fallen upon, from among those who are religious, wealthy, beautiful, of noble lineage and descent, and other qualities that call one to marry them. So choose according to your judgment, and among the best qualities to choose is religiousness, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her beauty, for her lineage, and for her religion. So win the one who is religious; may your hands be rubbed with dust (i.e., may you prosper)." In this verse is the indication that a person should choose before marriage. Indeed, the Lawgiver has permitted him to look at the one he wishes to marry, so that he may be informed about his matter.

Then He mentioned the number of wives He permitted, saying: {two, three, or four}; i.e., whoever wishes to take two, let him do so; or three, let him do so; or four, let him do so, and he should not exceed that. This is because the verse was revealed to explain the favour (of Allah); so it is not permissible to exceed what Allah the Exalted has named, by consensus (ijma'). This is because a man's desire may not be satisfied by one wife, so he is permitted one after another until he reaches four, for in four there is sufficiency for everyone except the rare case. Yet, this permission is only granted when he is secure against himself of oppression and injustice and is confident of fulfilling their rights. If he fears any of this, then he should limit himself to one or to what his right hand possesses (i.e., slave-women), for he is not obligated to make division (qasm) among those whom his right hand possesses. {That}; i.e., limiting oneself to one or to what the right hand possesses, {is more likely that you will not be unjust}; i.e., that you will not wrong. In this is the point that if a servant exposes himself to a matter from which oppression and injustice and failure to fulfil an obligation are feared, even if it is permissible, it is not appropriate for him to expose himself to it; rather he should adhere to ease and well-being, for well-being is the best thing given to a servant.

{4} Since many people wronged women and diminished their rights, especially the dowry (sadaq), which is a large sum paid at once and is difficult for a wife to receive, He commanded and urged them to give women {their dowries (sadaqat)}, i.e., their bridal gifts {as a gift (nihlah)}; i.e., with good disposition and a state of tranquillity. So do not delay them or diminish any of it. In this is the indication that the dowry is to be handed to the woman if she is of age, and that she owns it by the contract, because He attributed it to her, and attribution implies ownership. {But if they give you of it willingly}; i.e., of the dowry, {a part (nafsan)}, by which they are gracious to you, with consent and choice, by waiving some of it or deferring it or exchanging it; {then consume it, with ease and satisfaction}; i.e., there is no blame upon you in that, nor any consequence. In this is evidence that a woman has the right to dispose of her property, even by way of donation, if she is mature of judgment; but if she is not, her gift has no legal effect. And that the guardian has no claim to any of the dowry other than what she willingly gives. In His saying {so marry what seems good to you of women} is evidence that marrying a corrupt woman is not commanded, but rather forbidden, like the polytheist woman and the adulterous woman; as Allah the Exalted said: {And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe}, and He said: {The adulterer marries none but an adulterer or a polytheist}.

And the saying of the Exalted:

And the saying of the Exalted:

{5} "Al-sufaha'" (the foolish/incompetent): plural of "safih," which refers to one who does not handle property well. This is either due to lack of intellect, like the insane and the mentally deficient and the like, or due to lack of maturity (rushd), like the minor and one who is not mature. So Allah forbade the guardians (awliya') from giving these people their property, for fear of its corruption and destruction, because Allah made property a means of sustenance (qiyam) for His servants in the interests of their religion and their worldly life. These people do not handle the management and preservation of it well. So Allah commanded the guardian not to give them their property, but rather to provide for them from it, clothe them, and spend from it on what relates to their necessities and their religious and worldly needs, and to speak to them with kind words (qawlan ma'rufan): that is, if they ask for it, promise them that they will hand it over to them after they attain maturity, and similar things, and be gentle in speech with them to console their hearts.

In attributing the property to the guardians (in His words, "your property"), there is an indication that they are obligated to deal with the property of the foolish just as they deal with their own property, in terms of preservation, management, and not exposing it to risks.

The verse is evidence that the maintenance of the insane, the minor, and the foolish comes from their own property if they have property, based on His words: "and provide for them from it and clothe them."

It is also evidence that the guardian's word is accepted regarding what he claims to have spent on maintenance and clothing within reason, because Allah made him a trustee over their property, so the word of the trustworthy must be accepted.

The trial (ibtila') is: testing and examination. This is done by giving the orphan who is near to maturity, and whose maturity is possible, some of his wealth, and letting him dispose of it in a manner fitting his condition; thereby his maturity is shown apart from his foolishness. If he continues not to handle it well, his wealth is not handed over to him, but he remains in his foolishness, even if he reaches a great age. If his maturity and soundness in managing his wealth become evident, and he reaches marriageable age, then: ﴿Hand over to them their wealth﴾ in full and abundant, ﴿and do not consume it extravagantly﴾; that is, exceeding the lawful limit which Allah has permitted you from your own wealth, into the unlawful which Allah has forbidden you from their wealth; ﴿and in haste, lest they grow up﴾, that is, do not consume it during their childhood, when they are unable to take it from you or prevent you from consuming it, hastening, lest they grow up and take it from you and prevent you from it. This is one of the matters that occurs with many guardians who have no fear of Allah and no mercy and love toward those under their guardianship; they see this state as an opportunity, so they seize it and hasten to take what Allah has forbidden them. Thus Allah, exalted is He, forbade this particular situation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 7:

{7} The Arabs in the pre-Islamic period, out of their harshness and brutality, would not give inheritance to the weak, such as women and children, and would make the inheritance only for the strong men, because, in their own claim, they were the people of war, fighting, plundering and seizing spoils. So the Lord, the Merciful, the All-Wise, willed to legislate for His servants a law in which their men and their women, their strong and their weak, are equal. He preceded this with a general statement so that souls would become settled upon it, and the detailed explanation would come after the general statement, with souls already longing for it and the estrangement arising from ugly customs having dissipated. So He said: {For men there is a share} (i.e., a portion and a lot) {of what the parents and the relatives leave} (i.e., what they leave behind), {the parents} (namely, the father and the mother), {and the relatives}, a generality after a specification. {And for women there is a share of what the parents and relatives leave}. It was as if it were said: Is that share subject to custom and habit, so that they give them whatever they wish, or is it something determined? So the Exalted said: {a share ordained} (i.e., the Wise, All-Knowing One has determined it). The determination of that will come, God willing. Also, there is here another misconception: perhaps someone might imagine that women and children have no share except from a large amount of wealth. He removed that by His saying: {from what is little of it or much}. So blessed is God, the best of judges.

{8} This is one of God's excellent and sublime rulings, one that comforts hearts. He said: {And when the division takes place} — i.e., the division of inheritance — {relatives} — i.e., relatives who are not heirs, as indicated by His words {the division}, since the heirs are among those for whom the division is made — {and orphans and the needy} — i.e., those among the poor who are entitled — {then provide for them from it} — i.e., give them what is easily available from this wealth that came to you without toil, effort, hardship, or fatigue. Indeed their souls long for it and their hearts yearn for it. So comfort their hearts with what will not harm you and will benefit them.

From the meaning it is also derived that everyone who longs for and craves what is present before a person should be given a portion of it as is easily possible, as the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "When one of you is brought his servant's food, let him seat him with him; and if he does not seat him with him, then let him give him a morsel or two morsels," or as he said. The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) used to bring the first fruits of their trees to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they began to ripen, and he would bless them, look at the youngest child near him, and give it to him, knowing his strong longing for it. All of this applies when giving is possible. If it is not possible, because it is the right of foolish persons, or there is something more important than it, then they should say to them {kind words}, turning them away graciously with good speech that is neither coarse nor offensive.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 9–10:

{9} It has been said: this is addressed to those present at the deathbed of a dying person, who deviates in his bequest; it commands them to be just in his bequest and to treat its beneficiaries equally. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And let them speak words of appropriate justice﴾; that is, words of soundness that accord with equity and kindness. And that they should instruct whoever wishes to make a bequest concerning his children to treat his children after him in the way they would love their own children to be treated. It has also been said that what is meant by this is the guardians of the foolish (the insane, the minors and the weak), that they should deal with them in their religious and worldly interests in the way they would love those who come after them of their weak offspring to be dealt with. ﴿So let them fear Allah﴾: in their guardianship over others; that is, they should deal with them in a way that embodies the fear of Allah, by not humiliating them, by attending to their affairs, and by obligating them to the fear of Allah.

{10} When He had commanded them to this, He restrained them from consuming the property of orphans and threatened the severest punishment for it, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾; that is, without right. This restriction excludes what was previously permitted: the permission for the poor to eat from it in a reasonable manner, and the permission to mix their food with the food of orphans. So whoever consumes it unjustly, ﴿they only consume fire into their bellies﴾; that is, what they have consumed is fire blazing within their bodies, and they are the ones who introduced it into their bellies. ﴿And they will burn in a Blaze﴾; that is, a scorching, fiercely kindled fire. This is the greatest threat mentioned concerning sins, and it indicates the enormity and ugliness of consuming the property of orphans, and that it necessitates entry into the Fire. This shows that it is among the greatest of the major sins. We ask Allah for well-being.

These verses, together with the verse at the end of the surah, are the verses of inheritance that contain its rulings. For they, together with the authentic hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Give the fara'id (the fixed shares) to their rightful owners, and whatever remains goes to the nearest male relative," encompass most of the rulings of the fara'id, indeed all of them, as you will see; except the inheritance of grandmothers, which is not mentioned therein. However, it has been authentically established in the Sunan, from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and Muhammad ibn Maslama, that the Prophet (ﷺ) gave the grandmother a sixth. This is with the consensus of the scholars on that.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 9–10:

This is with the consensus of the scholars on that.

{11} Concerning His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾; that is, O parents, your children are trusts in your keeping, about whom Allah has enjoined you, so that you may attend to their religious and worldly welfare: you teach them, discipline them, restrain them from corrupting things, and command them to obey Allah and to remain constantly mindful of God-consciousness (taqwa). This is like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾. Children, therefore, are entrusted to their parents. If they fulfil that trust, they will have abundant reward; if they neglect it, they deserve the threat and the punishment. This shows that Allah is more merciful to His servants than parents are, since He has enjoined parents despite their perfect compassion towards their children.

Then He mentioned how they inherit, saying: ﴿For the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾; that is, the children of the loins (direct children) and the children of a son. For the male, a portion equal to two females, if there are no sharers with fixed shares, or what the fixed shares leave, they divide in this manner. The scholars have unanimously agreed upon this, and that when the children of the loins are present, the inheritance belongs to them, and the children of a son receive nothing, whether the children of the loins are males and females. This is with the combination of males and females. Here there are two cases: where only males are present, whose ruling will come, and where only females are present. He mentioned the latter with His words: ﴿If they are women above two﴾; that is, daughters of the loins or daughters of a son, three or more; ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there is only one﴾; that is, one daughter or one granddaughter; ﴿then for her is half﴾. This is unanimous.

It remains to be asked: from where is it derived that two daughters receive two-thirds, given the consensus on this? The answer: it is derived from His words, ﴿If there is only one, then for her is half﴾. The implication of this is that if they exceed one, the fixed share moves away from half, and there is nothing after that except two-thirds. Also, His words, ﴿For the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾: if a man leaves a son and a daughter, the son has two-thirds, and Allah has stated that he takes a share equal to two females, which indicates that two daughters have two-thirds. Also, since a daughter takes a third together with her brother, which is more harmful to her than to her sister, her taking it together with her sister is all the more fitting and proper. Also, His words concerning two sisters: ﴿If there are two, then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves﴾, is explicit regarding two sisters; so if two sisters, who are more distant, take two-thirds, then two daughters, who are closer, take it all the more fittingly. The Prophet (ﷺ) also gave the two daughters of Sa'd two-thirds, as in the Sahih.

It remains to be asked: what is the benefit of His words, ﴿above two﴾? It is said: the benefit of that, and Allah knows best, is that it makes known that the fixed share of two-thirds does not increase with their number beyond two, but rather it is for two and above.

The noble verse indicates that if there is one daughter of the loins together with a granddaughter or granddaughters through a son, then the daughter of the loins has half, and from the two-thirds which Allah prescribed for the daughters or the granddaughters, the remaining sixth goes to the granddaughter or granddaughters; this sixth is for that reason called the completion of the two-thirds. Similarly, a granddaughter with granddaughters lower than her. The verse also indicates that when the daughters or granddaughters fully exhaust the two-thirds, those granddaughters below them are excluded, because Allah prescribed for them only two-thirds, and that is complete; if they were not excluded, it would necessarily follow that a share greater than two-thirds would be prescribed for them, which contradicts the text. All these rulings are agreed upon among the scholars, and praise be to Allah.

His words, ﴿of what he leaves﴾, indicate that the heirs inherit everything the deceased leaves behind: property, land, goods, gold, silver, and other things, even blood-money that became due only after his death, and even debts owed to him.

Then He mentioned the inheritance of the parents, saying: ﴿And for his parents﴾; that is, his father and mother, ﴿each of them is entitled to a sixth of what he leaves if he has children﴾; that is, children of the loins or children of a son, male or female, one or many. As for the mother, she does not receive more than a sixth when there are any of the children. As for the father, when there are male children he does not deserve more than a sixth. If the child is a female or females, and nothing remains after the fixed share, as with parents and two daughters, he has no residue; but if something remains after the daughter's or daughters' share, the father takes a sixth as a fixed share and the remainder as residue, because we assign the fixed shares to their owners, and what remains goes to the nearest male. He is closer than a brother, an uncle, or others. ﴿But if he has no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾; that is, and the remainder is for the father, because He attributed the property to the father and mother with a single attribution, then specified the mother's share, which indicates that the remainder is for the father. It is known from this that the father, when there are no children, has no fixed share, but inherits the whole estate as residue, or what the fixed shares leave.

However, if one of the spouses is present along with the parents (these are called the two 'Umariyyat), the husband or wife takes their fixed share, and then the mother takes a third of what remains and the father takes the rest. This is shown by His words: ﴿and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾; that is, a third of what the two parents inherit, which in these two cases is: either a sixth with a husband, mother and father, or a quarter with a wife, mother and father. The verse therefore does not indicate that the mother takes a third of the whole estate when there are no children, such that one might say these two cases are excepted from it. This is clarified by the fact that what the husband or wife takes is in the position of what creditors take, so it comes from the capital, and the remainder is between the parents. Moreover, if we gave the mother a third of the estate, it would follow that in the husband case she would receive more than the father by half a sixth, or in the wife case the father would take more than her by half a sixth; and this has no parallel, for the established norm is that she equals the father, or he takes twice what the mother takes. ﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾: whether full brothers, or consanguine (paternal) or uterine (maternal), males or females, whether they are heirs or excluded by the father or the grandfather. However, it may be said that the apparent meaning of His words, ﴿But if he has brothers﴾, does not include non-inheriting brothers, as evidenced by the fact that it does not apply to those excluded from the half; accordingly, only inheriting brothers exclude her from the third. This is supported by the fact that the wisdom in their excluding her from the third is so that some property may remain for them, and that is absent here. And Allah knows best. But this is on condition that they be two or more.

This raises a difficulty, namely the use of the plural word "brothers". It is answered that the intended meaning is merely plurality, not the grammatical plural, and this is satisfied by two; and the plural may sometimes be used to mean two, as in His words about Dawud and Sulayman: ﴿And We were witnesses to their judgment﴾. And concerning uterine siblings He said: ﴿And if a man or woman has an inheritance of kalalah, and has a brother or a sister, then each of them receives a sixth; but if they are more than that, they are sharers in a third﴾: here He used the plural, and what is meant is two or more, by consensus. Accordingly, if he leaves a mother, a father and siblings, the mother has a sixth and the rest goes to the father; so they exclude her from the third together with the father's exclusion of them; except on the other possibility, where the mother has a third and the remainder goes to the father.

Then He said: ﴿after any bequest that he makes or debt﴾; that is, these fixed shares, portions and inheritances are only executed and due after the removal of the debts owed by the deceased to Allah or to human beings, and after the bequests that the deceased made after his death; the remainder after these is the estate which the heirs are entitled to. He mentioned the bequest before the debt, though the debt takes precedence, in order to emphasise its importance, since fulfilling it is burdensome for the heirs. Otherwise, debts take precedence over it, and are paid from the capital; as for the bequest, it is valid up to a third or less for a stranger who is not an heir, while anything beyond that is not executed except with the consent of the heirs.

He said: ﴿Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾; that is, if the assignment of inheritance were left to your intellects and choices, there would result such harm as only Allah knows, because of the deficiency of minds and their failure to know what is most fitting and best in every time and place; so they do not know which of the children or parents is more beneficial to them and closer to the attainment of their religious and worldly aims. ﴿An obligation from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾; that is, He prescribed it, Allah, who encompasses all things in knowledge, who perfected what He legislated and ordained what He ordained in the best measure; minds cannot propose the like of His sound rulings, which suit every time, place and circumstance.

{12} Then He said: ﴿And for you (husbands) is half of what your wives leave if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt. And for them (wives) is a quarter of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt﴾. The term "child", whose existence or non-existence is the condition, includes the children of the loins or the children of a son, male and female, one or many, whether from the spouse or from another; and it excludes the children of daughters, by consensus.

Then He said: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance of kalalah, or a woman, and has a brother or a sister﴾; that is, from the mother, as in some readings. The scholars unanimously agree that the siblings here are uterine siblings. When someone leaves an inheritance of kalalah, meaning he has no father, no child, no grandfather, no son's son, no daughter, no daughter's daughter however far down; this is kalalah, as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) explained it, and agreement has been reached on this, praise be to Allah. ﴿Each of them receives a sixth; but if they are more than one﴾; that is, more than one person; ﴿they are sharers in a third﴾; that is, they do not receive more than a third, even if they exceed two. His words, ﴿they are sharers in a third﴾, indicate that their males and females are equal, because the word "sharer" implies equality. The term "kalalah" indicates that descendants, however far down, and male ascendants, however far up, exclude uterine siblings, since Allah did not make them heirs except in kalalah; if the deceased did not leave a kalalah, they inherit nothing from him, by consensus. His words, ﴿they are sharers in a third﴾, indicate that full siblings are excluded in the case known as al-Himariyya, which is: a husband, a mother, uterine siblings and full siblings. The husband has a half, the mother a sixth, the uterine siblings a third, and the full siblings are excluded, because Allah attributed the third to the uterine siblings; if the full siblings shared it with them, that would combine what Allah distinguished in ruling. Moreover, uterine siblings are fixed-share holders while full siblings are residuaries, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Give the fixed shares to their owners; what remains goes to the nearest male." The owners of fixed shares are those whose portions Allah determined; in this case nothing remains after them, so the full siblings are excluded, and this is the correct view on the matter. As for the inheritance of full or consanguine siblings, it is mentioned in His words: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalalah...﴾ the verse; so a single full sister or consanguine sister has a half, two have two-thirds, and a single full sister together with consanguine sisters takes a half, and the remainder of the two-thirds goes to the consanguine sister or sisters, which is a sixth, the completion of the two-thirds. When full sisters exhaust the two-thirds, consanguine sisters are excluded, as already mentioned regarding daughters and granddaughters. If the siblings are men and women, then ﴿to the male a portion equal to that of two females﴾.

If it is asked: can the rulings on the inheritance of a killer, a slave, one of a different religion, a partly-free person, a hermaphrodite (khunthā), a grandfather alongside brothers not of the same mother, awl (proportional reduction), radd (return of residue), distant kindred, the remaining residuaries, and sisters not of the same mother alongside daughters or granddaughters, be derived from the Qur'an or not? It is said: yes, there are subtle hints and indications in it, difficult for anyone other than a careful reflector to grasp, which point to all these matters:

As for the killer and the one of a different religion, it is known that they do not inherit from the deceased from the divine wisdom in distributing the property among the heirs according to their nearness and their religious and worldly benefit; Allah pointed to this wisdom with His words: ﴿You do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾. It is known that the killer has striven for his inheritance by the greatest harm, so what gives him the basis for inheritance cannot withstand the harm of killing, which is the opposite of the benefit on which inheritance is ordered. It is known from this that killing is the greatest barrier preventing inheritance and cutting the ties of kinship, of which Allah said: ﴿And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾; and the established legal principle is that whoever hastens something before its time is punished by being deprived of it.

By this and similar reasoning it is known that one who differs in religion from the deceased has no inheritance, since the cause that requires inheritance, namely the connection of lineage, conflicts with the barrier, namely difference in religion, which entails complete separation; the barrier prevails, and it blocks the cause of inheritance, which is lineage, so the cause does not operate because the barrier is present. This is clarified by the fact that Allah made the rights of Muslims take precedence over the worldly rights of disbelieving relatives; when a Muslim dies, his property passes to the one who is more entitled to it. So His words, ﴿And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾, apply when their religions agree; but where they differ, religious brotherhood takes precedence over mere lineal kinship.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in Jala' al-Afham: "Reflect on this meaning in the verses of inheritance, and on His connecting inheritance there with the word 'wife' rather than 'woman', as in His words: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave﴾: this is a notice that this inheritance occurs only by marital union, which requires conformity and proportion; and between a believer and a disbeliever there is no conformity or proportion, so no inheritance occurs between them. The secrets of the Qur'an's individual words and compositions are beyond the intellects of all beings." End of quote.

As for the slave, he neither inherits nor is inherited from. That he is not inherited from is clear, since he has no property to pass on; rather everything he has belongs to his master. As for his not inheriting, it is because he does not own; if he did own, it would belong to his master, who is a stranger to the deceased. So His words, ﴿For the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾, ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave﴾, ﴿For each of them a sixth﴾, and similar verses, apply only to one capable of ownership; the slave is not capable of this, so it is known that he has no inheritance.

As for one who is partly free and partly enslaved, his rulings are divided: by the part that is free he receives what Allah ordained in the inheritance, since the free part is capable of ownership, while the enslaved part is not; accordingly the partly-free person inherits, bequeaths and excludes in proportion to the free part he has. Just as a servant is praised or blamed, rewarded or punished, in proportion to what he has of the grounds for these, so is this.

As for the hermaphrodite (khunthā): he is either clearly male, clearly female, or ambiguous. If clearly male, he has the rulings of males and is covered by the text on them; if clearly female, he has the rulings of females and is covered by the text on them. If ambiguous: if the male and female inherit equally, as with uterine siblings, the matter is clear. If his inheritance differs according to whether he is male or female, and we have no way of knowing which, we do not give him the larger of the two assessments, lest we wrong those with him among the heirs, nor the smaller, lest we wrong him; so it is obligatory to take a middle course and follow the more equitable of the two ways. Allah said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to piety﴾. There is no way to justice in such a case more than this method mentioned, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; so fear Allah as much as you are able.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 11–12 (part 2 of 2):

As for the inheritance of the grandfather alongside full or paternal brothers, and whether they inherit together with him or not: the Book of Allah supports the view of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), that the grandfather blocks full, paternal and maternal brothers just as the father blocks them. The explanation of this is that the grandfather is called "father" in more than one place in the Qur'an, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq..."﴾ [2:133], and Yusuf, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq and Ya'qub﴾ [12:38]. Allah thus called the grandfather, the father's father, a "father." This shows that the grandfather has the status of the father: he inherits what the father inherits and blocks whomever the father blocks. Since the scholars have agreed that the grandfather, in the absence of the father, has the same ruling as the father regarding inheritance alongside the children and others, among the brothers, the paternal uncles and their sons, and the rest of the rules of inheritance, it follows that his ruling should also be the same as the father's in blocking brothers who are not full brothers by the mother. And since the son of the father has the status of the son of the loins, why should the grandfather not have the status of the father? And since the scholars agreed that the paternal grandfather blocks the son of a brother, why should the grandfather of the deceased not block his brother? There is no text, allusion, indication, or sound analogy in favour of those who give inheritance to brothers alongside the grandfather.

As for the issues of 'awl (proportional reduction), its ruling is derived from the Qur'an. Allah, the Exalted, has fixed and determined shares for the heirs, and they are in two states: either some of them block others, or they do not. If some block others, the blocked heir falls away, does not compete, and receives nothing. If none block others, then either the fixed shares do not exhaust the estate, or they exhaust it without excess or deficiency, or the fixed shares exceed the estate. In the first two cases, each takes his share in full. In the last case, where the shares exceed the estate, there are two possibilities. Either we reduce some heirs below the share Allah prescribed for them and complete the shares of the others, but this is preference without a basis, since reducing one of them is no more justified than reducing another. So the second possibility is determined: we give each of them his share as far as possible and distribute the shortfall among them proportionally, as with the creditors' debts exceeding the debtor's property. There is no way to achieve this except through 'awl. From this it is known that 'awl in the shares has been specified by Allah in His Book.

By the exact opposite of this method, the principle of radd (return of the surplus) is known. When the shareholders' shares do not exhaust the estate and something remains for which there is no entitled agnate, near or distant, then giving it to one of them is preference without a basis, and giving it to others who are not close relatives of the deceased is injustice, deviation, and contradiction of His words: ﴿And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [8:75]. Therefore it is determined that the surplus is returned to the shareholders in proportion to their shares. Since the spouses are not of kin, they do not deserve more than their determined share [according to those who hold that they do not receive radd; as for the correct view, that the spouses are governed by the same rule as the rest of the heirs regarding radd, the aforementioned evidence covers all of them, just as the evidence of 'awl covers them].

By this is also known the inheritance of the relatives through the womb (dhawu al-arham). When the deceased leaves no shareholder and no agnate, and the matter stands between his property going to the public treasury for the benefit of strangers and his property returning to his relatives who are connected to the deceased through the recognized heirs, the second is determined. This is shown by the words of Allah: ﴿And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [8:75]. Diverting it to others would abandon those who are more entitled than others. Thus the inheritance of the relatives through the womb is determined. And since their inheritance is determined, it is known that they have no fixed share specified by name in the Book of Allah, and that between them and the deceased there are intermediaries through whom they became relatives, so they are placed in the position of those intermediaries through whom they are connected. And Allah knows best.

As for the inheritance of the remaining agnates, such as sons, brothers and their sons, paternal uncles and their sons... etc., the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Give the fixed shares to their owners, and what remains goes to the closest male relative." And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for each We have made heirs of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ [4:33]. So when we give the fixed shares to their owners and nothing remains, the agnate receives nothing. If something remains, it is taken by the agnates according to their categories and degrees. The categories of agnation are five: sonship, then fatherhood, then brotherhood and their sons, then paternal uncleship and their sons, then patronage (al-wala'). The nearer category is given precedence. If they are in one category, the nearer in rank is preferred. If they are of equal rank, the stronger is preferred, namely the full sibling. If they are equal in every respect, they share. And Allah knows best.

As for the sisters of the half-blood (paternal sisters) being agnates alongside daughters or granddaughters, taking what remains after their fixed shares, this is because nothing in the Qur'an indicates that sisters are excluded by daughters. Since this is the case, and something remains after the daughters take their fixed share, it is given to the sisters, and one does not turn away from them to a more distant agnate such as the nephew, the paternal uncle, or anyone more distant than them. And Allah knows best.

{11} Concerning His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾; that is, O parents, your children are trusts in your keeping, about whom Allah has enjoined you, so that you may attend to their religious and worldly welfare: you teach them, discipline them, restrain them from corrupting things, and command them to obey Allah and to remain constantly mindful of God-consciousness (taqwa). This is like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾. Children, therefore, are entrusted to their parents. If they fulfil that trust, they will have abundant reward; if they neglect it, they deserve the threat and the punishment. This shows that Allah is more merciful to His servants than parents are, since He has enjoined parents despite their perfect compassion towards their children.

Then He mentioned how they inherit, saying: ﴿For the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾; that is, the children of the loins (direct children) and the children of a son. For the male, a portion equal to two females, if there are no sharers with fixed shares, or what the fixed shares leave, they divide in this manner. The scholars have unanimously agreed upon this, and that when the children of the loins are present, the inheritance belongs to them, and the children of a son receive nothing, whether the children of the loins are males and females. This is with the combination of males and females. Here there are two cases: where only males are present, whose ruling will come, and where only females are present. He mentioned the latter with His words: ﴿If they are women above two﴾; that is, daughters of the loins or daughters of a son, three or more; ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there is only one﴾; that is, one daughter or one granddaughter; ﴿then for her is half﴾. This is unanimous.

It remains to be asked: from where is it derived that two daughters receive two-thirds, given the consensus on this? The answer: it is derived from His words, ﴿If there is only one, then for her is half﴾. The implication of this is that if they exceed one, the fixed share moves away from half, and there is nothing after that except two-thirds. Also, His words, ﴿For the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾: if a man leaves a son and a daughter, the son has two-thirds, and Allah has stated that he takes a share equal to two females, which indicates that two daughters have two-thirds. Also, since a daughter takes a third together with her brother, which is more harmful to her than to her sister, her taking it together with her sister is all the more fitting and proper. Also, His words concerning two sisters: ﴿If there are two, then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves﴾, is explicit regarding two sisters; so if two sisters, who are more distant, take two-thirds, then two daughters, who are closer, take it all the more fittingly. The Prophet (ﷺ) also gave the two daughters of Sa'd two-thirds, as in the Sahih.

It remains to be asked: what is the benefit of His words, ﴿above two﴾? It is said: the benefit of that, and Allah knows best, is that it makes known that the fixed share of two-thirds does not increase with their number beyond two, but rather it is for two and above.

The noble verse indicates that if there is one daughter of the loins together with a granddaughter or granddaughters through a son, then the daughter of the loins has half, and from the two-thirds which Allah prescribed for the daughters or the granddaughters, the remaining sixth goes to the granddaughter or granddaughters; this sixth is for that reason called the completion of the two-thirds. Similarly, a granddaughter with granddaughters lower than her. The verse also indicates that when the daughters or granddaughters fully exhaust the two-thirds, those granddaughters below them are excluded, because Allah prescribed for them only two-thirds, and that is complete; if they were not excluded, it would necessarily follow that a share greater than two-thirds would be prescribed for them, which contradicts the text. All these rulings are agreed upon among the scholars, and praise be to Allah.

His words, ﴿of what he leaves﴾, indicate that the heirs inherit everything the deceased leaves behind: property, land, goods, gold, silver, and other things, even blood-money that became due only after his death, and even debts owed to him.

Then He mentioned the inheritance of the parents, saying: ﴿And for his parents﴾; that is, his father and mother, ﴿each of them is entitled to a sixth of what he leaves if he has children﴾; that is, children of the loins or children of a son, male or female, one or many. As for the mother, she does not receive more than a sixth when there are any of the children. As for the father, when there are male children he does not deserve more than a sixth. If the child is a female or females, and nothing remains after the fixed share, as with parents and two daughters, he has no residue; but if something remains after the daughter's or daughters' share, the father takes a sixth as a fixed share and the remainder as residue, because we assign the fixed shares to their owners, and what remains goes to the nearest male. He is closer than a brother, an uncle, or others. ﴿But if he has no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾; that is, and the remainder is for the father, because He attributed the property to the father and mother with a single attribution, then specified the mother's share, which indicates that the remainder is for the father. It is known from this that the father, when there are no children, has no fixed share, but inherits the whole estate as residue, or what the fixed shares leave.

However, if one of the spouses is present along with the parents (these are called the two 'Umariyyat), the husband or wife takes their fixed share, and then the mother takes a third of what remains and the father takes the rest. This is shown by His words: ﴿and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾; that is, a third of what the two parents inherit, which in these two cases is: either a sixth with a husband, mother and father, or a quarter with a wife, mother and father. The verse therefore does not indicate that the mother takes a third of the whole estate when there are no children, such that one might say these two cases are excepted from it. This is clarified by the fact that what the husband or wife takes is in the position of what creditors take, so it comes from the capital, and the remainder is between the parents. Moreover, if we gave the mother a third of the estate, it would follow that in the husband case she would receive more than the father by half a sixth, or in the wife case the father would take more than her by half a sixth; and this has no parallel, for the established norm is that she equals the father, or he takes twice what the mother takes. ﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾: whether full brothers, or consanguine (paternal) or uterine (maternal), males or females, whether they are heirs or excluded by the father or the grandfather. However, it may be said that the apparent meaning of His words, ﴿But if he has brothers﴾, does not include non-inheriting brothers, as evidenced by the fact that it does not apply to those excluded from the half; accordingly, only inheriting brothers exclude her from the third. This is supported by the fact that the wisdom in their excluding her from the third is so that some property may remain for them, and that is absent here. And Allah knows best. But this is on condition that they be two or more.

This raises a difficulty, namely the use of the plural word "brothers". It is answered that the intended meaning is merely plurality, not the grammatical plural, and this is satisfied by two; and the plural may sometimes be used to mean two, as in His words about Dawud and Sulayman: ﴿And We were witnesses to their judgment﴾. And concerning uterine siblings He said: ﴿And if a man or woman has an inheritance of kalalah, and has a brother or a sister, then each of them receives a sixth; but if they are more than that, they are sharers in a third﴾: here He used the plural, and what is meant is two or more, by consensus. If clearly male, he has the rulings of males and is covered by the text on them; if clearly female, he has the rulings of females and is covered by the text on them. If ambiguous: if the male and female inherit equally, as with uterine siblings, the matter is clear. If his inheritance differs according to whether he is male or female, and we have no way of knowing which, we do not give him the larger of the two assessments, lest we wrong those with him among the heirs, nor the smaller, lest we wrong him; so it is obligatory to take a middle course and follow the more equitable of the two ways. Allah said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to piety﴾. There is no way to justice in such a case more than this method mentioned, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; so fear Allah as much as you are able.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 11–12 (part 2 of 2):

As for the inheritance of the grandfather alongside full or paternal brothers, and whether they inherit together with him or not: the Book of Allah supports the view of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), that the grandfather blocks full, paternal and maternal brothers just as the father blocks them. The explanation of this is that the grandfather is called "father" in more than one place in the Qur'an, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq..."﴾ [2:133], and Yusuf, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq and Ya'qub﴾ [12:38]. Allah thus called the grandfather, the father's father, a "father." This shows that the grandfather has the status of the father: he inherits what the father inherits and blocks whomever the father blocks. Since the scholars have agreed that the grandfather, in the absence of the father, has the same ruling as the father regarding inheritance alongside the children and others, among the brothers, the paternal uncles and their sons, and the rest of the rules of inheritance, it follows that his ruling should also be the same as the father's in blocking brothers who are not full brothers by the mother. And since the son of the father has the status of the son of the loins, why should the grandfather not have the status of the father? And since the scholars agreed that the paternal grandfather blocks the son of a brother, why should the grandfather of the deceased not block his brother? There is no text, allusion, indication, or sound analogy in favour of those who give inheritance to brothers alongside the grandfather.

As for the issues of 'awl (proportional reduction), its ruling is derived from the Qur'an. Allah, the Exalted, has fixed and determined shares for the heirs, and they are in two states: either some of them block others, or they do not. If some block others, the blocked heir falls away, does not compete, and receives nothing. If none block others, then either the fixed shares do not exhaust the estate, or they exhaust it without excess or deficiency, or the fixed shares exceed the estate. In the first two cases, each takes his share in full. In the last case, where the shares exceed the estate, there are two possibilities. Either we reduce some heirs below the share Allah prescribed for them and complete the shares of the others, but this is preference without a basis, since reducing one of them is no more justified than reducing another. So the second possibility is determined: we give each of them his share as far as possible and distribute the shortfall among them proportionally, as with the creditors' debts exceeding the debtor's property. There is no way to achieve this except through 'awl. From this it is known that 'awl in the shares has been specified by Allah in His Book.

By the exact opposite of this method, the principle of radd (return of the surplus) is known. When the shareholders' shares do not exhaust the estate and something remains for which there is no entitled agnate, near or distant, then giving it to one of them is preference without a basis, and giving it to others who are not close relatives of the deceased is injustice, deviation, and contradiction of His words: ﴿And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [8:75]. Therefore it is determined that the surplus is returned to the shareholders in proportion to their shares. Since the spouses are not of kin, they do not deserve more than their determined share [according to those who hold that they do not receive radd; as for the correct view, that the spouses are governed by the same rule as the rest of the heirs regarding radd, the aforementioned evidence covers all of them, just as the evidence of 'awl covers them].

By this is also known the inheritance of the relatives through the womb (dhawu al-arham). When the deceased leaves no shareholder and no agnate, and the matter stands between his property going to the public treasury for the benefit of strangers and his property returning to his relatives who are connected to the deceased through the recognized heirs, the second is determined. This is shown by the words of Allah: ﴿And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [8:75]. Diverting it to others would abandon those who are more entitled than others. Thus the inheritance of the relatives through the womb is determined. And since their inheritance is determined, it is known that they have no fixed share specified by name in the Book of Allah, and that between them and the deceased there are intermediaries through whom they became relatives, so they are placed in the position of those intermediaries through whom they are connected. And Allah knows best.

As for the inheritance of the remaining agnates, such as sons, brothers and their sons, paternal uncles and their sons... etc., the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Give the fixed shares to their owners, and what remains goes to the closest male relative." And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for each We have made heirs of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ [4:33]. So when we give the fixed shares to their owners and nothing remains, the agnate receives nothing. If something remains, it is taken by the agnates according to their categories and degrees. The categories of agnation are five: sonship, then fatherhood, then brotherhood and their sons, then paternal uncleship and their sons, then patronage (al-wala'). The nearer category is given precedence. If they are in one category, the nearer in rank is preferred. If they are of equal rank, the stronger is preferred, namely the full sibling. If they are equal in every respect, they share. And Allah knows best.

As for the sisters of the half-blood (paternal sisters) being agnates alongside daughters or granddaughters, taking what remains after their fixed shares, this is because nothing in the Qur'an indicates that sisters are excluded by daughters. Since this is the case, and something remains after the daughters take their fixed share, it is given to the sisters, and one does not turn away from them to a more distant agnate such as the nephew, the paternal uncle, or anyone more distant than them. And Allah knows best.

{13} That is, these details mentioned regarding inheritance are the limits of Allah which must be observed: one must neither exceed them nor fall short of them. This is evidence that bequest to an heir has been abrogated (naskh) by His, the Exalted's, determination of the shares of the heirs. Then His, the Exalted's, saying: {That are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them}. Thus, a bequest to an heir exceeding his right falls under this transgression, along with the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "There is no bequest to an heir."

Then He mentioned obedience to Allah and His Messenger and disobedience to them in general, so that the obligation to observe His limits regarding the obligatory shares, or to abandon that, is included in the generality. So He said: {And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger}: by complying with their command, the greatest of which is obedience to them in monotheism (tawhid), then the commands according to their varying degrees; and by avoiding their prohibitions, the greatest of which is associating partners with Allah (shirk), then the sins according to their varying categories. {He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever}: whoever performs the commands and avoids the prohibitions, entry into Paradise and salvation from the Fire is inevitable for him. {And that is the great attainment}: by which he is saved from His wrath and punishment and attains His reward and good pleasure, in lasting bliss which describers cannot describe.

{14} {And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger...} etc. Included in the name of disobedience is disbelief (kufr) and what is below it of sins. Therefore there is no basis in it for the Khawarij, who declare the people of sins to be disbelievers. For Allah, the Exalted, made entry into Paradise contingent upon obedience to Him and to His Messenger, and made entry into the Fire contingent upon disobedience to Him and to His Messenger. So whoever obeys Him with complete obedience enters Paradise without punishment, and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger with complete disobedience, which includes associating partners with Allah (shirk) and what is below it, enters the Fire and abides therein forever. Whoever combines in himself disobedience and obedience has in him what necessitates reward and punishment according to the degree of his obedience and disobedience.

Mass-transmitted (mutawatir) texts have established that the monotheists who possess the obedience of monotheism do not abide forever in the Fire; the tawhid they possess prevents them from abiding in it.

{15} That is: the women {who commit immorality}, meaning fornication (zina). He described it as "immorality" (fahisha) because of its heinousness and ugliness. {Call against them four witnesses from among you}, meaning from among your believing, upright (*'udul*) men. {And if they testify, then confine them to houses}, meaning keep them confined from going out, which invites suspicion. Confinement is also one of the punishments. {Until death takes them}, meaning this is the limit of the confinement. {Or God makes for them a way}, meaning a path other than confinement in houses.

This verse is not abrogated (*naskh*). Rather, it is limited to that time. The matter was like this at the beginning of Islam until God made for them a way, which is stoning the married (*muhsan*) and flogging the unmarried.

{16} Likewise {the two who commit it}, meaning the immorality, {from among you}: men and women. {Harm them}: with words, rebuke, reproach, and beating that deters from this immorality. Accordingly, when men commit immorality they are harmed, and when women commit it they are confined and harmed. The end of confinement is death, and the end of harm is repentance and reform. Hence He said: {If they repent}, meaning they turn back from the sin they committed, regret it, and resolve not to return to it, {and reform}, meaning they do the deeds that show the sincerity of their repentance. {Then leave them alone}, meaning cease harming them. {Indeed God is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful}, meaning He is greatly accepting of repentance from sinners who err, and of great mercy and kindness. From His kindness, He enabled them to repent, accepted it from them, and pardoned what proceeded from them.

From these two verses it is derived that the proof of fornication [must] consist of four male believers, and, all the more so, that their uprightness is a condition. God, exalted is He, was strict in this matter of immorality as a concealment for His servants, to the extent that the testimony of women alone, or of a man with women, or of fewer than four, is not accepted in it. Explicit testimony is also required, as the authentic hadiths indicate and as this verse alludes. When He said {call against them four witnesses from among you}, He did not suffice with that, but said {if they testify}, meaning there must be explicit testimony about a matter witnessed directly, without allusion or implication.

It is also derived from them that harm by word and deed, and confinement, were prescribed by God as discretionary punishment (*ta'zir*) for the category of disobedience by which deterrence is achieved.

{17–18} God's acceptance of repentance from His servants is of two kinds: first, His granting them the success (tawfiq) to repent, and second, His acceptance of it after it has come into being from the servant. Here He informs us that repentance is owed by God as a right which He has made binding upon Himself, out of His generosity and bounty, to those who do evil, that is, commit sins (ma'asi), "in ignorance" (bi-jahalah). This ignorance is their lack of knowledge of the consequences of sin and that it necessitates the wrath and punishment of God; it is also their ignorance of God's watching and observing them, and their ignorance of what it leads to in terms of diminishing faith or annihilating it. Thus every person who disobeys God is ignorant in this sense, even if he knows that the act is forbidden; indeed, knowledge that it is forbidden is a condition for it to be a sin for which one is punished.

"Then they repent soon" (thumma yatubuna min qarib): it may be that the meaning is: then they repent before witnessing death, for God surely accepts the repentance of a servant who repents before witnessing death and punishment. As for after the arrival of death, no repentance is accepted from sinners, nor is any return accepted from disbelievers, as God says concerning Pharaoh: ﴿When drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims"﴾ ... the verse; and God the Exalted says: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their belief was not going to benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the established way of Allah which has preceded among His servants﴾. Here He also says: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds [i.e., sins short of disbelief] until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For those, We have prepared a painful punishment﴾. This is because repentance in such a state is repentance under compulsion, which does not benefit its doer; only repentance by choice benefits.

It may also be that the meaning of His words "min qarib" is: close to the time of their committing the sin that necessitates repentance. The meaning then is that whoever hastens to desist from the moment the sin occurs, turns back to God, and regrets it, God will turn to him in repentance. This is in contrast to one who persists in his sin and insists upon his faults until firm traits settle in him; for him it becomes difficult to bring about complete repentance, and generally he is not granted success in repenting nor made easy the means to it. Like one who does evil with established knowledge and certain conviction, while being careless about God's watching him, he closes the door of mercy upon himself. Yes, God may grant success to His servant who persists in sins deliberately and with certainty to a beneficial repentance by which He erases what preceded of his evil deeds and what came before of his offenses; but mercy and success for the former is closer. For this reason He concluded the first verse with His words: ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾. From His knowledge is that He knows the sincere repentance from the insincere, and He recompenses each of them according to what he deserves by His wisdom. And from His wisdom is that He grants success to whom His wisdom and mercy require to be granted success in repentance, and forsakes whom His wisdom and justice require not to be granted success. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 19–21:

{19} In the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), when one of them died leaving a wife, his relative, such as his brother, his paternal cousin, or others like them, considered that he had a greater right to the wife than anyone else, and he would guard her from others, whether she liked it or not. If he desired her, he would marry her with a dowry that he himself liked, without her (having a say in it). If he did not want her, he would prevent her (from remarrying) (ʿaḍl), so that she could marry no one except whomever he chose. Sometimes he would refuse to let her marry until she gave him some of the inheritance of her deceased husband or some of her dowry. A man would also prevent his wife (from remarrying or leaving) whom he disliked, so that he might take back some of what he had given her. So God forbade the believers from all these situations, except for two cases: when she is willing and chooses to marry her late husband's relative, as is implied by His saying: {unwillingly} (karhan); and when they commit a clear immorality (fāḥishah mubayyinah), such as adultery, obscene speech, or harming her husband. In that case it is permissible for him to prevent her (from remarrying) as a punishment for her act, so that she may ransom herself from him, provided that the prevention is done justly.

Then He said: {And live with them in kindness (bil-maʿrūf)}. This includes both verbal and practical kindness. The husband must treat his wife kindly (bil-maʿrūf) through good companionship, refraining from harm, bestowing goodness, and good treatment. This includes maintenance (nafaqah), clothing, and the like. The husband is obliged to provide his wife with what is customary (maʿrūf) for someone of his standing toward someone of her standing, in that time and place, and this varies with circumstances. {But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God makes in it much good}; that is: O husbands, you should keep your wives even while disliking them, for in that there is much good. Among it is obeying God's command and accepting His injunction, which contains the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. Among it is that forcing himself to remain with her despite not loving her involves striving against the self and adopting beautiful character. Perhaps the dislike will pass and be replaced by love, as is often the case, and perhaps he will be granted a righteous child from her who benefits his parents in this world and the Hereafter.

{20} All of this applies where keeping the wife is possible and there is no prohibited harm. If separation is unavoidable and there is no place for keeping her, then keeping her is not obligatory. Rather, whenever {you desire to exchange a spouse for a spouse}; that is, to divorce one wife and marry another, then there is no blame upon you in that, nor any sin. However, when {you have given one of them}; that is, the one being separated from or the one you marry, {a great amount (qinṭār)}; that is, a large amount of wealth, {then do not take back from it anything}; rather, give it in full to them and do not delay (their due).

This verse indicates that a large dowry is not forbidden, although the better and more appropriate course is to follow the Prophet (ﷺ) in lightening the dowry. The indication is that God informed of a matter that occurred among them and did not denounce it, which shows it is not prohibited. Yet a large dowry may be forbidden if it entails religious harm and there is no benefit that outweighs it. Then He said: {Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?}; for this is not lawful, even if you resort to all kinds of stratagems, since its sinfulness is evident.

{21} God has explained the wisdom of this in His saying: {And how could you take it when you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?} The explanation is that before the marriage contract, the wife is forbidden to the husband, and she consented to make her lawful to him only with that dowry he pays her. So when he consummates the marriage and is intimate with her, the intimacy that was forbidden before and that she would not have permitted except for that compensation, then he has received what was exchanged, and the compensation becomes binding upon him. How then can he receive the exchange and afterward reclaim the compensation? This is among the greatest injustice and oppression. Likewise, God took from husbands a solemn covenant through the contract and the fulfilment of her rights. Then God, Exalted, said:
