Likewise, God took from husbands a solemn covenant through the contract and the fulfilment of her rights. Then God, Exalted, said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 19–21:

{19} In the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), when one of them died leaving a wife, his relative, such as his brother, his paternal cousin, or others like them, considered that he had a greater right to the wife than anyone else, and he would guard her from others, whether she liked it or not. If he desired her, he would marry her with a dowry that he himself liked, without her (having a say in it). If he did not want her, he would prevent her (from remarrying) (ʿaḍl), so that she could marry no one except whomever he chose. Sometimes he would refuse to let her marry until she gave him some of the inheritance of her deceased husband or some of her dowry. A man would also prevent his wife (from remarrying or leaving) whom he disliked, so that he might take back some of what he had given her. So God forbade the believers from all these situations, except for two cases: when she is willing and chooses to marry her late husband's relative, as is implied by His saying: {unwillingly} (karhan); and when they commit a clear immorality (fāḥishah mubayyinah), such as adultery, obscene speech, or harming her husband. In that case it is permissible for him to prevent her (from remarrying) as a punishment for her act, so that she may ransom herself from him, provided that the prevention is done justly.

Then He said: {And live with them in kindness (bil-maʿrūf)}. This includes both verbal and practical kindness. The husband must treat his wife kindly (bil-maʿrūf) through good companionship, refraining from harm, bestowing goodness, and good treatment. This includes maintenance (nafaqah), clothing, and the like. The husband is obliged to provide his wife with what is customary (maʿrūf) for someone of his standing toward someone of her standing, in that time and place, and this varies with circumstances. {But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God makes in it much good}; that is: O husbands, you should keep your wives even while disliking them, for in that there is much good. Among it is obeying God's command and accepting His injunction, which contains the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. Among it is that forcing himself to remain with her despite not loving her involves striving against the self and adopting beautiful character. Perhaps the dislike will pass and be replaced by love, as is often the case, and perhaps he will be granted a righteous child from her who benefits his parents in this world and the Hereafter.

{20} All of this applies where keeping the wife is possible and there is no prohibited harm. If separation is unavoidable and there is no place for keeping her, then keeping her is not obligatory. Rather, whenever {you desire to exchange a spouse for a spouse}; that is, to divorce one wife and marry another, then there is no blame upon you in that, nor any sin. However, when {you have given one of them}; that is, the one being separated from or the one you marry, {a great amount (qinṭār)}; that is, a large amount of wealth, {then do not take back from it anything}; rather, give it in full to them and do not delay (their due).

This verse indicates that a large dowry is not forbidden, although the better and more appropriate course is to follow the Prophet (ﷺ) in lightening the dowry. The indication is that God informed of a matter that occurred among them and did not denounce it, which shows it is not prohibited. Yet a large dowry may be forbidden if it entails religious harm and there is no benefit that outweighs it. Then He said: {Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?}; for this is not lawful, even if you resort to all kinds of stratagems, since its sinfulness is evident.

{21} God has explained the wisdom of this in His saying: {And how could you take it when you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?} The explanation is that before the marriage contract, the wife is forbidden to the husband, and she consented to make her lawful to him only with that dowry he pays her. So when he consummates the marriage and is intimate with her, the intimacy that was forbidden before and that she would not have permitted except for that compensation, then he has received what was exchanged, and the compensation becomes binding upon him. How then can he receive the exchange and afterward reclaim the compensation? This is among the greatest injustice and oppression. Likewise, God took from husbands a solemn covenant through the contract and the fulfilment of her rights. Then God, Exalted, said:

{22} That is: do not marry women whom your fathers have married; that is, the father, and whoever is above him (in ascent). "Indeed it was an abomination" — that is, a matter that is ugly, whose ugliness is extreme and great. "And hateful" — from Allah toward you, and from the creation; rather, because of that, the son is detested by his father and the father by his son, despite the command to be dutiful to him. "And evil is the way" — that is, the path is evil for whoever takes it, because this is among the customs of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) from which Islam came to purify and disassociate.

These noble verses comprise the prohibitions by lineage (blood relations), the prohibitions by fosterage (nursing relationship), the prohibitions by marriage (affinity), the prohibitions by combining (two women in one marriage), and the women who are permissible.

{23} As for the prohibited relatives by blood, they are the seven whom God mentioned: the mother, which includes every woman to whom you are related by birth, however remote; the daughter, which includes every woman who is related to you by birth from you, however remote; the sisters, whether full, paternal or maternal; the paternal aunt, which includes every sister of your father or of your grandfather, however far up; the maternal aunt, which includes every sister of your mother or of your grandmother, however far up, whether or not she is an heir; and the daughters of a brother and the daughters of a sister, meaning however far down. These are the ones prohibited by blood by the consensus of the scholars, as the text of the noble verse states. Whoever is other than these falls under His saying: {and lawful to you is what lies beyond that}, such as the daughter of the paternal uncle, the daughter of the paternal aunt, the daughter of the maternal uncle and the daughter of the maternal aunt.

As for those prohibited by nursing, God mentioned among them the mother and the sister. In this is the prohibition of the mother, although the milk is not hers; it belongs to the owner of the milk. By alerting us to this, He indicated that the owner of the milk becomes the father of the nursling. Once fatherhood and motherhood are established, what branches from them is established as well, such as their siblings, their ascendants and their descendants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What is prohibited by blood is prohibited by nursing." So the prohibition spreads through the nursing woman and the man who has the milk, just as it spreads among relatives, and to the nursling's descendants only. This holds, however, on condition that the nursing consists of five sucklings within the two years, as the Sunnah has explained.

As for those prohibited by marriage, they are four: the wives of fathers, however far up, and the wives of sons, however far down, whether they are heirs or excluded; and the mothers of the wife, however far up. These three are prohibited merely by the contract. The fourth is the stepdaughter, who is the daughter of one's wife, however far down; she is not prohibited until one has consummated the marriage with her mother, as He said here: {and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage...} to the end of the verse. The majority of scholars have said that His saying {who are in your guardianship} is a restriction that came out in the manner of what is usual, and has no implied meaning; the stepdaughter is prohibited even if she is not in his guardianship. However, this restriction has two benefits. The first: it draws attention to the wisdom behind the prohibition of the stepdaughter, that she is in the position of a daughter, and so it is abhorrent to permit her. The second: it indicates the permissibility of being alone with a stepdaughter, that she is in the position of one who is in his guardianship among his daughters and the like. And God knows best.

As for those prohibited by combining: God mentioned the combining of two sisters and prohibited it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibited combining a woman with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt. Thus every two women between whom there is a prohibited kinship, were one of them assumed to be male and the other female, it would be unlawful for him to marry them both; combining them is prohibited, because of what it causes of severance among the relatives.

{24} Among the prohibitions in marriage are {the married women}, meaning those who have husbands. Marrying them is prohibited as long as they remain under the husband's responsibility, until he divorces them and their waiting period ends. {Except what your right hands possess}, meaning through captivity. So when a disbelieving woman who has a husband is taken captive, she becomes lawful to the Muslims after her womb has been cleansed. As for when a married slave-woman is sold or gifted, her marriage is not annulled, because the second owner takes the place of the first. This is also shown by the story of Barirah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) gave her the choice.

His saying {the Book of God upon you} means: adhere to it and be guided by it, for in it are healing and light, and in it is the detailed distinction between the lawful and the unlawful.

Included in His saying {and lawful to you is what lies beyond that} is everything not mentioned in this verse; it is lawful and good. The prohibited is limited, while the lawful has no bound or limit, out of God's gentleness, mercy and facilitation for His servants. His saying {that you seek with your wealth} means: that you seek, from among those whom God has made lawful to you, those upon whom your gaze and choice fall, being {chaste}, meaning abstaining from fornication and keeping your women chaste. {Not committing fornication}: sifah means pouring out water in lawful or unlawful ways; the one who does so does not keep his wife chaste, because he has placed his desire in the unlawful, so his motivation toward the lawful weakens, and he is no longer chaste toward his wife. It also indicates that one who is not chaste should not be married, based on His saying, exalted is He: {The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater}.

{So for what you enjoy of them}, meaning: from those whom you have married. {Give them their payments}, meaning: the payments in return for enjoyment. For this reason, when the husband consummates the marriage with his wife, her dowry is established upon him. {As an obligation}, meaning: your giving them their payments is an obligation God has imposed upon you, not like a voluntary gift which one may enforce or revoke as he wishes. Or the meaning of His saying {as an obligation} is: determined, which you have set, so it became binding upon you; so do not reduce any of it. {And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation}, meaning: by an increase from the husband or a remission from the wife, out of willingness and good consent. This is the view of many commentators. Many of them said: it was revealed concerning temporary marriage with women, which was lawful at the beginning of Islam, then the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibited it; it was commanded that it be limited in time and that the payment be fixed, and then when the term between them had ended, if they agreed after the obligation, there is no blame on them. From His knowledge and wisdom He has legislated these laws for you and set these limits that separate the lawful from the unlawful. Then God, exalted, said:

{25} That is: whoever is unable to afford the means (tawl), which is the bridal gift (mahr), to marry free believing women (al-muhsanat, i.e., free women), and fears for himself hardship (al-'anat), that is, fornication and great difficulty, then it is permissible for him to marry believing enslaved women (al-imaa al-mamlukat). This is according to what appears outwardly; otherwise, God knows best who is a truly sincere believer and who is not. The affairs of this world are built upon outward appearances, while the rulings of the Hereafter are built upon what lies within. ﴿So marry them﴾; that is, the enslaved women, ﴿with the permission of their people﴾; that is, their masters, whether one or several. ﴿And give them their bridal gifts according to what is reasonable﴾; that is, even if they are slave-girls, for just as the mahr is obligatory for a free woman, so it is obligatory for a slave-girl as well. However, marrying slave-girls is not permissible except when they are ﴿chaste﴾; that is, modest and abstaining from fornication, ﴿not committing open fornication﴾; that is, not openly committing adultery, ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾; that is, lovers in private.

The summary is that it is not permissible for a free Muslim man to marry a slave-girl except under four conditions mentioned by God: that she is a believer, that she is chaste outwardly and inwardly, that he is unable to afford the means to marry a free woman, and that he fears hardship (al-'anat). When these conditions are fulfilled, it is permissible for him to marry them. Nevertheless, patience in refraining from marrying them is better, because it avoids exposing children to slavery, and because of the baseness and disgrace involved. This applies when patience is possible; but if one cannot refrain from what is forbidden except by marrying them, then it becomes obligatory, and therefore He said: ﴿But to be patient is better for you, and God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

As for His words ﴿And when they are chaste﴾; that is, when they marry or embrace Islam (the slave-girls), ﴿then upon them is half the punishment of free chaste women﴾; that is, free women, ﴿of punishment﴾. This is the part that can be halved, which is the lashing, so they receive fifty lashes. As for stoning (rajm), there is no stoning for slave-girls, because it cannot be halved. According to the first opinion: if they do not marry, there is no prescribed penalty (hadd) for them; rather, they receive a discretionary punishment (ta'zir) that deters them from committing indecency. According to the second opinion: if non-Muslim slave-girls commit indecency, they likewise receive discretionary punishment.

He concluded this verse with these two noble names: the Forgiving and the Merciful, because these rulings are a mercy to the servants, a generosity and a kindness toward them. He did not constrict them but granted them the utmost ease. Perhaps the mention of forgiveness after the mention of the prescribed penalty is an indication that the prescribed penalties are expiations by which God forgives the sins of His servants, as is related in the hadith.

The ruling for a male slave regarding the aforementioned penalty is the same as the ruling for a slave-girl, since there is no difference between them.

{26} He, may He be exalted, informs of His great favour, His bountiful gift, His good upbringing of His believing servants, and the ease of His religion, saying: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾; that is, all that you need to have made clear of the truth and falsehood, the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿And to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾; that is, those upon whom Allah bestowed favour from among the prophets and their followers, in their praiseworthy conduct, their upright deeds, their complete characters and their perfect success. Therefore He carried out what He willed, made clear to you, and explained with an explanation as He explained to those before you, and guided you with a great guidance in knowledge and action. ﴿And to turn to you in forgiveness﴾; that is, He is gentle [with you] in your affairs and in what He has legislated for you, so that you are able to stand upon what Allah has delimited and to be content with what He has made lawful, whereby your sins decrease through what Allah has made easy for you. This is from His turning to His servants in forgiveness. And from His turning to them in forgiveness is that when they sin, He opens for them the doors of mercy, inspires their hearts to turn penitently to Him and to humble themselves before Him, and then turns to them in forgiveness by accepting what He has enabled them to do; so to Him belong all praise and thanks for that. And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾; that is, [perfect in knowledge], perfect in wisdom. Of His knowledge is that He taught you what you did not know, and among it are these matters and limits. And of His wisdom is that He turns in forgiveness to whoever His wisdom and mercy require to be forgiven, and forsakes whoever His wisdom and justice require to be unfit for repentance.

{27} And His saying: ﴿And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness﴾; that is, a repentance that gathers your scattered affairs, unites your dispersed, and brings near your distant. ﴿But those who follow their desires desire that you deviate with a great deviation﴾; that is, they incline wherever their desires incline, prefer them over what pleases their Beloved, and worship their whims, from among the various kinds of disbelievers and sinners who put their desires before obedience to their Lord. So these desire ﴿that you deviate with a great deviation﴾; that is, that you turn away from the straight path to the path of those who earned anger and of those who are astray. They desire to divert you from obedience to the Most Merciful to obedience to Satan, and from adhering to the limits in which all happiness lies in carrying out His commands to following those in whom all wretchedness lies. So when you know that Allah, may He be exalted, commands you with what is good for your welfare, success and happiness, and that these followers of their desires command you with what brings utmost loss and misery, then choose for yourselves the more worthy of the two callers, and select the better of the two ways.

{28} ﴿Allah desires to lighten for you﴾; that is, by the ease of what He commands you and what He forbids you. Then, although hardship arises in some of the laws, He permitted for you what your need requires, such as carrion and blood for the one compelled, and marrying a slave woman for the free man under those previously mentioned conditions. This is due to His complete mercy, His comprehensive kindness, and His knowledge and wisdom regarding human weakness in all respects: weakness of constitution, weakness of will, weakness of resolve, weakness of faith, and weakness of patience. It is therefore fitting that Allah lightens for him what he is weak to bear, and what his faith, patience and strength cannot endure.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 29–30:

{29} God, exalted is He, forbids His believing servants to consume their wealth among themselves in falsehood. This includes taking it through usurpation and theft, through gambling, and through base gains. Indeed, it may also include consuming one's own wealth in a manner of wantonness and extravagance, because this is from falsehood and not from truth. Then, when He forbade consuming wealth in falsehood, He permitted them to consume it through trades and gains that are free of impediments and that fulfil the conditions, such as mutual consent and other requirements.

{And do not kill yourselves}; that is, let none of you kill another, and let no person kill himself. This includes throwing oneself into destruction (al-tahlukah) and undertaking dangers that lead to loss and ruin. {Indeed, God is ever Merciful to you}: among His mercy is that He preserved your souls and your wealth, forbade you from squandering and destroying them, and attached to that the prescribed penalties (hudud) that He established.

Reflect on the conciseness and comprehensiveness in His words {Do not consume your wealth} {and do not kill yourselves}: how they encompass the wealth of others, your own wealth, killing yourself, and killing others, in a phrase more concise than saying: "Let none of you consume the wealth of another, and let none of you kill another." Yet that phrase would be restricted to the wealth and lives of others. Moreover, the attribution of wealth and lives to the believers in general indicates that the believers, in their mutual affection, compassion, sympathy, and welfare, are like a single body, since faith unites them in their religious and worldly interests.

Having forbidden consuming wealth in falsehood, which carries the greatest harm to them, both to the one who consumes it and to the one whose wealth is taken, He permitted them what serves their interest: the various kinds of gain, trade, crafts, and hiring. So He said: {except that it be trade by mutual consent among you}; that is, such trade is permitted to you. The condition of mutual consent, although the matter is trade, is stipulated because it indicates that the contract must not be a contract of usury (riba), since usury is not trade but contrary to its purpose. It also indicates that each of the contracting parties must consent and enter into it by choice. And among the completeness of consent is that the subject of the contract be known; for if it is not known, consent cannot be conceived. The item must also be capable of being delivered, since what cannot be delivered resembles gambling. Thus, sale involving uncertainty (gharar) in all its forms lacks consent, so its contract is not valid. It also indicates that contracts are concluded by whatever indicates them, whether by speech or by action, because God stipulated consent; by whatever means consent is achieved, the contract is concluded thereby.

Then He concluded the verse with His words: {Indeed, God is ever Merciful to you}: among His mercy is that He protected your blood and your wealth, safeguarded them, and forbade you from violating them.

{30} Then He said: {And whoever does that}; that is, consumes wealth in falsehood and kills souls. {Through transgression and injustice}; that is, not through ignorance or forgetfulness. {We will drive him into a Fire}; that is, a great Fire, as the indefiniteness (in "nāran") indicates. {And that is ever easy for God}.

{30} Then He said: {And whoever does that}; that is, consumes wealth in falsehood and kills souls. {Through transgression and injustice}; that is, not through ignorance or forgetfulness. {We will drive him into a Fire}; that is, a great Fire, as the indefiniteness (in "nāran") indicates. {And that is ever easy for God}.

{31} This is from the grace and kindness of God toward His believing servants. He promised them that if they avoid the major prohibited sins, He will forgive them all their misdeeds and bad deeds, and admit them to a noble abode abounding in good, which is Paradise, containing what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Included in avoiding the major sins is performing the obligations whose neglect would constitute committing a major sin, such as the five daily prayers, the Friday prayer, and Ramadan fasting. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, so long as the major sins are avoided."

The best definition of major sins (kaba'ir, the plural of kabirah) is: a major sin is any act for which there is a prescribed legal penalty (hadd) in this world, or a threat of punishment (wa'id) in the Hereafter, or the negation of faith (nafy iman) for its doer, or the placing of a curse (la'nah) or wrath (ghadab) upon its doer.

{32} Almighty God forbids the believers from wishing for what God has granted others as favour, whether it is something attainable or not. So women should not wish for the distinctive qualities of men by which God has preferred them over women, nor should one who is poor or deficient wish, merely as a wish, for the state of the wealthy and the perfect. For this is envy itself: wishing that the blessing God has given to another were yours while he is deprived of it. It also entails resentment at God's decree, inclination toward idleness, and vain hopes unaccompanied by any action or earning. What is praiseworthy is two things: that the servant strive according to his ability for what benefits him in his religious and worldly interests, and that he ask God Almighty for His bounty, not relying on himself or on other than his Lord. For this reason God Almighty said: ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned﴾, that is, of their deeds that produce what is sought. ﴿And for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾. So each of them obtains nothing but what he has earned and toiled for. ﴿And ask God of His bounty﴾, that is, for all your interests in religion and in the world. This is the perfection of the servant and the sign of his happiness, unlike one who abandons action, or who relies on himself without being in need of his Lord, or who combines the two; for such a person is forsaken and a loser. And His saying ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing of all things﴾: He gives to those whom He knows to be worthy of it, and withholds from those whom He knows do not deserve it.

{33} That is: {And for every one}: of mankind {We have appointed heirs (mawali)}; that is, they will be inherited from by them, and they will be supported by them through strengthening, aid, and assistance in affairs, {of that which the parents and the near relatives leave}. This includes all the relatives, of the ascendants, the descendants, and the collateral kin; these are the heirs (mawali) from among the kindred. Then He mentioned another type of heirs (mawali), saying: {And those with whom your oaths have bound you}; that is, those with whom you have made alliance, through the pledge of alliance you concluded with them, for support, assistance, sharing of wealth, and other things. All of this is among the blessings of God upon His servants, since the allies (mawali) cooperate in ways that none of them could manage alone. God, the Exalted, said: {Then give them their share}; that is, give the allies (mawali) their share, which must be fulfilled through support, aid, and assistance, in what is not disobedience to God, and inheritance for the nearer relatives among the allies (mawali). {Indeed, God is ever, over all things, Witness}; that is, Knowing of everything by His knowledge of all matters, and Seeing of His servants' movements, and Hearing of all their voices.

He, exalted is He, informs that ﴿Men are the protectors (qawwamun) of women﴾; that is, they are their guardians and managers, by compelling them to fulfil the rights of God, exalted is He, such as observing His obligations and restraining them from corruptions. Men are obliged to compel them to that. They are also their protectors by providing for them, clothing them and housing them. Then he mentioned the reason that makes men responsible for women, saying: ﴿because God has given preference to some of them over others, and because they spend of their property﴾. That is, it is because of the preference of men over women and their favouring them. The preference of men over women is in several respects: the authority (wilayat) being restricted to men; prophethood; messengership; their being singled out for many acts of worship, such as jihad, the festival prayers and the Friday congregation; and what God has specially given them of intellect, sobriety, patience and endurance, which women do not have to the same degree. Likewise, they are singled out for spending on their wives, and indeed many expenditures are特 specific to men, distinguishing them from women. Perhaps this is the secret of His saying ﴿they spend﴾ with the object omitted, to indicate the generality of the expenditure. From all of this it is known that the husband is like a governor and master to his wife, and she, in his possession, is a captive, a servant. So his duty is to carry out what God has entrusted to him, and her duty is to be devoted to the obedience of her Lord and the obedience of her husband. Therefore He said: ﴿So the righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾; that is, obedient to God, exalted is He, ﴿guarding in the husband's absence﴾; that is, obedient to their husbands even in their absence, guarding the husband's honour and property, and that is through God's preservation of them and His granting them success, not from themselves, for the soul indeed commands to evil, but whoever puts his trust in God, God will suffice him in whatever concerns him of his religion and worldly affairs.

Then He said: ﴿As for those from whom you fear nushuz (rebellion)﴾; that is, their rising up against the obedience of their husbands, by disobeying him in word or deed. He disciplines her by the mildest means, then the next mildest. ﴿Admonish them﴾; that is, by explaining God's ruling on obedience to and disobedience of the husband, encouraging obedience and warning against disobedience. If they desist, that is what is required; otherwise, the husband may forsake them in bed (hajr), by not lying with them or having intercourse with them, to the extent that the purpose is achieved. If that does not work, he may strike them with a non-severe blow (darb ghayr mubarrih). If the purpose is achieved by one of these means and they obey you, ﴿then do not seek a means against them﴾; that is, you have obtained what you love, so leave off rebuking them for past matters and searching out faults whose mention is harmful and from which evil arises. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Most High, Great﴾; that is, He possesses absolute loftiness in all aspects and considerations: loftiness of essence, loftiness of rank, and loftiness of dominance. Al-Kabir (the Great) is the One above whom there is none greater, none more majestic, none mightier, great in His essence and attributes.

{35} That is: if you fear a breach between the spouses, estrangement and alienation, to the point that each of them is on a side (apart from the other), {then send an arbiter (hakam) from his family and an arbiter from her family}; that is, two men who are legally responsible (mukallaf), Muslim, just (adl), and sensible, who know what lies between the spouses and understand reconciliation and separation. This is derived from the word "hakam," since none is fit to be an arbiter except one who possesses these qualities. They should examine what each of them holds against the other, and then oblige each of them to do what is due. If neither of them is able to do so, they should content the other spouse with acceptance of what is available of provision and character. As long as they can achieve reunion and reconciliation, they should not deviate from it. But if the situation reaches the point where their reunion and reconciliation are possible only through enmity, severance and disobedience to Allah, and they judge that separating them is better, they shall separate them. The consent of the husband is not a condition, as is indicated by the fact that Allah named them "the two arbiters" (al-hakamayn), and an arbiter (hakam) rules even if the one ruled against does not consent. For this reason He said: {If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them}; that is, through a sound opinion and speech that draws hearts and joins the two companions together. {Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted}; that is, Knowing of all apparent and hidden matters, aware of the concealed affairs and their secrets. From His knowledge and awareness is that He has legislated for you these noble rulings and beautiful laws.

{36–37} God commands His servants to worship Him alone, with no partner. This means entering under the bondage of His servitude ('ubudiyyah) and submitting to His commands and prohibitions out of love, humility, and sincerity toward Him in all acts of worship, outward and inward. He forbids associating anything with Him, whether a lesser shirk or a greater shirk, whether an angel, a prophet, a saint, or any other created being, who possess no power to benefit or harm themselves, nor to cause death, life, or resurrection. Rather, what is obligatory and binding is to devote worship sincerely to the One who has absolute perfection from every aspect, and who has complete governance, which no one shares with Him or assists Him in.

Then, after commanding worship of Him and fulfilling His right, He commands the fulfilment of the rights of the servants, the nearest first, then the next nearest, saying: {And to parents, good treatment}; that is, treat them well with noble speech, gentle address, and beautiful conduct, by obeying their commands and avoiding what they forbid, spending on them, honouring those connected to them, and maintaining the ties of kinship, for you have no kinship except through them. Good treatment has two opposites: bad treatment (isa'ah) and the absence of good treatment, and both are forbidden. {And to the near of kin} likewise, good treatment, and this includes all relatives, near or distant, by treating them well in speech and deed, and by not severing the ties of kinship through word or deed. {And the orphans}; that is, those whose fathers have died while they were young. They have a right upon the Muslims, whether they are relatives or not, by taking them under care, showing them kindness, comforting their hearts, disciplining them, and raising them in the best manner in matters of their religion and their worldly life. {And the needy}: those whom need and poverty have confined, so that they have not obtained their sufficiency nor the sufficiency of those they support. God commands good treatment toward them by relieving their want, removing their poverty, urging others to do so, and doing whatever is possible in this regard. {And the neighbour who is of kin}; that is, the near neighbour who has two rights: the right of neighbourhood and the right of kinship. He has a right and a kindness upon his neighbour that is in accordance with custom ('urf). Likewise {the neighbour who is a stranger}; that is, one who has no kinship. The closer the neighbour by door, the more emphatic his right. The neighbour should look after his neighbour with gifts, charity, invitations, gentleness in words and deeds, and by not harming him by word or deed. {And the companion at your side}: it has been said this is the companion on a journey, and it has been said it is the wife, and it has been said it is the companion in general. The last is perhaps the most preferable, for it includes the companion at home and on the road, and it includes the wife. A companion has a right over his companion beyond mere Islam: assisting him in matters of his religion and worldly affairs, advising him, being faithful to him in ease and hardship, in what he likes and what he dislikes, loving for him what he loves for himself and disliking for him what he dislikes for himself. The more the companionship grows, the more the right is affirmed and increased. {And the wayfarer}: the stranger who may or may not be in need in a foreign land. He has a right upon the Muslims because of the severity of his need and because he is away from his homeland, by conveying him to his destination or part of it, honouring him and making him feel at ease. {And what your right hands possess}; that is, among humans and animals, by providing for their sufficiency, not burdening them with what is hard for them, helping them with what they have taken on, and disciplining them in what serves their welfare. Whoever carries out these commands is one who submits to his Lord, humbles himself before the servants of God, and yields to God's command and law, and deserves abundant reward and beautiful praise. Whoever does not do so is a servant turned away from his Lord, not submissive to His commands, nor humble toward creation; rather he is arrogant toward the servants of God, self-admiring, and boastful in his speech. Therefore He said: {Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-conceited}; that is, self-admiring and arrogant toward creation, {boastful}; one who praises himself and extols himself with pride and insolence toward the servants of God. Those whose conceit and boasting prevent them from fulfilling these rights are the ones He condemns in His words: {Who are stingy}; that is, they withhold what is obligatory upon them of rights, {and enjoin stinginess upon people}, by their words and deeds, {and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty}; that is, the knowledge by which the misguided are guided and by which the ignorant seek right guidance, yet they conceal it from them and display to them falsehood that stands between them and the truth. Thus they combine stinginess with wealth and stinginess with knowledge, and striving toward the loss of their own selves and the loss of others. These are the attributes of the disbelievers. Therefore God said: {And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment}; that is, just as they were arrogant toward the servants of God, withheld His rights, and caused others to be prevented from generosity and from being guided, He will humiliate them with painful punishment and everlasting disgrace. We seek refuge in You, O Allah, from every evil.

{38} Then He informed about spending that proceeds from showing off, reputation-seeking, and lack of faith in Him, saying: {And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people}; that is, to be seen by them, praised by them, and esteemed by them. {And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day}; that is, their spending does not proceed from sincerity and faith in Allah, nor from hope for His reward. This is one of the steps and works of Satan, to which he calls his party, so that they become companions of the Blaze, and it arises from their being accompanied by him and his incitement toward it. Therefore He said: {And whoever has Satan as a companion—evil is he as a companion}; that is, what a wretched companion and friend, one who wishes to destroy his companion and strives against him with the utmost striving. Just as whoever is stingy with what Allah has given him and conceals what Allah has bestowed upon him is a sinful disobedient one who opposes his Lord, so too whoever spends and worships other than Allah is sinful and disobedient to his Lord, deserving punishment, because Allah commanded obedience to Him and compliance with His command only in sincerity; as He said: {And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, devoting religion to Him alone}. This is the accepted deed, whose doer deserves praise and reward. Therefore Almighty God urged it by His words:

Therefore God said: {And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment}; that is, just as they were arrogant toward the servants of God, withheld His rights, and caused others to be prevented from generosity and from being guided, He will humiliate them with painful punishment and everlasting disgrace. We seek refuge in You, O Allah, from every evil.

{38} Then He informed about spending that proceeds from showing off, reputation-seeking, and lack of faith in Him, saying: {And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people}; that is, to be seen by them, praised by them, and esteemed by them. {And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day}; that is, their spending does not proceed from sincerity and faith in Allah, nor from hope for His reward. This is one of the steps and works of Satan, to which he calls his party, so that they become companions of the Blaze, and it arises from their being accompanied by him and his incitement toward it. Therefore He said: {And whoever has Satan as a companion—evil is he as a companion}; that is, what a wretched companion and friend, one who wishes to destroy his companion and strives against him with the utmost striving. Just as whoever is stingy with what Allah has given him and conceals what Allah has bestowed upon him is a sinful disobedient one who opposes his Lord, so too whoever spends and worships other than Allah is sinful and disobedient to his Lord, deserving punishment, because Allah commanded obedience to Him and compliance with His command only in sincerity; as He said: {And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, devoting religion to Him alone}. This is the accepted deed, whose doer deserves praise and reward. Therefore Almighty God urged it by His words:

{39} That is: What harm or hardship would befall them if they had faith in God, which is sincerity (ikhlas), and spent from their wealth which God provided them and bestowed upon them? They would have combined sincerity and spending. And since sincerity is a secret between the servant and his Lord, which none can perceive but God, He—exalted is He—informed of His knowledge of all conditions, saying: ﴿And God was ever Knowing of them.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 40–42:

{40} Almighty God informs us of the perfection of His justice and bounty, and of His being free from whatever contradicts this, namely injustice, whether little or much, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight﴾; that is, He does not diminish from the good deeds of His servant, nor increase his evil deeds. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. ﴿And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾; that is, up to ten times its like, or more than that, according to its nature, its benefit, and the state of its doer in sincerity, love, and perfection. ﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾; that is, in addition to the reward of the deed itself: the granting of success in other deeds, and the bestowal of abundant goodness and copious benefit.

{41} Then He said: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these people?﴾; that is, how will those circumstances be? And how will that great judgment be, which combines that the One who passes it is in full knowledge, full justice, and full wisdom, by the testimony of the purest of creation, who are the Messengers, against their nations, together with the acknowledgment of the one judged? This, by Allah, is the judgment that is the most comprehensive, most just, and most magnificent of judgments. There, those judged will remain acknowledging it, along with the perfection of His bounty, justice, praise, and commendation. There, some people will be made happy with success, salvation, honour, and triumph, and other people will be made wretched with disgrace, humiliation, and painful punishment.

{42} For this reason He said: ﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that they were leveled into the earth﴾; that is, they combined disbelief in Allah and His Messenger with disobedience to the Messenger. ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾; that is, rather, they will acknowledge before Him what they did, and their tongues, hands, and feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do. On that Day Allah will pay them their full due, their rightful recompense, and they will know that Allah is the manifest Truth. As for what has been reported, that the disbelievers will conceal their disbelief and denial, this will occur in some stations of the Day of Resurrection, when they think their denial will benefit them against the punishment of Allah. But when they recognise the realities and their limbs bear witness against them, then the matter will become clear, and there will remain no place, benefit, or use for concealment.

{43} God, exalted is He, forbids His believing servants from approaching the prayer while they are intoxicated, until they know what they are saying. This applies both to approaching the places of prayer, such as the mosque, for a drunkard is not permitted to enter it, and to the prayer itself, for prayer and any other act of worship are not permissible for the intoxicated person, because his mind is confused and he does not know what he is saying. For this reason, God, exalted is He, set a limit to this prohibition and made it conditional upon the presence of knowledge of what the drunkard is saying.

This noble verse has been abrogated by the absolute prohibition of wine, for wine was initially not forbidden. Then God, exalted is He, alluded to its prohibition in His saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.﴾ Then He forbade them from wine at the time of prayer, as in this verse. Then He prohibited it absolutely at all times in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are but filth from the work of Satan, so avoid it﴾ [5:90]. Nevertheless, its prohibition becomes more severe at the time of prayer, because it includes this great corruption of preventing the attainment of the purpose of prayer, which is its spirit and essence, namely humility and presence of heart; for wine intoxicates the heart and turns one away from the remembrance of God and from prayer.

It is derived from the meaning that entering into prayer is prohibited in a state of excessive drowsiness in which the person does not perceive what he says and does. Indeed, there may even be an indication that whoever wishes to pray should clear his mind of every preoccupation that distracts his thoughts, such as holding back the two impurities (urine and feces) and craving for food and the like, as related in the authentic hadith concerning this.

Then He said: ﴿nor in a state of major impurity, except while passing through [a place of prayer]﴾; that is, do not approach the prayer while one of you is in a state of major impurity, except in this condition, which is that of passing through, that is, you pass through the mosque without remaining in it. ﴿Until you have washed﴾; that is, once you have bathed. This is the limit of the prohibition on approaching prayer for one in major impurity, so it is permissible for one in major impurity merely to pass through the mosque.

﴿And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have contacted women, and you do not find water, then perform tayammum﴾: He permitted tayammum for the sick absolutely, whether water is present or absent, and the cause is illness that makes using water difficult. Likewise travel, for it is a likely occasion for lacking water; so if the traveler lacks it, or finds only what is needed for his drinking and the like, it is permissible for him to perform tayammum. Likewise, if a person becomes impure by urine, feces, or contact with women, it is permitted for him to perform tayammum if he does not find water, whether at home or on a journey, as the general wording of the verse indicates. The summary is that God, exalted is He, permitted tayammum in two situations: the absence of water, which applies absolutely whether at home or on a journey; and the hardship of using it, due to illness or the like.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿or you have contacted women﴾: Does it mean sexual intercourse? In that case the verse is an explicit text permitting tayammum for one in major impurity, as is supported by the numerous authentic hadiths. Or does it mean merely touching with the hand, restricted to cases where it is likely to cause the emission of madhy (pre-seminal fluid), that is, touching that is done out of desire? In that case the verse indicates that wudu is nullified by such touching. The jurists cited His saying: ﴿and you do not find water﴾ as evidence for the obligation to seek water when the time of prayer enters, for it is not said that one "did not find" someone who did not search; rather, that occurs only after searching. It is also cited as evidence that water altered by some pure substance is permissible, indeed obligatory, to use for purification, since it falls under His saying ﴿and you do not find water﴾, and this is water. This has been disputed on the grounds that it is not unqualified water, and there is room for consideration in that.

In this [noble verse] there is the legislation of this great ruling by which God bestowed favor upon this community, namely the legislation of tayammum, and the scholars have unanimously agreed upon it, and all praise is due to God.

Tayammum is performed with clean earth (al-sa'id al-tayyib), which is everything that rises upon the surface of the earth, whether or not it has dust. It is possible, however, that this is restricted to what has dust, because God said ﴿and wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾, and what has no dust cannot be wiped with. His saying ﴿wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ indicates the place of wiping in tayammum: the entire face and the two hands up to the wrists, as the authentic hadiths indicate. It is recommended that this be done with a single strike, as indicated by the hadith of 'Ammar, and in it is the teaching that the tayammum of one in major impurity is like the tayammum of others, with the face and hands.

Benefit: Know that the principles of medicine revolve around three principles: preserving health from harmful things, expelling harmful things from the body, and protecting oneself from them through diet. God has alerted to these in His Mighty Book. As for preserving health and guarding against harm, He commanded eating and drinking without extravagance, and permitted the traveler and the sick to break the fast in order to preserve their health by using what sustains the body in a balanced way, and to protect the sick from what harms him. As for expelling what is harmful, God permitted the pilgrim (muhrim) who is troubled in his head to shave it, to remove the congested vapors within it; this is an alert to expelling what is more important than that, such as urine, feces, vomit, semen, blood, and other things. Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, pointed this out.

The verse contains the obligation to wipe the whole face and both hands, and that tayammum is permissible even if the time has not become narrow, and that one is not addressed to seek water except after the existence of the cause that makes it obligatory. And God knows best.

Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾; that is, abundant in pardon and forgiveness toward His believing servants, by facilitating what He commanded them and making it extremely easy, such that it is not hard for the servant to comply and thus be burdened. Among His pardon and forgiveness is that He showed mercy to this community by legislating the purification with earth in place of water when its use is impossible. Among His pardon and forgiveness is that He opened the door of repentance and turning back to the sinners, invited them to it, and promised them the forgiveness of their sins. Among His pardon and forgiveness is that if a believer came to Him with the earth's fill of sins, then met Him without associating anything with Him, He would come to him with its fill of forgiveness.

{44} This is a censure of those who "were given a portion of the Scripture," and within it is a warning to His servants against being deceived by them and falling into their snares. He informs that they themselves "purchase error" (yashtarun al-dalalah); that is, they love it with a great love and prefer it with the preference of one who spends much wealth in pursuit of what he loves. Thus they prefer misguidance to guidance, disbelief to faith, and wretchedness to happiness. And despite this, "they wish that you should lose the way" (yuridun an tadillu al-sabil); so they are eager to mislead you to the utmost degree of eagerness, exerting their effort in that. But since Allah is the Protector (Wali) of His believing servants and their Helper, He made clear to them what their misguidance and their misleading of others entailed.

{45} For this reason He said: "And Allah suffices as a Protector (Wali)." That is, He manages the affairs of His servants, shows them kindness in all their matters, and facilitates for them that by which their happiness and success come about. "And Allah suffices as a Helper (Nasir)": He gives them victory over their enemies, makes clear to them what they should beware of from them, and aids them against them. So His guardianship (wilayah) includes the attainment of good, and His help includes the removal of evil.

{46} Then He explained the manner of their misguidance, their obstinacy, and their preference of falsehood over truth, saying: "From those who are Jews" (min alladhina hadu); that is, the Jews, and their scholars of misguidance in particular, "they distort words from their places" (yuharrifun al-kalim 'an mawadi'ihi). This may be by altering the wording, or the meaning, or both together. Among their distortions is applying to someone else the attributes mentioned in their books, which do not fit and are not true except of Muhammad (ﷺ), claiming that they are not meant for him nor intended by them, but rather were intended for someone other than him, and concealing that. This is their condition in knowledge, the worst of conditions: they reversed the realities in it, placed truth upon falsehood, and denied the truth on account of it. As for their condition in action and submission, they "say: We hear and we disobey" (yaqulun sami'na wa 'asayna); that is, "we hear your word and we disobey your command." This is the utmost of disbelief, obstinacy, and recoil from submission. Likewise they address the Messenger (ﷺ) with the most vile address and the furthest from courtesy, saying: "Hear without being made to hear" (isma' ghayra musma'); their intention is: "Hear from us, without being made to hear what you love, but rather be made to hear what you hate." And "Ra'ina" (wa ra'ina): their intention by it is foolishness, with an ugly defect, and they think that since the expression can bear other than what they intended, it will pass off upon Allah and His Messenger. Thus they used that expression, which they twist with their tongues, to reach the slandering of the religion and the defaming of the Messenger, and they openly state this among themselves. For this reason He said: "Twisting their tongues and slandering the religion" (layyan bi-alsinatihim wa ta'nan fi al-din). Then He guided them to what is better for them than that, saying: "And if they had said: We hear and we obey; and hear and look upon us (unzurna), it would have been better for them and more upright." This is because such speech includes good address, the courtesy fitting in addressing the Messenger, entering under the obedience of Allah, submission to His command, and gentle politeness in seeking knowledge by hearing their question and attending to their matter. This is what they should have adopted. But since their natures were not pure, they turned away from that, and Allah expelled them for their disbelief and obstinacy. For this reason He said: "But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few."

{47} Almighty God commands the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, to believe in the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what God has sent down to him of the Great Qur'an, which is dominant over (muhayman 'ala) the other earlier books and which confirms them; for they gave information about it, and when the thing they informed of came to pass, it became a confirmation of that information. Furthermore, if they do not believe in this Qur'an, then they have not believed in what is in their hands of the books, because the books of God confirm one another and agree with one another. So the claim to believe in some of them while disbelieving in others is a false claim that cannot be true.

In His saying: ﴿Believe in what We have sent down, confirming what you already have﴾, there is an exhortation to them, and that they should be the first of others to hasten to it, because of the favor God has bestowed upon them of knowledge and the Book, which requires that their obligation be greater than that of others. For this reason He threatened them for not believing, saying: ﴿before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs﴾. This is a recompense of the same kind as their deeds: just as they abandoned the truth, preferred falsehood, and reversed realities, making falsehood truth and truth falsehood, they are recompensed in kind by having their faces obliterated just as they obliterated the truth, and by having them turned back upon their backs by being made to be on the back of their necks, and this is the most hideous of conditions. ﴿Or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾: by banishing them from His mercy and punishing them by transforming them into apes, as He did to their brethren who transgressed on the Sabbath, when We said to them: "Be apes, despised." ﴿And the command of God is always fulfilled﴾, like His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾.

{48} He, exalted is He, informs that He does not forgive whoever associates anything with Him among the created beings, and that He forgives what is less than that of sins, both minor and major. This forgiveness is subject to His will, when His wisdom requires forgiving them. Sins other than shirk (associating partners with God), God has made many means for their forgiveness: such as good deeds that erase (sins), and afflictions that expiate them in this world, in the barzakh (intermediate state), and on the Day of Resurrection; the supplication of believers for one another; the intercession of intercessors; and above all of that, His mercy, which is due to the people of faith and monotheism. This is in contrast to shirk, for the polytheist has closed off for himself the doors of forgiveness and shut the doors of mercy against himself. Acts of obedience do not benefit him without monotheism, and afflictions do not avail him anything. {And for the wrongdoers there will be no intercessor on the Day of Resurrection, nor a close friend.} For this reason He, exalted is He, said: {And whoever associates others with God has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin} (Qur'an 4:48); i.e., he has committed a great crime. And what greater wrong is there than one who equates the created being, who was made from dust, deficient in every respect, utterly poor in his very essence in every way, who does not possess for himself any benefit, harm, death, life, or resurrection, with the Creator of everything, the Perfect in every respect, the Self-Sufficient in His essence beyond all His creation, in whose hand is benefit and harm, giving and withholding, and every blessing that comes from created beings is from Him, exalted is He? Is there anything greater than this wrong? For this reason He has decreed for its doer everlasting abiding in punishment and deprivation of reward: {Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire} (Qur'an 5:72).

This noble verse applies to the one who does not repent. As for the one who repents, shirk and what is less than it are forgiven for him, as God, exalted is He, said: {Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God; indeed God forgives all sins} (Qur'an 39:53); i.e., for whoever turns to Him in repentance and returns to Him.

{49} This is an expression of wonder from God toward His servants, and a rebuke of those who praise themselves among the Jews and Christians, and of whoever follows their path from among everyone who purifies himself by a matter that is not in him. This is because the Jews and Christians say: "We are the children of God and His beloved" (Qur'an 5:18), and they say: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian" (Qur'an 2:111). This is mere claim for which there is no proof. The proof is only what God has informed of in the Qur'an, in His saying: "Yes, whoever submits his face to God while being a doer of good will have his reward with his Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve" (Qur'an 2:112). These are the ones whom God has purified. For this reason He said here: "Rather, God purifies whom He wills" (Qur'an 4:49); that is, by faith and righteous action, by abandoning vile character traits and adorning oneself with beautiful qualities. As for these people, although they purify themselves by their own assertion that they are upon something and that the reward belongs to them alone, they are liars in that. They have no share in the qualities of the purified because of their wrongdoing and disbelief, not because of any injustice from God toward them. For this reason He said: "And they will not be wronged the extent of a fatil" (Qur'an 4:49). This is to establish generality; that is, they will not be wronged anything, nor the amount of the fatil that is in the split of a date-pit, or that which is twisted from the dirt of the hand and other things.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 4, verses 58–59:**

{58} The *amanat* (trusts, singular *amanah*) are everything a person is entrusted with and commanded to fulfil. Allah commanded His servants to discharge them, that is, in full and complete, neither diminished, nor withheld, nor delayed. This includes the trusts of public offices, property, secrets, and the commands that no one knows except Allah. The jurists (*fuqaha'*) have mentioned that whoever is entrusted with a trust must keep it in a safe place suited to it. They said: because it cannot be discharged except by keeping it, so keeping it is obligatory. In His words ﴿to their rightful owners﴾ there is an indication that it must not be handed over or delivered to anyone other than the one who entrusted it, and his agent stands in his place. So if one hands it to someone other than its owner, he has not discharged it.

﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾. This includes judging between them in matters of blood, property and honour, in small matters and great, whether the party is near or far, righteous or wicked, a friend or an enemy. By "justice" which Allah commanded to judge by is what He legislated through His Messenger ﷺ, of the *hudud* (prescribed punishments) and rulings. This requires knowing justice in order to judge by it. Since these commands are good and just, He said: ﴿Indeed, excellent is that with which He instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ This is a praise by Allah of His commands and prohibitions, because they contain the benefits of both abodes and the averting of their harms, for their Lawgiver is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, from whom nothing is hidden, and who knows the interests of the servants that they do not know.

{59} Then He commanded obedience to Himself and to His Messenger, which is by carrying out their commands, obligatory and recommended, and avoiding their prohibitions. He commanded obedience to *ulu al-amr* (those in authority), who are the rulers over the people: the leaders, the judges, and the muftis (jurisconsults). For the affairs of people's religion and worldly life are not sound except by obeying them and submitting to them, in obedience to Allah and desire for what is with Him. But on condition that they do not command disobedience to Allah. If they command that, there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator. Perhaps this is the secret of omitting the verb when commanding obedience to them and mentioning it with obedience to the Messenger: the Messenger commands only obedience to Allah, and whoever obeys him has obeyed Allah, whereas for those in authority, the condition of obeying them is that it not be a sin.

Then He commanded referring everything about which people dispute, from the foundations of religion and its branches, to Allah and to the Messenger ﷺ, that is, to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. For in them both is the decision on all matters of disagreement, whether explicitly, by their generality, by allusion, by indication, by implication, or by the general meaning on which similar cases are analogised (*qiyas*). For the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger are the foundation of religion, and faith is not sound except by them. Therefore referring to them is a condition of faith. So He said: ﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. This indicates that whoever does not refer disputed matters to them is not truly a believer, but rather a believer in *taghut* (false authority), as mentioned in the verse following it. ﴿That﴾, that is, referring to Allah and His Messenger, ﴿is better and more favourable in outcome﴾. For the ruling of Allah and His Messenger is the best and most just of rulings, and the most beneficial for people in the matters of their religion, their worldly life, and their final end.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 60–63:

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to seek judgment from the taghut (every ruler or authority that judges by other than the Law of Allah)?﴾ Allah marvels His servants at the state of the hypocrites, who claim they believe in what the Messenger brought and in what came before him. Yet they desire to seek judgment from the taghut, which is everyone who judges by other than the Law of Allah, so he is a taghut. Meanwhile, they have been ordered ﴿to reject it﴾. How can this combine with faith? Faith requires submission to the Law of Allah and making it the judge in every matter. Whoever claims to be a believer yet chooses the judgment of the taghut over the judgment of Allah is lying in that claim. This is from the misguidance of Shaytan (Satan) toward them. Therefore He said: ﴿And Satan desires to lead them far astray﴾ from the truth.

﴿How, then,﴾ will be the state of these misguided ones ﴿when a calamity strikes them because of what their hands have put forward﴾ of sins, among them seeking judgment from the taghut? ﴿Then they come to you﴾ making excuses for what they did, and they say: ﴿We intended nothing but good and reconciliation.﴾ That is, we did not intend in this anything but kindness to the disputants and conciliation between them. They are liars in that, for true kindness lies entirely in seeking the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?

Therefore He said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, that is, of hypocrisy and bad intent. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, that is, do not concern yourself with them, nor confront them over what they did and committed. ﴿And admonish them﴾, that is, make clear to them the judgment of Allah, with encouragement to submit to Allah and warning against abandoning it. ﴿And say to them in themselves a far-reaching word﴾, that is, advise them privately, between you and them, for that is more effective in achieving the aim, and be thorough in rebuking them and suppressing them from what they were upon. In this is evidence that one who commits sins, even if one turns away from him, should still be advised privately, and his admonition should be pursued thoroughly with what is thought to achieve the aim.

They are liars in that, for true kindness lies entirely in seeking the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?

Therefore He said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, that is, of hypocrisy and bad intent. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, that is, do not concern yourself with them, nor confront them over what they did and committed. ﴿And admonish them﴾, that is, make clear to them the judgment of Allah, with encouragement to submit to Allah and warning against abandoning it. ﴿And say to them in themselves a far-reaching word﴾, that is, advise them privately, between you and them, for that is more effective in achieving the aim, and be thorough in rebuking them and suppressing them from what they were upon. In this is evidence that one who commits sins, even if one turns away from him, should still be advised privately, and his admonition should be pursued thoroughly with what is thought to achieve the aim.

{64} He, the Exalted, informs us of something that implies the command and exhortation to obey the Messenger and submit to him. The purpose of sending messengers is that they be obeyed, so that those to whom they are sent submit to them in everything they command and forbid, and that they be held in honor, as a master is honored by one who obeys him. This also establishes the infallibility (ʿiṣmah) of the messengers in what they convey from God and in what they command and forbid. God commanded obedience to them unconditionally, so if they were not infallible, never prescribing what is wrong, He would not have commanded it unconditionally. His words, ﴿by God's leave﴾, mean that obedience from the one who obeys proceeds from God's decree (qadāʾ) and predestination (qadar). This contains the affirmation of divine decree and predestination, the exhortation to seek God's help, and the clarification that a person cannot obey the Messenger unless God helps him.

Then He informs us of His great generosity and bounty, and of His call to those who have committed misdeeds to acknowledge their sins, repent, and seek God's forgiveness. He says: ﴿And if, when they had wronged themselves, they had come to you﴾, meaning acknowledging their sins and remorseful over them, ﴿and asked God's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found God Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾, meaning He would have turned to them in forgiveness of their wrong, and shown them mercy by accepting their repentance, granting them success in it, and rewarding them for it. This coming to the Messenger (ﷺ) is specific to his lifetime, because the context indicates this, since seeking forgiveness from the Messenger can only occur during his life. As for after his death, nothing is to be requested from him, and to do so is shirk.

{65} Then God swore by His noble Self that they do not believe until they make the Messenger judge in what they dispute among themselves, meaning in every matter in which disagreement arises, unlike matters of consensus (ijmāʿ), which can only be based on the Book and the Sunnah. Yet this judgment is not sufficient until no constriction (ḥaraj) or tightness remains in their hearts. Their making him judge in a grudging manner is also not sufficient until they submit to his judgment with full submission, with an open chest, tranquil souls, and obedience both outwardly and inwardly. Thus, judgment belongs to the station of Islam, the removal of constriction belongs to the station of faith (īmān), and submission belongs to the station of excellence (iḥsān). Whoever attains these stations and perfects them has attained all the levels of religion. Whoever abandons this mentioned judgment without committing to it is a disbeliever, and whoever abandons it while committed to it has the ruling of those like him among the disobedient.

{66} Almighty God informs that if He had prescribed upon His servants commands that are burdensome to the souls, such as killing oneself and leaving one's homes, only a few and a rare minority of them would have done it. So let them praise their Lord and thank Him for facilitating what He commanded them, the commands that are easy for everyone and whose performance is not difficult. In this is an indication that the servant should consider the opposite of what he is in of disliked things, so that acts of worship become light for him and he increases in praise and thanks to his Lord.

Then He informs that if they {did what they were admonished with}, i.e., what was assigned to them at every time according to its measure, and they exerted their resolve and spared their souls to perform it and complete it, and their souls did not aspire to what they had not reached and were not preparing for, this is what the servant should do: look at the state he is obliged to perform, complete it, and then advance gradually, little by little, until he reaches what has been decreed for him of knowledge and action in matters of religion and worldly life. This is in contrast to one whose soul aspires to a matter he has not reached and has not yet been commanded with; for he hardly reaches that, because of the scattering of resolve, the arising of laziness, and the lack of energy. Then He arranged what they would obtain upon performing what they were admonished with, and it is four matters:

The first: goodness, in His saying: {it would have been better for them}; i.e., they would have been among the good people, characterized by their attributes of good deeds that they were commanded to do; and the attribute of the wicked would be negated from them by that, because the establishment of a thing necessitates the negation of its opposite.

The second: the attainment of firmness and steadfastness and its increase. Indeed, God makes firm those who believe because of what they did of faith, which is the performance of what they were admonished with. So He makes them firm in the worldly life when trials arrive regarding commands, prohibitions, and calamities, so they attain a steadfastness by which they are enabled to perform the commands and abandon the prohibitions that the soul inclines to do; and when calamities that the servant dislikes befall, he is enabled to be firm by being granted success in patience, or contentment, or gratitude, so help from God descends upon him to perform that. And they attain steadfastness upon the religion at death and in the grave. Also, the servant who performs what he has been commanded does not cease to train himself upon the legal commands until he becomes accustomed to them and longs for them and for their like, so that this becomes a help for him to remain steadfast in acts of obedience.

{67} The third: His saying: {And We would have given them from Us a great reward}; i.e., in the immediate and the hereafter, which is for the spirit, the heart, and the body, and of everlasting bliss, of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human.

So whoever is guided to a straight path has been granted success in every good, and every evil and harm is repelled from him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 69–70:

{69} That is: whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, according to his condition and the measure of what is obligatory upon him, whether male or female, young or old; {then they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour}; that is, the great blessing that entails perfection, success and happiness: {of the prophets}, those whom Allah preferred with His revelation and specially chose by sending them to creation and calling them to Allah, exalted is He. {And the truthful}: they are those whose affirmation of what the messengers brought was perfected; they knew the truth and affirmed it with their certainty, and by upholding it in speech, action and state, and by calling to Allah. {And the martyrs}: those who fought in the way of Allah to make the word of Allah supreme, and were killed. {And the righteous}: those whose outward and inward were made righteous, so their deeds were made righteous. Thus, whoever obeys Allah, exalted is He, is with these and in their companionship. {And excellent are those as companions}: through gathering with them in the Gardens of Bliss and delight in their nearness, in the neighbourhood of the Lord of the worlds.

{70} {That is the bounty}: which they attained {from Allah}. It is He who granted them success in that and helped them to it, and bestowed upon them reward beyond what their deeds could reach. {And sufficient is Allah as Knower}: He knows the states of His servants and who among them deserves the abundant reward, by what they performed of righteous deeds in which the heart and the limbs were in agreement.
