{70} {That is the bounty}: which they attained {from Allah}. It is He who granted them success in that and helped them to it, and bestowed upon them reward beyond what their deeds could reach. {And sufficient is Allah as Knower}: He knows the states of His servants and who among them deserves the abundant reward, by what they performed of righteous deeds in which the heart and the limbs were in agreement.

{71} God commands His believing servants to take their precautions against their disbelieving enemies. This includes taking every means by which one can fight them, and by which their plotting and strength can be repelled: using fortifications and trenches, learning archery and horsemanship, learning the crafts that help in this, and knowing their entrances, exits and schemes. It also includes mobilization in the way of God (al-nafir fi sabil Allah). For this reason He said: ﴿Go forth in small groups or go forth all together﴾. That is, scattered (ثبات, thubat): a detachment (sariyyah) or an army sets out while others remain behind, or all go forth together. All of this follows what benefits Muslims, what weakens the enemy, and what secures the Muslims' religion. This verse is similar to His saying: ﴿Prepare against them whatever you can of strength﴾.

{72} Then He spoke of the weak in faith, who are lax in jihad (striving in the way of God). He said: ﴿And indeed among you﴾, that is, O believers, ﴿is one who lingers﴾, that is, who holds back from jihad in the way of God out of weakness, cowardice and fear. This is the correct view. It has been said that the meaning is that he discourages others (ليبطئن غيره), that is, he dissuades them from fighting, and that these are the hypocrites. But the first view is preferable for two reasons. The first is His saying ﴿among you﴾, since the address is to the believers. The second is His saying at the end of the verse: ﴿as if there had never been between you and him any affection﴾, for God has severed the bond of affection between the disbelievers, both polytheists and hypocrites, and the believers.

Moreover, this is the reality: the believers are of two kinds. Those who are truthful in their faith have that faith bring them perfect conviction and jihad. And there are the weak, who entered Islam, so that faith in them is feeble and cannot withstand jihad. This is like God's saying: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted'"﴾, and the rest of the verses.

Then He mentioned the aims of these laggards and the final purpose of their intentions, and that the greatest of their concern is this world and its trappings. He said: ﴿If a misfortune strikes you﴾, that is, a defeat, a killing, or the enemy gaining the upper hand over you in some circumstance, for God has wisdoms in that, ﴿he says, "God has blessed me since I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ Out of the weakness of his mind and faith, he considered that staying back from jihad, in which that misfortune occurred, was a blessing. He did not realize that the true blessing is success in this great act of obedience, by which faith grows strong, the servant is saved from punishment and loss, and he gains great reward and the pleasure of the Generous, the Bestower. As for sitting back, although it may bring some rest for a while, it is followed by long fatigue and great pains, and he misses what the mujahidin obtain.

{73} Then He said: ﴿But if a bounty from God reaches you﴾, that is, victory and spoils of war, ﴿he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great success."﴾ That is, he wishes to be present in order to obtain the spoils. He has no desire or intention other than that, as if he were not one of you, O assembly of believers, and as if there were no bond of faithful affection between you and him. Its requirement is that believers share in all their interests and in repelling their harms. They rejoice when these are attained, even if it is through the hand of another of their brothers in faith, and they grieve when these are lost, and they all strive together in every matter by which they set right their religion and their worldly lives. So this man, who desires only the world, does not possess the faithful spirit described here.

{74} Among God's kindness to His servants is that He does not cut off His mercy from them, nor close its doors to them. Rather, whoever attains less than what befits him, He commands and calls to make up his deficiency and perfect his soul. For this reason He commanded these people to sincerity and to going forth in His way. He said: ﴿So let those fight in the way of God who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾. This is one of the opinions concerning this verse, and it is the most correct. It has been said that its meaning is: let the believers who are perfect in faith and truthful in their faith fight in the way of God, ﴿those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾, that is, who sell this world, turning away from it, for the Hereafter, desiring it. These are the ones addressed, because they are the ones who have prepared themselves and resolved upon fighting the enemies, due to the complete faith they possess, which requires that. As for those laggards, they are not regarded, whether they go out or stay behind. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration"﴾, and the rest of the verses, and His saying: ﴿If these disbelieve in it, We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾.

It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: let the fighter and the striver fight against the disbelievers, ﴿those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾. In this reading, ﴿those﴾ is in the accusative position as an object. ﴿And whoever fights in the way of God﴾, by that being a jihad that God and His Messenger have commanded, and the servant being sincere to God in it, intending the face of God, ﴿and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward﴾: an increase in his faith and religion, spoils of war, good repute, and the reward of the mujahidin in the way of God, for whom God has prepared in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

That is, scattered (ثبات, thubat): a detachment (sariyyah) or an army sets out while others remain behind, or all go forth together. All of this follows what benefits Muslims, what weakens the enemy, and what secures the Muslims' religion. This verse is similar to His saying: ﴿Prepare against them whatever you can of strength﴾.

{72} Then He spoke of the weak in faith, who are lax in jihad (striving in the way of God). He said: ﴿And indeed among you﴾, that is, O believers, ﴿is one who lingers﴾, that is, who holds back from jihad in the way of God out of weakness, cowardice and fear. This is the correct view. It has been said that the meaning is that he discourages others (ليبطئن غيره), that is, he dissuades them from fighting, and that these are the hypocrites. But the first view is preferable for two reasons. The first is His saying ﴿among you﴾, since the address is to the believers. The second is His saying at the end of the verse: ﴿as if there had never been between you and him any affection﴾, for God has severed the bond of affection between the disbelievers, both polytheists and hypocrites, and the believers.

Moreover, this is the reality: the believers are of two kinds. Those who are truthful in their faith have that faith bring them perfect conviction and jihad. And there are the weak, who entered Islam, so that faith in them is feeble and cannot withstand jihad. This is like God's saying: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted'"﴾, and the rest of the verses.

Then He mentioned the aims of these laggards and the final purpose of their intentions, and that the greatest of their concern is this world and its trappings. He said: ﴿If a misfortune strikes you﴾, that is, a defeat, a killing, or the enemy gaining the upper hand over you in some circumstance, for God has wisdoms in that, ﴿he says, "God has blessed me since I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ Out of the weakness of his mind and faith, he considered that staying back from jihad, in which that misfortune occurred, was a blessing. He did not realize that the true blessing is success in this great act of obedience, by which faith grows strong, the servant is saved from punishment and loss, and he gains great reward and the pleasure of the Generous, the Bestower. As for sitting back, although it may bring some rest for a while, it is followed by long fatigue and great pains, and he misses what the mujahidin obtain.

{73} Then He said: ﴿But if a bounty from God reaches you﴾, that is, victory and spoils of war, ﴿he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great success."﴾ That is, he wishes to be present in order to obtain the spoils. He has no desire or intention other than that, as if he were not one of you, O assembly of believers, and as if there were no bond of faithful affection between you and him. Its requirement is that believers share in all their interests and in repelling their harms. They rejoice when these are attained, even if it is through the hand of another of their brothers in faith, and they grieve when these are lost, and they all strive together in every matter by which they set right their religion and their worldly lives. So this man, who desires only the world, does not possess the faithful spirit described here.

{74} Among God's kindness to His servants is that He does not cut off His mercy from them, nor close its doors to them. Rather, whoever attains less than what befits him, He commands and calls to make up his deficiency and perfect his soul. For this reason He commanded these people to sincerity and to going forth in His way. He said: ﴿So let those fight in the way of God who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾. This is one of the opinions concerning this verse, and it is the most correct. It has been said that its meaning is: let the believers who are perfect in faith and truthful in their faith fight in the way of God, ﴿those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾, that is, who sell this world, turning away from it, for the Hereafter, desiring it. These are the ones addressed, because they are the ones who have prepared themselves and resolved upon fighting the enemies, due to the complete faith they possess, which requires that. As for those laggards, they are not regarded, whether they go out or stay behind. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration"﴾, and the rest of the verses, and His saying: ﴿If these disbelieve in it, We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾.

It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: let the fighter and the striver fight against the disbelievers, ﴿those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾. In this reading, ﴿those﴾ is in the accusative position as an object. ﴿And whoever fights in the way of God﴾, by that being a jihad that God and His Messenger have commanded, and the servant being sincere to God in it, intending the face of God, ﴿and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward﴾: an increase in his faith and religion, spoils of war, good repute, and the reward of the mujahidin in the way of God, for whom God has prepared in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

{71} God commands His believing servants to take their precautions against their disbelieving enemies. This includes taking every means by which one can fight them, and by which their plotting and strength can be repelled: using fortifications and trenches, learning archery and horsemanship, learning the crafts that help in this, and knowing their entrances, exits and schemes. {75} This is an exhortation from God to His believing servants, and an urging upon them to fight in His cause. It shows that this has become obligatory for them, and that great blame is directed at them for abandoning it. So He says: ﴿And why should you not fight in the cause of God,﴾ while the weak men, women and children, who are unable to devise any means and do not find a way, have nevertheless suffered the greatest oppression from their enemies. They pray that God would appoint for them a protector and a helper who will rescue them from this town whose people are wrongdoers. Thus your fighting in this manner falls under the category of fighting and defending your families, your children and your women-folk; for the door of jihad which is the pursuit of the disbelievers, although it contains great merit and the one who stays back from it is blamed most severely, the jihad in which the weak among you are rescued is greater in reward and more beneficial in outcome, in that it falls under the category of repelling the enemies.

Then he said:

{76} This is information from God that the believers fight in His cause, {and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut} (ṭāghūt), who is Satan. Within this are several benefits:

Among them: a servant's struggle (jihad) in the cause of God, his sincerity and his following (of the Prophet) are in proportion to his faith. Striving in the cause of God is among the effects of faith, its requirements and its necessary consequences; just as fighting in the cause of the Taghut is among the branches of disbelief and its requirements.

Among them: the one who fights in the cause of God should have, and it is fitting for him to have, a degree of patience and endurance that others cannot sustain. If the allies of Satan are patient and fight while they are upon falsehood, then the people of truth are more deserving of this. As God, exalted is He, said on this meaning: {If you suffer pain, then indeed they suffer pain as you suffer pain, and you hope from God what they do not hope...} (4:104), the verse.

Among them: the one who fights in the cause of God relies upon a firm support, which is the truth and reliance upon God. The possessor of strength and a firm support is required to show patience, steadfastness and vigour in a way that is not required of one who fights for falsehood, which has no reality and no good outcome. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: {So fight the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak} (4:76). And the kayd (plot/scheme) is the pursuit of hidden paths to harm the enemy. Satan, however far his deceit may reach, is in an extreme state of weakness that cannot stand before the least of the truth nor before God's plot against His believing servants.

{77} When the Muslims were in Makkah, they were commanded to perform the prayer (al-Salah) and to give zakah, meaning to aid the poor, not the well-known zakah (the obligatory alms-tax, zakah) with its nisab (minimum threshold) and conditions, for that was not made obligatory until Madinah. They were not commanded to fight the enemies, for several reasons:

Among them: it is part of the wisdom of the Creator, exalted is He, that He legislates for His servants in a manner that does not burden them, beginning with what is most important, then what is next, and the easiest before the easier.

Among them: had fighting been made obligatory upon them while their number and equipment were few and their enemies many, this would have led to the annihilation of Islam. So the greater interest was given precedence over what is less than it. And there are other wisdoms besides these.

Some of the believers wished that fighting had been made obligatory upon them in that situation, when it was not fitting for it. What was fitting then was to carry out what they had been commanded at that time: tawhid (affirming the oneness of God), the prayer, zakah, and the like. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But if they had done what they were admonished with, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness﴾. When they migrated to Madinah and Islam became strong, fighting was prescribed for them at its appropriate time. Then a group of those who had been hastening to fight before that time, out of fear of the people, weakness, and faintheartedness, said: ﴿Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾ In this there is their impatience and their objection against Allah. What was due from them was the opposite of this state: submission to the command of Allah and patience with His orders. They reversed the required matter and said: ﴿Why did You not delay us to a near term?﴾ That is, "Why did You not postpone the obligation of fighting to a period later than the present time?" This state often afflicts one who is not steady and hastens into matters before their time. He generally does not endure them when they arrive, nor does he bear their burden, but remains of little patience.

Then Allah admonished them concerning this state of holding back from fighting, saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. That is, the enjoyment of the pleasures and comforts of this world is little. Bearing burdens in obedience to Allah for a short period is therefore easy for souls and light upon them, for when they know that the hardship they endure will not last long, it becomes easy for them. How much more so when they weigh this world against the Hereafter, and see that the Hereafter is better than it in its essence, its pleasures, and its duration. As for its essence, the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in the authentic hadith: "The place of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it." As for its pleasures, they are pure, free from troubles. Indeed, every pleasure that comes to mind or occurs to thought is surpassed by the pleasure of Paradise, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾. And Allah said through His Prophet: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

As for the pleasures of this world, they are mixed with various kinds of disturbance. If one compared its pleasures with the pains, worries, and griefs that accompany them, there would be no comparison between them in any respect. As for their duration, this world is transient, and the lifespan of a person in relation to this world is a very brief thing, whereas the Hereafter is everlasting in its bliss, and its people abide in it forever. So when the intelligent person reflects upon these two abodes and grasps their reality as it should be grasped, he will know what is most worthy of preference, of striving for, and of exertion in seeking. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. That is, those who guard against shirk and all the forbidden things. ﴿And you will not be wronged even as much as the thread of a date-stone﴾. That is, your striving for the Hereafter you will find complete and abundant, not diminished in any way.

{78} Then He informed that caution does not avail against decree, and that sitting at home does not repel anything from one who sits, saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾. That is, at whatever time and in whatever place. ﴿Even if you should be within towers well constructed﴾. That is, within impregnable fortresses and lofty residences. All of this is an incitement to jihad in the way of Allah: sometimes by encouraging through its virtue and reward, sometimes by warning of the punishment for abandoning it, sometimes by informing that sitting at home does not benefit those who sit, and sometimes by facilitating the path to it and shortening it.

Then He said: ﴿And if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; but if evil strikes them, they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [the matter] with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself. And We have sent you to the mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness.﴾

{78} He, exalted is He, informs about those who do not know, who turn away from what the messengers brought and oppose them, that when good comes to them, that is, fertility, abundance of wealth, plenty of children, and health, they say: ﴿This is from Allah﴾. And if evil befalls them, that is, drought, poverty, sickness, the death of children and loved ones, they say: ﴿This is from you﴾, that is, "because of what you have brought us, O Muhammad!" They regarded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a bad omen, just as their likes regarded the messengers of Allah as a bad omen. As Allah informed about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿When good came to them, they said, "This is ours"; but if evil struck them, they ascribed it as ill omen to Moses and those with him﴾. The people of Salih said: ﴿We consider you and those with you as a bad omen﴾. The people of Ya-Sin said to their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you...﴾, the verse. So when their hearts resembled one another in disbelief, their statements and actions resembled one another. Likewise, whoever attributes the occurrence of evil or the loss of good to what the messengers brought, or to part of it, falls within this grave condemnation. Allah answered them: ﴿Say, "All"﴾, that is, of the good and evil, the benefit and the harm, ﴿is from Allah﴾, that is, by His decree, His destiny, and His creation. ﴿So what is [the matter] with these people﴾, that is, those from whom this false statement issued, ﴿that they can hardly understand any statement﴾, that is, they do not understand any statement at all, nor come close to understanding it, or they understand from it only a weak understanding. In any case, this is a condemnation and rebuke of them for their failure to understand and comprehend from Allah and from His Messenger, and that is because of their disbelief and their turning away.

Included within this is praise for the one who understands from Allah and His Messenger, and an incitement to that and to the means that help achieve it: attentiveness to their speech, reflection upon it, and following the paths that lead to it. For if they had understood from Allah, they would have known that good and evil, and good deeds and bad deeds, are all by the decree and destiny of Allah, and nothing of them escapes that, and that the messengers, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon them, are not a cause of any evil that occurs, neither they themselves nor what they brought, for they were sent with the interests of this world, the Hereafter, and religion.

{79} Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever good reaches you﴾, that is, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from Allah﴾: it is He who bestows it and facilitates it by facilitating its causes. ﴿And whatever evil reaches you﴾, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of your sins and your earnings, and what Allah pardons is more numerous. Allah, exalted is He, has opened for His servants the doors of His kindness, commanded them to enter through His righteousness and bounty, and informed them that sins prevent His bounty. So if the servant commits them, let him blame no one but himself, for he is the one who prevents himself from receiving Allah's bounty and righteousness.

Then He informed about the universality of the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness﴾, that you are truly the Messenger of Allah, by what He supported you with through His help, the manifest miracles, and the clear proofs. These are the greatest testimony absolutely, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you."﴾ When one knows that Allah, exalted is He, is perfect in knowledge, complete in power, and great in wisdom, and that He has supported His Messenger with what He supported him with and granted him a great victory, he will be certain thereby that he is the Messenger of Allah. Otherwise, had he fabricated some of the sayings attributed to Him, He would have seized him by the right hand and then severed his aorta.

For if they had understood from Allah, they would have known that good and evil, and good deeds and bad deeds, are all by the decree and destiny of Allah, and nothing of them escapes that, and that the messengers, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon them, are not a cause of any evil that occurs, neither they themselves nor what they brought, for they were sent with the interests of this world, the Hereafter, and religion.

{79} Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever good reaches you﴾, that is, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from Allah﴾: it is He who bestows it and facilitates it by facilitating its causes. ﴿And whatever evil reaches you﴾, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of your sins and your earnings, and what Allah pardons is more numerous. Allah, exalted is He, has opened for His servants the doors of His kindness, commanded them to enter through His righteousness and bounty, and informed them that sins prevent His bounty. So if the servant commits them, let him blame no one but himself, for he is the one who prevents himself from receiving Allah's bounty and righteousness.

Then He informed about the universality of the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness﴾, that you are truly the Messenger of Allah, by what He supported you with through His help, the manifest miracles, and the clear proofs. These are the greatest testimony absolutely, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you."﴾ When one knows that Allah, exalted is He, is perfect in knowledge, complete in power, and great in wisdom, and that He has supported His Messenger with what He supported him with and granted him a great victory, he will be certain thereby that he is the Messenger of Allah. Otherwise, had he fabricated some of the sayings attributed to Him, He would have seized him by the right hand and then severed his aorta.

{77} When the Muslims were in Makkah, they were commanded to perform the prayer (al-Salah) and to give zakah, meaning to aid the poor, not the well-known zakah (the obligatory alms-tax, zakah) with its nisab (minimum threshold) and conditions, for that was not made obligatory until Madinah. They were not commanded to fight the enemies, for several reasons:

Among them: it is part of the wisdom of the Creator, exalted is He, that He legislates for His servants in a manner that does not burden them, beginning with what is most important, then what is next, and the easiest before the easier.

Among them: had fighting been made obligatory upon them while their number and equipment were few and their enemies many, this would have led to the annihilation of Islam. So the greater interest was given precedence over what is less than it. And there are other wisdoms besides these.

Some of the believers wished that fighting had been made obligatory upon them in that situation, when it was not fitting for it. What was fitting then was to carry out what they had been commanded at that time: tawhid (affirming the oneness of God), the prayer, zakah, and the like. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But if they had done what they were admonished with, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness﴾. When they migrated to Madinah and Islam became strong, fighting was prescribed for them at its appropriate time. Then a group of those who had been hastening to fight before that time, out of fear of the people, weakness, and faintheartedness, said: ﴿Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾ In this there is their impatience and their objection against Allah. What was due from them was the opposite of this state: submission to the command of Allah and patience with His orders. They reversed the required matter and said: ﴿Why did You not delay us to a near term?﴾ That is, "Why did You not postpone the obligation of fighting to a period later than the present time?" This state often afflicts one who is not steady and hastens into matters before their time. He generally does not endure them when they arrive, nor does he bear their burden, but remains of little patience.

Then Allah admonished them concerning this state of holding back from fighting, saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. That is, the enjoyment of the pleasures and comforts of this world is little. Bearing burdens in obedience to Allah for a short period is therefore easy for souls and light upon them, for when they know that the hardship they endure will not last long, it becomes easy for them. How much more so when they weigh this world against the Hereafter, and see that the Hereafter is better than it in its essence, its pleasures, and its duration. As for its essence, the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in the authentic hadith: "The place of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it." As for its pleasures, they are pure, free from troubles. Indeed, every pleasure that comes to mind or occurs to thought is surpassed by the pleasure of Paradise, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾. And Allah said through His Prophet: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

As for the pleasures of this world, they are mixed with various kinds of disturbance. If one compared its pleasures with the pains, worries, and griefs that accompany them, there would be no comparison between them in any respect. As for their duration, this world is transient, and the lifespan of a person in relation to this world is a very brief thing, whereas the Hereafter is everlasting in its bliss, and its people abide in it forever. So when the intelligent person reflects upon these two abodes and grasps their reality as it should be grasped, he will know what is most worthy of preference, of striving for, and of exertion in seeking. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. That is, those who guard against shirk and all the forbidden things. ﴿And you will not be wronged even as much as the thread of a date-stone﴾. That is, your striving for the Hereafter you will find complete and abundant, not diminished in any way.

{78} Then He informed that caution does not avail against decree, and that sitting at home does not repel anything from one who sits, saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾. That is, at whatever time and in whatever place. ﴿Even if you should be within towers well constructed﴾. That is, within impregnable fortresses and lofty residences. All of this is an incitement to jihad in the way of Allah: sometimes by encouraging through its virtue and reward, sometimes by warning of the punishment for abandoning it, sometimes by informing that sitting at home does not benefit those who sit, and sometimes by facilitating the path to it and shortening it.

Then He said: ﴿And if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; but if evil strikes them, they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [the matter] with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself. And We have sent you to the mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness.﴾

{78} He, exalted is He, informs about those who do not know, who turn away from what the messengers brought and oppose them, that when good comes to them, that is, fertility, abundance of wealth, plenty of children, and health, they say: ﴿This is from Allah﴾. And if evil befalls them, that is, drought, poverty, sickness, the death of children and loved ones, they say: ﴿This is from you﴾, that is, "because of what you have brought us, O Muhammad!" They regarded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a bad omen, just as their likes regarded the messengers of Allah as a bad omen. As Allah informed about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿When good came to them, they said, "This is ours"; but if evil struck them, they ascribed it as ill omen to Moses and those with him﴾. The people of Salih said: ﴿We consider you and those with you as a bad omen﴾. The people of Ya-Sin said to their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you...﴾, the verse. So when their hearts resembled one another in disbelief, their statements and actions resembled one another. Likewise, whoever attributes the occurrence of evil or the loss of good to what the messengers brought, or to part of it, falls within this grave condemnation. Allah answered them: ﴿Say, "All"﴾, that is, of the good and evil, the benefit and the harm, ﴿is from Allah﴾, that is, by His decree, His destiny, and His creation. ﴿So what is [the matter] with these people﴾, that is, those from whom this false statement issued, ﴿that they can hardly understand any statement﴾, that is, they do not understand any statement at all, nor come close to understanding it, or they understand from it only a weak understanding. In any case, this is a condemnation and rebuke of them for their failure to understand and comprehend from Allah and from His Messenger, and that is because of their disbelief and their turning away.

Included within this is praise for the one who understands from Allah and His Messenger, and an incitement to that and to the means that help achieve it: attentiveness to their speech, reflection upon it, and following the paths that lead to it. For if they had understood from Allah, they would have known that good and evil, and good deeds and bad deeds, are all by the decree and destiny of Allah, and nothing of them escapes that, and that the messengers, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon them, are not a cause of any evil that occurs, neither they themselves nor what they brought, for they were sent with the interests of this world, the Hereafter, and religion.

{79} Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever good reaches you﴾, that is, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from Allah﴾: it is He who bestows it and facilitates it by facilitating its causes. ﴿And whatever evil reaches you﴾, in religion and worldly life, ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of your sins and your earnings, and what Allah pardons is more numerous. Then He informed about the universality of the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness﴾, that you are truly the Messenger of Allah, by what He supported you with through His help, the manifest miracles, and the clear proofs. These are the greatest testimony absolutely, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you."﴾ When one knows that Allah, exalted is He, is perfect in knowledge, complete in power, and great in wisdom, and that He has supported His Messenger with what He supported him with and granted him a great victory, he will be certain thereby that he is the Messenger of Allah. Otherwise, had he fabricated some of the sayings attributed to Him, He would have seized him by the right hand and then severed his aorta.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 80–81:

{80} That is: whoever obeys the Messenger of Allah in his commands and prohibitions, then he has obeyed Allah (تعالى), because he does not command or forbid except by the command of Allah, His law, His revelation and His sending down. In this is the infallibility (ʿiṣmah) of the Messenger (ﷺ), for Allah commanded obedience to him absolutely. Had he not been infallible in everything he conveys from Allah, He would not have commanded obedience to him absolutely and praised [those who obey him] for that. This is among the shared rights, for rights are of three kinds: a right of Allah (تعالى) that belongs to no one of creation, which is the worship of Allah, turning to Him, and what follows from that; a category specific to the Messenger, which is ta'zir (honouring and supporting), tawqir (reverence) and nusrah (support); and a shared category, which is faith in Allah and His Messenger, loving them, and obeying them. Allah combined these rights in His saying: ﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and honour him and revere him, and glorify Him morning and evening﴾. So whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah, and he has the reward and good that is ordained for obedience to Allah. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾: from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, for he harms only himself and does not harm Allah in any way. ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾; that is, you are not to guard their deeds and states. Rather, We sent you as a conveyer (of the message), a clarifier and an advisor. You have discharged your duty, and your reward is due from Allah, whether they are guided or not, as He said (تعالى): ﴿So remind; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller...﴾ — the verse.

{81} It is necessary that obedience to Allah and His Messenger be both outward and inward, in the presence and in absence. As for one who shows obedience and commitment in the presence, but when he is alone with himself or with those of his kind, abandons obedience and turns to its opposite, then the obedience he displayed is neither beneficial nor useful. He resembles those of whom Allah said: ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾; that is, they display obedience when they are with you. ﴿But when they have gone out from you﴾; that is, they went out and were alone in a state in which they are not observed, ﴿a faction of them plans by night other than what you say﴾; that is, they plotted and devised other than your obedience, and there was nothing there but disobedience. In His saying ﴿a faction of them plans by night other than what you say﴾ is evidence that the matter upon which they settled was other than obedience, because tabyit (planning by night) is the arranging of a matter at night in a manner upon which the opinion settles. Then He threatened them for what they did, saying: ﴿And Allah records what they plan by night﴾; that is, He preserves it against them and will recompense them for it in the fullest recompense, and this is a threat to them. Then He commanded His Messenger to confront them with aversion and not to rebuke them harshly, for they cannot harm him at all when he relies upon Allah and seeks His help in supporting His religion and establishing His law. Hence He said: ﴿So turn away from them, and rely upon Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 82:

{82} He, may He be exalted, commands the contemplation of His Book, which is reflection upon its meanings, focusing the mind upon it, its beginnings and its outcomes, and what follows from these. For in contemplating the Book of Allah lies the key to (all) sciences and knowledge, through it every good is derived, all branches of knowledge are extracted from it, and through it faith increases in the heart and its tree takes firm root. It makes known the Lord who is worshipped and what He possesses of attributes of perfection and what He is exalted above of defects. It makes known the path that leads to Him, the description of its people, and what they will have upon meeting Him. It makes known the enemy who is the true enemy, the path that leads to punishment, the description of its people, and what they will have when the causes of punishment are present. And the more the servant reflects upon it, the more he increases in knowledge, action and insight. For this reason Allah commanded it, urged it, and informed us that it is the very purpose for which the Qur'an was sent down, as He, may He be exalted, said: {A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded} [Sad 38:29]; and He, may He be exalted, said: {Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?} [Muhammad 47:24].

Among the benefits of contemplating the Book of Allah is that through it the servant attains the degree of certainty and knowledge that it is the speech of Allah, because he sees that its parts confirm one another and agree with one another. You find that its wisdoms, stories and reports are repeated in the Qur'an in several places, all of them consistent and corroborating, none of them contradicting another. Thereby the perfection of the Qur'an becomes known, and that it is from Him whose knowledge encompasses all matters. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: {Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction} [An-Nisa 4:82]; that is: since it is from Allah, there is no contradiction in it at all.

This is a discipline from God to His servants regarding this improper conduct of theirs, and that when a matter of great importance or general public interest comes to them, one that concerns security and the joy of the believers, or fear that would bring calamity upon them, they should verify it and not hasten to spread that news. Rather, they should refer it to the Messenger and to those among them who are the people of ulu al-amr (ulu al-amr: those in authority), namely the people of judgment, knowledge, sincere counsel, intellect and sound composure, who know affairs and know the interests and their opposites. If they see in announcing it a benefit, an invigoration of the believers, joy for them, and precaution against their enemies, they do so; and if they see that there is no benefit in it, or that there is benefit but its harm exceeds its benefit, they do not announce it. For this reason He said: {Would have known it those among them who draw it out}; that is, they extract it by their thinking, their sound opinions and their rightly guided knowledge.

In this there is evidence for a principle of conduct: when a matter of inquiry arises, it should be entrusted to one who is qualified for it and left to its people, and one should not put himself forward ahead of them, for that is closer to correctness and more likely to secure safety from error.

It also contains a prohibition against haste and rushing to publicize matters the moment they are heard, and a command to reflect before speaking and to consider whether it is a benefit, in which case a person proceeds with it, or not, in which case he refrains from it.

Then He, exalted is He, said: {And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy}; that is, in granting you success, discipline, and teaching you what you did not know, {you would have followed Satan, except for a few}; because man by his nature is wrongdoing and ignorant, so his self commands him only to evil. When he turns to his Lord, holds fast to Him, and strives in that, his Lord shows him kindness, grants him success in every good, and protects him from the accursed Satan.

{84} This is the best state of a servant: that he strives within himself to obey Allah's command, including jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) and other things, and that he urges others to do the same. Sometimes both of these, or one of them, is lacking in the servant. For this reason, [Allah] said to His Messenger: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself﴾. That is, you have no power over anyone other than yourself, so you will not be held responsible for the actions of others. ﴿And urge the believers﴾ to fight. This includes everything that stirs the energy of the believers and strengthens their hearts: encouraging them, informing them of the weakness and failure of the enemies, and of the reward Allah has prepared for those who fight and the punishment for those who stay behind. All of this, and things like it, fall under urging others to fight. ﴿Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾; that is, through your fighting in the way of Allah and your urging one another. ﴿And Allah is greater in might﴾; that is, in strength and power, ﴿and greater in punishment﴾, against the sinner in himself and as a deterrent to others. Had He willed, the Exalted would have triumphed over the disbelievers by His power and would not have left any of them remaining. But in His wisdom, He tests some of His servants by means of others, so that the market of jihad is established, and so that beneficial faith is attained: faith by choice, not faith by compulsion, and subjugation that benefits nothing.

{85} By "intercession" (shafa'ah) is meant here assistance in some matter. Whoever intercedes for another and stands with him in some matter of good, including intercession on behalf of the wronged against one who has wronged them, will have a share of that intercession according to his effort, his deed, and his benefit, and nothing is diminished from the reward of the principal party or the one who directly acts. Whoever assists another in some matter of evil will bear a portion of the sin according to what he did and what he assisted in. In this there is a great exhortation to cooperate in righteousness and piety, and a great deterrent against cooperating in sin and transgression. He confirmed this with His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Witness over all things﴾; that is, Watcher, Preserver, and Reckoner over these deeds, so He will recompense each one with what he deserves.

{86} At-tahiyya (greeting): it is the utterance issued by one of two people meeting, in a manner of honour and supplication, together with whatever accompanies that utterance of cheerfulness and the like. The highest kinds of greeting are those prescribed by the Shari'a, namely salam (peace), both by initiating it and by returning it. So God, exalted is He, commanded the believers that when they are greeted with any greeting whatsoever, they should return it with one better than it in wording and cheerfulness, or with its equal in that. The implied meaning of this is a prohibition against not returning it at all, or returning it with something less than it. From the noble verse, the encouragement to initiate salam and greeting is derived in two ways:

The first: God commanded returning it with something better or its equal, and this necessitates that greeting is legally desired (mathlub shar'an).

The second: what is derived from the comparative form af'al (more/most), namely "ahsan" (better), which indicates the sharing of the greeting and its return in goodness, as is the original principle in this.

Excepted from the general scope of the noble verse is one who greets someone in a state in which he is not to be greeted, such as someone occupied with recitation, or listening to a khutba, or a worshipper, and the like; for the answering of his greeting is not required. Likewise excepted from this is one whom the Lawgiver has commanded to be shunned and not greeted, namely the disobedient who has not repented, and who is deterred by shunning; he is shunned, is not greeted, and his greeting is not returned. This is because of the conflict with the greater benefit. Included in the returning of greeting is every greeting that people are accustomed to, provided it is not forbidden by the Shari'a, for he is commanded to return it or something better than it. Then God, exalted is He, threatened and warned concerning the doing of good deeds and bad deeds by His saying: {Indeed, God is ever Account-Taker over all things} (﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا﴾): He keeps account of the deeds of the servants, the good and the bad of them, the small and the great of them, and then He recompenses them according to what His bounty, His justice and His praiseworthy wisdom require.

{87} He, may He be exalted, informs of His singularity in divinity, and that there is no one worthy of worship and no one deserving to be taken as God except Him, because of His perfection in His essence and attributes, and because He alone is the One who creates, governs, and bestows blessings, both apparent and hidden. This necessarily entails the command to worship Him and to draw near to Him with all kinds of worship, since He alone deserves that, and since He is the one who recompenses His servants according to what they have performed of His worship or neglected of it. For this reason He swore an oath to the occurrence of the place of recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection, and said: ﴿He will surely gather you﴾; that is, your first and last, into one assembly, on ﴿the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾; that is, there is no doubt or uncertainty in it in any respect, neither by rational proof nor by revealed proof.

As for the rational proof, it is what we observe of the revival of the earth after its death, and of the existence of the first creation, the recurrence of which is more readily possible than the first, and of the wisdom which affirms with certainty that God did not create His creatures in vain, living and then dying.

As for the revealed proof, it is the report of the Most Truthful of the truthful about it, indeed His swearing an oath to it. For this reason He said: ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than God?﴾ Likewise He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to swear to it in more than one place in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for God.﴾

And in His saying: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than God?﴾ and ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than God?﴾ there is an announcement that His speech, His reports, and His sayings are at the highest level of truthfulness, indeed the highest of all. Therefore, whatever is said regarding beliefs, sciences, and deeds that contradicts what God has reported is false, because it contradicts the certain true report; so it cannot be true.

The hypocrites mentioned in these verses are those who outwardly display Islam but did not emigrate and remain in their disbelief. Among the Companions, may God be pleased with them, there was confusion about them. Some were reluctant to fight them and to cut off their alliance because of the faith they outwardly displayed. Others knew their state from the evidence of their actions and ruled that they were disbelievers. God informed them that they should not be uncertain about them or doubt them. Rather, their situation is clear and not ambiguous: they are hypocrites, whose disbelief is well established, and who, in addition, wish that you would disbelieve as they have and be like them. So when you have verified this about them, ﴿Do not take from among them allies﴾. This requires not loving them, since alliance is a branch of love. It also requires hating them and being hostile to them, because a prohibition of something is a command to its opposite. This command is limited to their emigration. If they emigrate, the same rulings that apply to the Muslims apply to them, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) applied the rulings of Islam to everyone who was with him and emigrated to him, whether they were truly believers or only outwardly believers. If they do not emigrate and turn away, then ﴿seize them and kill them wherever you find them﴾, meaning at any time and in any place. This is among the evidences showing the abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) of fighting during the sacred months, as is the view of the majority of scholars. Those who dispute this say that these are unrestricted texts, to be understood as restricting the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months.

Then God excepted three groups from the fighting against these hypocrites.

Two groups He commanded to be left alone and made this binding:
The first: those who reach a people between whom and the Muslims there is a covenant and pact not to fight, and who then join them. Such a person has their ruling regarding the protection of blood and property.
The second group: people ﴿whose hearts are constrained from fighting you or fighting their own people﴾, meaning they remain unwilling to fight you and unwilling to fight their own people, and they prefer to avoid fighting both parties. God also commanded that these be left alone and mentioned the wisdom in this in His words: ﴿Had God willed, He would have given them power over you, so they would have fought you﴾. The possible situations are of three kinds: either they would be with you and fight your enemies, which is impossible for these people, or the matter lies between fighting you alongside their own people, and not fighting either party. The latter is the easier of the two for you. God is capable of giving them power over you, so accept the well-being and praise your Lord who restrained their hands from you while they were able to do so. {92} This form is one of the expressions of prohibition: it is impossible and inconceivable that a believer should kill a believer, i.e., deliberately.

This statement conveys the severity of its prohibition and that it is utterly incompatible with faith. Such an act only proceeds either from a disbeliever or from a grave sinner (fasiq) whose faith has become gravely deficient, and for whom something greater than that is to be feared. For true faith prevents the believer from killing his brother, with whom God has established the bond of faith-based brotherhood, whose requirements include loving him, supporting him, and removing any harm that befalls him. And what harm is greater than killing? This is confirmed by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not revert to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks." Thus it is known that killing is a practical form of disbelief, and it is the greatest of the major sins after associating partners with God.

Since the words "And it is not for a believer to kill a believer" are a general expression covering all circumstances, and it is not conceivable that he kill his brother in any manner whatsoever, God, exalted is He, made an exception for killing by mistake, saying: "except by error." The one who errs and does not intend to kill is neither sinful nor audacious toward the sanctities of God. However, since he has committed a grievous act, whose very form is sufficient for its ugliness even if he did not intend it, God commanded expiation and blood-money, saying: "And whoever kills a believer by mistake..." whether the killer is male or female, free or slave, young or old, sane or insane, Muslim or disbeliever, as the word "whoever" (man), which denotes generality, indicates. This is one of the secrets of using "man" in this place: the context of the speech would normally require "if he kills," but this wording does not encompass what "man" encompasses. Likewise, whether the one killed is male or female, young or old, as the indefiniteness in the conditional context indicates. The killer must free "a believing slave" as expiation for that, to be paid from his property. This includes the young and the old, the male and the female, the sound and the defective, according to the view of some scholars. However, wisdom requires that the freeing of a defective slave not suffice for expiation, because the purpose of manumission is to benefit the freed person, and if he would be harmed by being freed, and remaining in servitude is more beneficial to him, then his manumission does not suffice. Moreover, the phrase "freeing a slave" itself indicates this, for liberation is the release of one whose benefits are owed to another so that they become his own; if there are no benefits in him, the notion of liberation cannot be conceived. So reflect on this, for it is clear.

As for blood-money, it is obligatory upon the paternal kin (aqilah) of the killer in cases of error and quasi-deliberate killing. "Handed over to his family": as a consolation to their hearts. By "his family" here is meant his heirs, for heirs inherit what the deceased leaves, so the blood-money is included in what he left. The details of blood-money are numerous and are mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. His saying: "unless they forgo it" means that the heirs of the slain forgo the blood-money by way of pardon, whereupon it falls away. This encourages them to pardon, because God called it charity (sadaqah), and charity is desirable at all times. "But if he was from a people hostile to you," i.e., from warring disbelievers, "and he was a believer, then a believing slave shall be freed," i.e., there is no blood-money owed to his family upon you, due to their lack of sanctity in respect of their blood and property. "But if he was from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then blood-money handed over to his family and the freeing of a believing slave," and this is because of the sanctity of his family by virtue of the treaty and covenant they have. "Whoever cannot find" a slave or the price of one, i.e., he is unable to afford it, having nothing beyond his basic needs and necessities sufficient to purchase a slave, "then fasting two consecutive months," i.e., he must not break the fast between them without an excuse. If he breaks it due to an excuse, the excuse does not interrupt the consecutiveness, such as illness, menstruation and the like; but if he breaks it without an excuse, the succession is broken and he must begin the fast anew. "A repentance from God," i.e., these expiations which God has made obligatory upon the killer are a repentance from God toward His servants, a mercy to them, and an expiation for whatever shortcoming or lack of caution may occur from them, as commonly happens with one who kills by mistake. "And God is ever Knowing, Wise," i.e., of perfect knowledge and perfect wisdom, nothing escapes Him, not an atom's weight on earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller or greater than that, at any time and in any place, and nothing in His creation or legislation departs from His wisdom; rather, everything He has created and legislated contains the utmost wisdom.

And of His knowledge and wisdom is that He made obligatory upon the killer an expiation suited to what he committed, for he caused the destruction of a sanctified soul and brought it from existence to non-existence. It is fitting that he free a slave and bring him out from the bondage of servitude to creatures into complete freedom. If he cannot find such a slave, he fasts two consecutive months, thereby removing himself from the bondage of desires and sensual pleasures, which cut the servant off from his eternal happiness, to worship God, exalted is He, by abandoning them seeking nearness to God. He, exalted is He, extended this period with its great number of days and the obligation of consecutiveness. Feeding the poor was not prescribed in these instances for lack of suitability, unlike in the case of zihar, as will come, God willing. And of His wisdom is that He made blood-money obligatory for killing, even if by mistake, so that it may serve as a deterrent and a restraint against much killing, by employing the means that preserve against it. And of His wisdom is that it was made obligatory upon the paternal kin in cases of accidental killing by the consensus of the scholars, because the killer has not committed a sin, and it would be burdensome for him to bear this crushing blood-money; so it is fitting that those between whom and him there is assistance, support and help in securing benefits and warding off harms should bear it. Perhaps this is among the reasons they prevent those who are bound to pay on their behalf from killing, out of fear of burdening them; and it is lightened for them by distributing it among them according to their circumstances and capacity. It was also lightened by deferring it for them over three years. And of His wisdom and knowledge is that He consoles the family of the slain for their calamity through the blood-money He made obligatory upon the guardians of the killer.

{93} It was previously stated that God informed us that the killing of a believer by a believer does not occur, and that killing is a practical form of disbelief. Here He mentions the threat against one who kills intentionally, a threat that makes hearts tremble, breaks open hearts, and disturbs people of intellect. Nothing is mentioned among the types of major sins that is greater than this threat, nor even like it, namely the report that his recompense is Jahannam (Hell). That is: this great sin alone is sufficient to requite its doer with Jahannam, with its great punishment, its humiliating disgrace, the wrath of the Compeller, the loss of success and salvation, and the arrival of ruin and loss. So we seek refuge in Allah from every cause that distances one from His mercy.

This threat has the same ruling as similar texts of warning concerning some major sins and disobedience, stating abiding in the Fire or deprivation of Paradise. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed in interpreting them, while they agreed on the invalidity of the view of the Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah, who hold that such people abide in the Fire even if they are monotheists. The correct interpretation of them is what the verifying Imam Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in "al-Madarij." For after mentioning the interpretations of the scholars on this and criticizing them, he said:

"A group said: these texts and similar ones, in which the cause requiring punishment is mentioned, do not necessitate that the ruling exists merely because its cause exists. The ruling is only completed by the existence of its requirement and the absence of its impediments. The utmost these texts do is inform that such-and-such is a cause of punishment and requires it. The evidence has established the impediments: some by consensus and some by textual proof. Repentance is an impediment by consensus, monotheism is an impediment by the mass-transmitted texts that cannot be repelled, great good deeds that efface sins are an impediment, great calamities that expiate sins are an impediment, and the enforcement of prescribed punishments (hudud) in this world is an impediment by explicit text. There is no way to nullify these texts, so the texts must be applied from both sides. From here arose the weighing between good deeds and bad deeds, taking into account the requirement of punishment and its impediment, and applying whichever is weightier. They said: upon this is built the welfare and harms of both abodes, and upon this are built the legal rulings (shar'i) and the decreed rulings (qadari). This is the requirement of the wisdom that pervades existence, and by it the connection of causes and their effects is established, both in creation and in command. Allah has made for every opposite an opposite that repels and resists it, and the ruling belongs to the stronger of the two. Strength requires health, while wellness, corruption of humors and their rebellion are impediments to the working of nature; the action of strength and the ruling belong to the dominant of the two. Likewise the powers of medicines and diseases. The servant may have in him a requirement for health and a requirement for ruin, and each prevents the other's full effect and resists it. When one prevails over the other and subdues it, the effect is his. From here it is known that people are divided into those who enter Paradise and do not enter the Fire, and the reverse, and those who enter the Fire and then leave it, their stay in it being according to what is in them of the requirement of remaining, in speed or slowness of leaving. And whoever has an illuminated insight sees by it everything Allah has reported in His Book concerning the Return and its details, until it is as if he witnesses it with his own eyes, and he knows that this is the requirement of His divinity, lordship, might and wisdom, and that the opposite is impossible for Him, and attributing that to Him is attributing to Him what is not fitting. Thus the attribution of that to his insight is like the attribution of the sun and stars to his sight. This is the certainty of faith, which burns sins as fire burns firewood. The possessor of this station of faith cannot persist in sins, even if they occur from him and are many, for the light of faith he has commands him to renew repentance at every moment, returning to Allah with every breath. This is among the most beloved of creatures to Allah." End of his words; may Allah sanctify his soul and reward him on behalf of Islam and the Muslims with goodness.

{94} Almighty God commands His believing servants, when they go out to fight in His cause and seeking His good pleasure, to clarify and verify all their matters that are unclear. For matters are of two kinds: clear and unclear. Clear, evident matters do not need verification and clarification, for that would be obtaining what is already obtained. As for unclear, ambiguous matters, a person needs to verify and clarify them, so that he knows whether or not to proceed with them. For verification in these matters brings many benefits and averts great evils, through which the servant's religion, intellect, and steadiness are known. This is in contrast to one who hastens into matters at their outset before their ruling has become clear to him, for that leads to what is not appropriate, as happened to those whom God rebuked in the verse, when they did not verify and killed the one who greeted them with peace, who had with him a small herd of sheep or someone else's property, thinking that by this he sought protection from being killed. This was in fact an error. Therefore He rebuked them, saying: {Do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of the worldly life, for with God are abundant gains}; that is: let not the fleeting, small worldly gain drive you to commit what is not appropriate, so that you lose what is with God of abundant, lasting reward, for what is with God is better and more enduring. In this there is an indication that when a servant sees his own desires inclining toward a state in which he has a passion and which is harmful to him, he should remind himself of what God has prepared for those who restrain their souls from their desires and prefer the good pleasure of God over the pleasure of their own souls, for in that there is an encouragement for the soul to comply with God's command, even if it is hard for it.

Then God said, reminding them of their former state before they were guided to Islam: {Thus you were before, and then God bestowed His favor upon you}; that is: just as He guided you after your misguidance, so He guides others. And just as guidance came to you little by little, so it is with others. Looking at the perfect person's former, deficient state, and dealing with those who are in a similar state according to what one knows of his former condition, and calling him with wisdom and good admonition, is among the greatest causes of benefit to him and his benefiting. For this reason He repeated the command to clarify, saying: {so verify}. If one who went out to fight in the cause of God, to strive against the enemies of God, and prepared himself with every kind of preparation to strike them, is commanded to clarify regarding the one who offered him peace, and the indication was strong that he had greeted only to seek refuge from being killed and out of fear for himself, then this indicates the command to clarify and verify in all situations in which some kind of ambiguity occurs, so that the servant verifies them until the matter becomes clear to him and right guidance and correctness become evident. {Indeed, God is ever Acquainted with what you do}: He will recompense each one for what he did and intended, according to what He knows of the conditions and intentions of His servants.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 95–96:

{95–96} That is: those believers who strive (jahada) with their selves and their wealth are not equal to those who do not go out for jihad and do not fight the enemies of Allah. This contains an exhortation to go out for jihad, an encouragement toward it, and a warning against laziness and sitting back from it without an excuse. As for those with a valid excuse, such as the sick, the blind, the lame, and one who does not find what he needs to equip himself, they are not in the same position as those who sit back without excuse. Whoever among the people of excuse is content with his sitting back, not intending to go out in the way of Allah were it not for the presence of the obstacle, and does not even speak to himself about it, he is in the position of one who sits back without excuse. But whoever is resolved to go out in the way of Allah were it not for the presence of the obstacle, wishes for it and speaks to himself about it, he is in the position of one who went out for jihad, because when a firm intention is accompanied by what is within its capacity of speech or action, its owner is placed in the position of the doer.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explicitly stated the preference of the strivers over the sitting-back ones in rank (darajah), that is, in elevation. This is a preference in general terms, and then He stated it in detail. He promised them forgiveness from their Lord and mercy, which includes the attainment of every good and the averting of every evil, and the ranks which the Prophet (ﷺ) explained in the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred ranks, between each two ranks is as the distance between the heaven and the earth, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way."

This reward which Allah has ordained for jihad is similar to what is in Surah al-Saff in His saying: {O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [You should] believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you should know. He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment} ... to the end of the surah.

Reflect on the excellence of this transition from one state to what is higher than it. He first negated equality between the striver and others, then explicitly stated the striver's preference over the sitting-back one by a rank, then moved on to his preference by forgiveness, mercy, and ranks. This transition from a state to what is higher than it, when praising and preferring, or descending from a state to what is below it, when blaming and censuring, is better in expression and more striking to the soul. Likewise, when Allah prefers one thing over another while each of them has some merit, he guards against misunderstanding by mentioning the merit that encompasses both, lest anyone imagine a disparagement of the one preferred over. As He said here: {And to each Allah has promised the best}, and as He said in the verses mentioned in al-Saff in His saying: {And give good tidings to the believers}, and as in His saying: {Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought}; that is, [they are not equal] to those who were not like that. Then He said: {And to each Allah has promised the best}, and as He said: {So We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge}. Whoever examines preference among persons, groups, and deeds should be alert to this subtle point. Likewise, if one speaks in censure of persons or doctrines, he should mention what they share when preferring one of them over another, lest it be imagined that the one preferred has attained perfection. For example, if it is said: "The Christians are better than the Magians," he should add: "and each of them is a disbeliever." And: "Killing is more heinous than fornication, and each of them is a major sin, which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden and warned against."

When He promised the strivers forgiveness and mercy, which proceed from His two noble names, the Most Forgiving (al-Ghafur) and the Most Merciful (al-Rahim), He concluded this verse with them, saying: {And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful}.
