{95–96} That is: those believers who strive (jahada) with their selves and their wealth are not equal to those who do not go out for jihad and do not fight the enemies of Allah. This contains an exhortation to go out for jihad, an encouragement toward it, and a warning against laziness and sitting back from it without an excuse. As for those with a valid excuse, such as the sick, the blind, the lame, and one who does not find what he needs to equip himself, they are not in the same position as those who sit back without excuse. Whoever among the people of excuse is content with his sitting back, not intending to go out in the way of Allah were it not for the presence of the obstacle, and does not even speak to himself about it, he is in the position of one who sits back without excuse. But whoever is resolved to go out in the way of Allah were it not for the presence of the obstacle, wishes for it and speaks to himself about it, he is in the position of one who went out for jihad, because when a firm intention is accompanied by what is within its capacity of speech or action, its owner is placed in the position of the doer.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explicitly stated the preference of the strivers over the sitting-back ones in rank (darajah), that is, in elevation. This is a preference in general terms, and then He stated it in detail. He promised them forgiveness from their Lord and mercy, which includes the attainment of every good and the averting of every evil, and the ranks which the Prophet (ﷺ) explained in the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred ranks, between each two ranks is as the distance between the heaven and the earth, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way."

This reward which Allah has ordained for jihad is similar to what is in Surah al-Saff in His saying: {O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [You should] believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you should know. He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment} ... to the end of the surah.

Reflect on the excellence of this transition from one state to what is higher than it. He first negated equality between the striver and others, then explicitly stated the striver's preference over the sitting-back one by a rank, then moved on to his preference by forgiveness, mercy, and ranks. This transition from a state to what is higher than it, when praising and preferring, or descending from a state to what is below it, when blaming and censuring, is better in expression and more striking to the soul. Likewise, when Allah prefers one thing over another while each of them has some merit, he guards against misunderstanding by mentioning the merit that encompasses both, lest anyone imagine a disparagement of the one preferred over. As He said here: {And to each Allah has promised the best}, and as He said in the verses mentioned in al-Saff in His saying: {And give good tidings to the believers}, and as in His saying: {Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought}; that is, [they are not equal] to those who were not like that. Then He said: {And to each Allah has promised the best}, and as He said: {So We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge}. Whoever examines preference among persons, groups, and deeds should be alert to this subtle point. Likewise, if one speaks in censure of persons or doctrines, he should mention what they share when preferring one of them over another, lest it be imagined that the one preferred has attained perfection. For example, if it is said: "The Christians are better than the Magians," he should add: "and each of them is a disbeliever." And: "Killing is more heinous than fornication, and each of them is a major sin, which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden and warned against."

When He promised the strivers forgiveness and mercy, which proceed from His two noble names, the Most Forgiving (al-Ghafur) and the Most Merciful (al-Rahim), He concluded this verse with them, saying: {And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 97–99:

{97} This is a severe warning for one who abandons emigration (hijrah) while being able to undertake it, until he dies. The angels who take his soul rebuke him with this great rebuke, and they say to them: {In what state were you?} That is: in what condition were you? And by what were you distinguished from the polytheists? Rather, you increased their numbers, and perhaps you supported them against the believers, and you missed much good, the struggle (jihad) alongside His Messenger, being with the Muslims, and aiding them against their enemies. {They said, "We were oppressed in the land."} That is: we were weak, subdued, and wronged, having no ability to emigrate. But they were not truthful in this, because God rebuked them and threatened them, and God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. He excepted the truly oppressed, and for this reason the angels said to them: {Was not the earth of God spacious, so that you might have emigrated therein?} This is a rhetorical question affirming a fact; that is: it is established for everyone that the earth of God is spacious. Wherever the servant is in a place where he cannot manifest his religion, he has a wide expanse of earth in which he can worship God, as God, the Exalted, said: {O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.} God said about these people, who have no excuse: {Their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination.} As mentioned before, this verse mentions the stated cause; its result may follow when its conditions are met and its impediments are absent, though an impediment may prevent it.

The verse indicates that emigration is among the greatest obligations, and abandoning it is among the prohibited acts, indeed among the greatest major sins. The verse also indicates that everyone who dies has fully completed what was decreed for him of provision, term, and deeds; this is derived from the word "tawaffi" (taking in full), for it indicates this, since if anything of that remained for him, he would not have been "tawaffa" (fully taken). It also contains belief in the angels and praise of them, since God brought that address to them in the form of affirmation and approval from them, and His agreement with its place.

{98–99} Then He excepted the truly oppressed, who have no ability to emigrate in any way: {and they cannot find a way}. Concerning these, God said: {As for those, God may pardon them, and God is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.} And {perhaps} (ʿasā) and similar expressions are certain to occur from God, by the requirement of His generosity and kindness. In the expectation of reward for one who performs some deeds there is a benefit: that he may not fulfill them as their right is due, nor perform them in the proper manner that is fitting, but rather be deficient, and so does not deserve that reward. And God knows best.

The noble verse indicates that one who is unable to do what is commanded, whether obligatory or otherwise, is excused, as God said regarding those unable to fight: {No blame is upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick.} He said regarding the general commands: {So fear God as much as you are able.} The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If I command you with something, then do of it what you are able." However, a person is not excused unless he exerts his utmost effort and all avenues of stratagem are closed to him, based on His saying: {They are not able to devise a plan.}

The verse also draws attention to the fact that the means of transport (dalil) for the Hajj and 'Umrah, and similar things that require travel, are among the conditions of capability (istita'ah).

This passage concerns encouraging emigration (hijrah) and making it appealing, and explaining the benefits it contains. The One who is true to His promise promised that whoever emigrates in His cause, seeking His pleasure, will find in the earth "muraghaman" (a place of refuge and opposition to the enemies of the faith) and "sa'ah" (abundance). The muraghamah encompasses the benefits of the religion, and the sa'ah encompasses the benefits of this world. This is because many people imagine that emigration brings dispersal after closeness, poverty after wealth, humiliation after honor, and hardship after ease, but the matter is not so. For the believer, as long as he remains among the polytheists, his religion is in a state of extreme deficiency: not in the acts of worship that are confined to himself, such as prayer and the like, nor in the acts of worship that extend to others, such as jihad by word and deed and what follows from it, because he is unable to do these. He is also at risk of being turned away from his religion, especially if he is weak. But when he emigrates in the cause of God, he becomes able to establish the religion of God and to wage jihad against the enemies of God and to oppose them, for "muraghamah" is a comprehensive term for everything by which the enemies of God are enraged, whether by word or deed. Likewise, he gains abundance in his provision, and this has happened just as God, exalted is He, informed.

Consider this with regard to the Companions, may God be pleased with them: when they emigrated in the cause of God and left their homes, children and wealth for God's sake, their faith was perfected by this, and they attained complete faith, great jihad and victory for the religion of God, such that they became leaders for those after them. Likewise, they obtained, as a consequence of this, conquests and spoils, such that they became the richest of people. And so every one who does as they did obtains what they obtained until the Day of Resurrection.

Then He said: {And whoever leaves his house emigrating to God and His Messenger}; that is, intending his Lord, His pleasure, His love for His Messenger, and support for the religion of God, and not any other aim. {Then death overtakes him}: by killing or otherwise, {his reward has become due from God}; that is, he has attained the reward of the emigrant who reached his intended goal, by the guarantee of God, exalted is He. This is because he intended, resolved, and began and commenced the action. It is of God's mercy toward him and those like him that He gave them their full reward even if they did not complete the action, and forgave them whatever shortcoming occurred from them in emigration and otherwise. For this reason He concluded this verse with these two noble names, saying: {And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful}: He forgives the believers the sins they have committed, especially those who repent and turn back to their Lord; Merciful toward all creation with a mercy by which He brought them into existence, kept them healthy, and provided them with wealth, children, strength and other things; Merciful toward the believers, in that He guided them to faith, taught them knowledge by which certainty is attained, facilitated for them the means of happiness and success, and that by which they reach the utmost of gains. They will see of His mercy and generosity what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. So we ask God not to deprive us of His goodness because of the evil of what we have.

{101} These two verses are the foundation for the concession of shortening (qasr) and the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). He, exalted is He, says: {And when you travel through the land}; i.e., on a journey. The apparent meaning of the verse implies permission to shorten the prayer on any journey whatsoever, even a journey of disobedience; this is the position of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. The majority (al-jumhur), namely the three Imams and others, disagreed with this, and did not permit the concession on a journey of disobedience, specifying the verse by its meaning and context (takhsis); for the concession is an ease from Allah to His servants when they travel, that they may shorten and break their fast, and the one who travels in disobedience is not suited to the lightening of his condition.

And His saying: {there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer}; i.e., there is no sin or wrongdoing upon you in that. This does not contradict that shortening is the better course, because the negation of blame removes some of the doubt that arises in many souls. Nor does it contradict obligation, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Baqara in His saying: {Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of Allah...} to the end of the verse. The removal of doubt in this place is evident, because the prayer is established among the Muslims as obligatory in its complete form, and this will not remove from the souls of most of them except by mentioning what contradicts it. And two matters indicate that shortening is better than completing: First: the constant practice of the Prophet (ﷺ) of shortening on all his journeys. Second: that this falls under the category of ease, concession and mercy towards the servants, and Allah, exalted is He, loves that His concessions be accepted, just as He dislikes that His disobedience be committed.

And His saying: {that you shorten from the prayer}, and He did not say: "that you shorten the prayer." In this there are two benefits. The first: had He said "that you shorten the prayer," shortening would not be restricted by any limit, and one might think that if he shortened most of the prayer and made it a single rak'a, it would suffice. So His saying {from the prayer} indicates that shortening is bounded, defined, and referred back to what is established from the practice of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. The second: that {min} (from) indicates partiality (tab'id), so that it is known that shortening applies to some of the obligatory prayers, not all of them; for the Fajr and Maghrib prayers are not shortened, and what is shortened is the four-rak'a prayer, from four to two rak'as.

Having established that shortening during travel is a concession, know that the exegetes have differed regarding this condition, namely His saying: {if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you}, whose apparent meaning indicates that shortening is not permitted except with both conditions together: travel with fear. The essence of their disagreement returns to whether what is meant by His saying {that you shorten} is the shortening of the number only, or the shortening of the number and the form. The difficulty arises only on the first view. This matter was difficult for the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, until he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about it, saying: "O Messenger of Allah! Why do we shorten the prayer when we are secure?" meaning: and Allah says {if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you}. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is a charity which Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity." Or as he said. Accordingly, this condition was mentioned in view of the usual circumstance in which the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions were; for most of his journeys were journeys of jihad.

There is another benefit in it: it explains the wisdom and the public interest in the legislation of the concession of shortening; so this verse clarifies the greatest hardship conceivable that is suited to the concession, namely the combination of travel and fear. This does not imply that one may not shorten with travel alone, which is the source of hardship. As for the second view, that what is meant by shortening [here] is the shortening of number and form, the condition remains on its own basis: when travel and fear are both present, shortening of number and shortening of form are permitted; when travel alone is present, shortening of number only is permitted; or when fear alone is present, shortening of form only is permitted.

{102} For this reason He mentioned the description of the prayer of fear after it, with His saying: {And when you are among them and establish for them the prayer}; i.e., you lead them in prayer, establishing it and completing what is obligatory in it, and their performing what is fitting for you and them to perform. Then He explained this with His saying: {let a group of them stand with you}; i.e., and another group standing facing the enemy, as is indicated by what follows. {Then when they have prostrated}; i.e., those who are with you, meaning they have completed their prayer. He expressed the prayer by prostration to show the excellence of prostration and that it is a pillar of the prayer, indeed its greatest pillar. {Then let them go behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come forward}: these are the group who stood facing the enemy. {And let them pray with you}. This indicates that the Imam remains after the first group departs, waiting for the second group; when they arrive, he prays with them the remainder of his prayer, then sits waiting for them until they complete their prayer, and then he gives the salam with them. This is one of the forms of the prayer of fear; for it has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) in many ways, all of which are permissible.

This verse indicates that congregational prayer is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) for two reasons:
The first: Allah, exalted is He, commanded it in this severe situation, at the time of intense fear of enemies and caution against their attack; if He obligated it in this severe situation, then obligating it in a state of tranquility and security is all the more fitting and appropriate.
The second: those performing the prayer of fear leave out many conditions and requirements in it, and many actions that would nullify the prayer in other circumstances are excused in it; and this is only because of the emphasis on the obligation of congregation; for there is no contradiction between an obligation and a recommendation. Had congregation not been obligatory, these necessary matters would not have been abandoned on its account.

The noble verse also indicates that it is preferable and better that they pray behind a single Imam, even if that entails omitting something that would not be omitted if they prayed behind several imams; this is for the sake of the unity of the Muslims' word, their agreement, and the non-division of their word, and so that this is more effective in instilling awe in the hearts of their enemies.

He, exalted is He, commanded taking up arms and caution in the prayer of fear. Although this involves movement and distraction from some aspects of the prayer, there is in it a predominant benefit, namely the combination of prayer and jihad and caution against enemies who are most eager to strike the Muslims, to attack them and their belongings. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: {The disbelievers wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings, so they might attack you in one single assault}.

Then Allah excused those who have an excuse, such as illness or rain, from putting down their weapons, but with taking precaution. He said: {And there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill, but take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment}. Among the humiliating punishment is what Allah commanded His party, the believing servants and supporters of His religion, the monotheists, to do: to kill and fight them wherever they find them, to seize them, to besiege them, to lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, and to be cautious of them in all circumstances, and not to be heedless of them, lest the disbelievers attain some of their aims against them. So to Allah belongs the greatest praise and commendation for what He has bestowed upon the believers, and for supporting them with His aid and His teachings, which, had they followed them perfectly, no banner would have been defeated for them, and no enemy would have prevailed over them at any time.

His saying: {Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you}: indicates that this group completes all their prayer before going to the position of the guards, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remains waiting for the other group before the salam; because he first mentioned that the group stands with him, informing of their accompanying him, then he attributed the subsequent action to them rather than to the Messenger, and this indicates what we have mentioned.

And in His saying {Let another group who have not prayed come forward and let them pray with you}: there is evidence that the first group has prayed, and that the entire prayer of the second group is with the Imam in actuality in their first rak'a and in effect (hukman) in their last rak'a; this necessitates the Imam waiting for them until they complete their prayer, and then he gives the salam with them. This is apparent to the one who reflects.

This verse indicates that congregational prayer is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) for two reasons:
The first: Allah, exalted is He, commanded it in this severe situation, at the time of intense fear of enemies and caution against their attack; if He obligated it in this severe situation, then obligating it in a state of tranquility and security is all the more fitting and appropriate.
The second: those performing the prayer of fear leave out many conditions and requirements in it, and many actions that would nullify the prayer in other circumstances are excused in it; and this is only because of the emphasis on the obligation of congregation; for there is no contradiction between an obligation and a recommendation. Had congregation not been obligatory, these necessary matters would not have been abandoned on its account.

The noble verse also indicates that it is preferable and better that they pray behind a single Imam, even if that entails omitting something that would not be omitted if they prayed behind several imams; this is for the sake of the unity of the Muslims' word, their agreement, and the non-division of their word, and so that this is more effective in instilling awe in the hearts of their enemies.

He, exalted is He, commanded taking up arms and caution in the prayer of fear. Although this involves movement and distraction from some aspects of the prayer, there is in it a predominant benefit, namely the combination of prayer and jihad and caution against enemies who are most eager to strike the Muslims, to attack them and their belongings. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: {The disbelievers wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings, so they might attack you in one single assault}.

Then Allah excused those who have an excuse, such as illness or rain, from putting down their weapons, but with taking precaution. He said: {And there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill, but take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment}. Among the humiliating punishment is what Allah commanded His party, the believing servants and supporters of His religion, the monotheists, to do: to kill and fight them wherever they find them, to seize them, to besiege them, to lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, and to be cautious of them in all circumstances, and not to be heedless of them, lest the disbelievers attain some of their aims against them. So to Allah belongs the greatest praise and commendation for what He has bestowed upon the believers, and for supporting them with His aid and His teachings, which, had they followed them perfectly, no banner would have been defeated for them, and no enemy would have prevailed over them at any time.

His saying: {Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you}: indicates that this group completes all their prayer before going to the position of the guards, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remains waiting for the other group before the salam; because he first mentioned that the group stands with him, informing of their accompanying him, then he attributed the subsequent action to them rather than to the Messenger, and this indicates what we have mentioned.

And in His saying {Let another group who have not prayed come forward and let them pray with you}: there is evidence that the first group has prayed, and that the entire prayer of the second group is with the Imam in actuality in their first rak'a and in effect (hukman) in their last rak'a; this necessitates the Imam waiting for them until they complete their prayer, and then he gives the salam with them. This is apparent to the one who reflects.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 103:

{103} That is: when you have finished your prayer, whether the prayer of fear or other prayers, then remember Allah in all your conditions and circumstances. However, the prayer of fear was singled out for this for several benefits:

Among them: the heart's righteousness, success and happiness lie in turning (inabah) to Allah, Exalted is He, in love, and in the heart being filled with His remembrance and praise of Him. The greatest means of attaining this purpose is the prayer (salah), whose reality is that it is a connection (silah) between the servant and his Lord.

Among them: it contains, from the realities of faith and the knowledge of certainty, what necessitated that Allah make it obligatory upon His servants every day and night. It is known that in the prayer of fear these praiseworthy aims are not fully achieved, because of the preoccupation of the heart and the body and the fear, so He commanded that it be made up for (jabr) by remembrance after it.

Among them: fear necessitates a restlessness and anxiety of the heart, which is a likely cause of its weakness, and when the heart weakens, the body weakens in resisting the enemy. Remembering Allah and increasing in it are among the greatest strengtheners of the heart.

Among them: remembrance of Allah, Exalted is He, together with patience and steadfastness, is a cause of success and of victory over the enemies; as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may be successful﴾. So He commanded increasing in it in this state, along with other wisdoms.

As for His saying: ﴿And when you are secure, then establish prayer﴾; that is: when you are safe from fear and your hearts and bodies are at ease, then complete your prayer in the most perfect manner, outwardly and inwardly, with its pillars, its conditions, its humility and all its complements. ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾; that is: obligatory at its appointed time. This indicates its obligation and that it has a time which it is not valid without, and these are the times which have been established among the Muslims, young and old, scholar and ignorant, and they took this from their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) through his saying: "Pray as you have seen me praying."

His saying ﴿upon the believers﴾ indicates that prayer is the measure of faith, and according to the faith of the servant will his prayer be, complete and perfect. This also indicates that disbelievers, even if they are bound by the rulings of the Muslims such as the dhimmis, are not addressed with the branches of the religion such as prayer, nor are they commanded to it; rather, it is not valid from them as long as they remain in their disbelief, though they will be punished for it and for all the other rulings in the Hereafter.

{104} That is: do not weaken or grow lax in pursuing your enemy among the disbelievers; that is, in fighting them and standing guard (murabatah) for that purpose. For the weakness of the heart calls for the weakness of the body, and that renders one unable to resist the enemies. Rather, be strong and energetic in fighting them. Then He mentioned what strengthens the hearts of the believers, mentioning two things:

The first: what afflicts you of pain, fatigue, wounds, and the like, afflicts your enemies as well. Therefore it is not in keeping with human manliness and Islamic valor that you should be weaker than they, when you and they are equal in that which necessitates such (conditions). For the customary course of things is that one grows weak only when pains have followed one another upon him and the enemies have prevailed over him continuously, not one who is defeated at one time and gains the upper hand over his foe at another.

The second matter: you hope from God what they do not hope for. You hope for the attainment of His reward and deliverance from His punishment. Indeed, the elite among the believers have lofty aims and high hopes: the victory of God's religion, the establishment of His law, the expansion of the sphere of Islam, the guidance of those who have gone astray, and the suppression of the enemies of the religion. These matters necessitate for the sincere believer increased strength, multiplied energy, and perfect courage. For one who fights and endures in order to attain his worldly honor, if he attains it, is not like one who fights to attain worldly and otherworldly happiness and to win the good pleasure of God and His Paradise. Glorified is He who differentiates between His servants and distinguishes between them by His knowledge and wisdom. This is why He said: {And God is ever Knowing and Wise}: perfect in knowledge, perfect in wisdom.

(105) He, exalted is He, informs that He sent down to His servant and messenger the Book with truth, meaning preserved in its revelation from the devils, so that falsehood cannot reach it from them. Rather, it descended with truth and also contains truth. Its reports are true, and its commands and prohibitions are just. ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾. He also informs that He sent it down so that you might judge between the people. In another verse: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them﴾. It is possible that this verse refers to judging between people in matters of dispute and disagreement, and that verse refers to clarifying the whole religion, its roots and its branches. It is also possible that both verses have one meaning, so that judging between people here includes judging between them concerning blood, honour, property and all other rights, as well as in matters of belief and all matters of rulings. His words ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ mean: not by your own desire, but by what Allah has taught you and inspired in you, as in His saying, ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾. In this is evidence of his infallibility (ﷺ) in what he conveys from Allah of all rulings and other matters, and that a judge must have knowledge and justice, as shown by His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾, and He did not say "by what you have seen." He also made judging between people dependent on knowledge of the Book.

When Allah commanded judging between people in a way that includes justice and equity, He forbade oppression and injustice, which are the opposite of justice, saying: ﴿And do not be a pleader for the treacherous﴾. That is, do not argue on behalf of one whose treachery you know, whether he is a claimant to what is not his or a denier of a right owed by him, whether you know this or only suppose it. In this is evidence for the prohibition of disputing for falsehood, and of representing the wrongdoer in religious disputes and worldly rights. The implication of the verse permits taking on representation in a dispute for one who is not known for wrongdoing.

(106) ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what has proceeded from you, if anything did proceed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is, He forgives a great sin for whoever seeks His forgiveness and repents and turns back to Him, and He grants him success in righteous deeds afterward, which bring reward and remove punishment.

(107) ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾. Ikhtiyan (betraying) and khiyanah (betrayal) have the same meaning as wrongdoing, injustice and sin. This includes the prohibition of arguing on behalf of one who has committed a wrong and upon whom a punishment is due, whether a hadd (fixed penalty) or ta'zir (discretionary penalty). He must not be defended by denying what he did as treachery, or by averting the legal punishment that resulted from it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾. That is, one who is much given to treachery and sin. When love is negated, its opposite is established, which is hatred. This is like a reason for the prohibition mentioned earlier.

(108) Then He mentioned about these treacherous people that ﴿they conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him﴾. This is from weakness of faith and deficiency of certainty, when fear of creatures is greater in their hearts than fear of Allah. So they strive, by permissible and forbidden means, to avoid disgrace before people. Yet they have openly defied Allah with grave deeds and have not cared that He sees them and is aware of them. He is with them in knowledge in all their circumstances, especially when they plot what does not please Him in speech, such as clearing the guilty and accusing the innocent of the crime, and striving for this with the Messenger (ﷺ) so that he would do what they had plotted. They combined several crimes and did not watch over the Lord of the earth and the heavens, who knows their secrets and inner thoughts. For this reason He threatened them, saying: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what they do, Encompassing﴾. That is, He has encompassed that in knowledge. Yet He did not hasten punishment upon them. Rather He gave them respite, offered them repentance, and warned them against persisting in their sin, which brings severe punishment.

(109) ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their advocate?﴾ That is: suppose you argued on their behalf in this worldly life, and your argument averted from them some of what they feared of shame and disgrace before people; what good does that bring them or benefit them? Who will argue for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, when the proof is directed against them, and their tongues, hands and feet testify against them for what they used to do? On that Day Allah will pay them their true due, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth. So who will argue for them, when He knows the secret and what is more hidden, and who will set up witnesses against them against which denial is impossible?

This verse contains guidance to compare what is supposed to be worldly benefit resulting from abandoning Allah's commands or committing His prohibitions, with what is lost of the reward of the Hereafter or what is gained of its punishments. So let the one whose soul urges him to abandon a command of Allah say: "You have abandoned His command out of laziness and negligence. What benefit have you gained? What reward of the Hereafter have you lost? What misery, deprivation, failure and loss has resulted from this abandonment?" Likewise, when his soul calls him to what it desires of forbidden appetites, let him say to it: "Suppose you do what you desire. Its pleasure will pass, and it will be followed by worries, griefs, regrets, the loss of reward and the attainment of punishment, a part of which is enough for the intelligent person to refrain from it." This is among the greatest things that benefit a servant to reflect upon, and it is the distinctive mark of true intellect, unlike one who claims intellect and is not so. Due to his ignorance and wrongdoing, such a person prefers present pleasure and immediate ease, even if consequences follow. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

(110) Then Exalted is He said: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: whoever dares to commit sins and plunges into sin, then seeks Allah's forgiveness with complete seeking, which entails acknowledging the sin, regretting it, ceasing from it, and resolving never to return to it. The One who never breaks His promise has promised such a person forgiveness and mercy. He will forgive him the sin that proceeded from him, remove the deficiency and blemish that resulted from it, restore to him the righteous deeds he had performed earlier, and grant him success in what remains of his life. He will not let his sin become a barrier to his success, because He has forgiven him, and when He forgives, He forgives what follows from it.

Know that the phrase "doing evil" (su') when used without qualification includes all sins, minor and major. It is called su' because it harms its doer by its punishment, and because it is in itself bad and not good. Likewise, "wronging oneself" (zulm al-nafs), when used without qualification, includes wronging it by association with Allah and whatever is less than that. But when one of them is joined with the other, each may be explained according to what suits it. So "doing evil" here is explained as the injustice that harms people, namely wronging them in their lives, property and honour. And "wronging oneself" is explained as the wrongs and sins between Allah and His servant. Wronging oneself is called wrongdoing because the servant's soul is not his own possession to dispose of as he wishes. Rather it belongs to Allah, Exalted is He, who has placed it with the servant as a trust and commanded him to keep it on the path of justice by directing it to the straight path in knowledge and action. So he strives to teach it what it has been commanded and to act upon what is obligatory. Striving outside this path is wrongdoing to himself, betrayal, and deviation of it from justice, whose opposite is oppression and injustice.

(111) Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin only earns it against himself﴾. This includes every sin, small or great. Whoever commits an evil deed, its worldly and otherworldly punishment falls upon himself and does not extend to others, as Allah said: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. However, when evils appear and are not denounced, their punishment becomes general and their sin encompasses others. These cases also fall under the ruling of this noble verse, because whoever abandons the obligatory denunciation has earned a sin. In this is a demonstration of Allah's justice and wisdom: He does not punish anyone for the sin of another, nor does He punish anyone more than the punishment arising from his own sin. For this reason He said: ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾. That is: He has perfect knowledge and complete wisdom. From His knowledge and wisdom is that He knows the sin, what proceeded from the sinner, the motive that drove him to it, and the punishment that follows from it. He also knows the state of the sinner: if sin proceeds from him due to the overpowering of his soul that commands evil, while he returns to his Lord repeatedly at many times, then He will forgive him and grant him success in repentance. But if it proceeds from him through daring against what is forbidden, with contempt for his Lord's sight and carelessness regarding His punishment, then such a person is far from forgiveness and far from being granted success in repentance.

(112) Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾. That is, one who accuses an innocent person of his sin, although he himself is guilty, has borne upon his back slander toward the innocent and a clear manifest sin. This shows that such an act is among the major sins and destructive ones. It combines several corruptions: earning the sin and the wrong, then accusing one who did not commit it, then the vile lie of clearing oneself and accusing the innocent, then the worldly punishment that is averted from the one deserving it and imposed upon one who does not deserve it, and then what follows from this, namely people's talk about the innocent person, along with other corruptions. We ask Allah for well-being from these and from every evil.

(113) Then He mentioned His favour upon His Messenger, by protecting and preserving him from those who wanted to lead him astray. He said: ﴿And if not for the favour of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you﴾. The reason for the revelation of these noble verses, as the exegetes mention, is that a household in Medina stole. When their theft was discovered, they feared disgrace, so they took the stolen goods and threw them into the house of one who was innocent of it. The thief sought help from his tribe to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him to clear their companion publicly before the people. They said that he had not stolen, and that the one who had stolen was the one in whose house the theft was found, who was innocent. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to clear their companion. Then Allah revealed these verses as a reminder and clarification of that event, and as a warning to the Messenger (ﷺ) against disputing on behalf of the treacherous. For defending the wrongdoer is a form of misguidance. Misguidance is of two kinds: misguidance in knowledge, which is ignorance of the truth, and misguidance in action, which is acting contrary to what is obligatory. Allah protected His Messenger from this kind of misguidance just as He protected him from misguidance in deeds. He informed that their scheme and deception would return upon themselves, as is the case with every schemer, saying: ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves﴾, because that scheming and contrivance did not achieve their aim, and they gained nothing but failure, deprivation, sin and loss. This is a great blessing upon His Messenger (ﷺ), comprising a blessing in action, namely the success to do what is obligatory and protection from every forbidden thing. Then He mentioned His blessing upon him in knowledge, saying: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾. That is: He sent down to you this great Qur'an and wise Reminder, in which is the clarification of everything and the knowledge of the earlier and later generations.

Wisdom (al-hikmah) is either the Sunnah, concerning which some of the early scholars (al-salaf, the righteous predecessors) said: the Sunnah was sent down upon him just as the Qur'an was sent down. Or it is knowledge of the secrets of the Sharia beyond knowledge of its rulings, and placing things in their proper places and arranging each thing according to its measure. ﴿And taught you what you did not know﴾. This includes everything Allah taught him. Indeed, he (ﷺ), as Allah described him before prophethood, ﴿did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾, and ﴿He found you lost and guided you﴾. Then Allah continued to reveal to him, to teach him and to perfect him, until he attained a station of knowledge that the earlier and later generations could not reach. So he was the most knowledgeable of creation in every respect, the most comprehensive of the attributes of perfection, and the most perfect in them. For this reason He said: ﴿And ever has the favour of Allah upon you been great﴾. His favour upon the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is greater than His favour upon all creation, and the kinds of favour that Allah bestowed upon him cannot be enumerated nor fully counted.

However, when evils appear and are not denounced, their punishment becomes general and their sin encompasses others. These cases also fall under the ruling of this noble verse, because whoever abandons the obligatory denunciation has earned a sin. In this is a demonstration of Allah's justice and wisdom: He does not punish anyone for the sin of another, nor does He punish anyone more than the punishment arising from his own sin. For this reason He said: ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾. That is: He has perfect knowledge and complete wisdom. From His knowledge and wisdom is that He knows the sin, what proceeded from the sinner, the motive that drove him to it, and the punishment that follows from it. He also knows the state of the sinner: if sin proceeds from him due to the overpowering of his soul that commands evil, while he returns to his Lord repeatedly at many times, then He will forgive him and grant him success in repentance. But if it proceeds from him through daring against what is forbidden, with contempt for his Lord's sight and carelessness regarding His punishment, then such a person is far from forgiveness and far from being granted success in repentance.

(112) Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾. That is, one who accuses an innocent person of his sin, although he himself is guilty, has borne upon his back slander toward the innocent and a clear manifest sin. This shows that such an act is among the major sins and destructive ones. It combines several corruptions: earning the sin and the wrong, then accusing one who did not commit it, then the vile lie of clearing oneself and accusing the innocent, then the worldly punishment that is averted from the one deserving it and imposed upon one who does not deserve it, and then what follows from this, namely people's talk about the innocent person, along with other corruptions. We ask Allah for well-being from these and from every evil.

(113) Then He mentioned His favour upon His Messenger, by protecting and preserving him from those who wanted to lead him astray. They said that he had not stolen, and that the one who had stolen was the one in whose house the theft was found, who was innocent. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to clear their companion. Then Allah revealed these verses as a reminder and clarification of that event, and as a warning to the Messenger (ﷺ) against disputing on behalf of the treacherous. For defending the wrongdoer is a form of misguidance. Misguidance is of two kinds: misguidance in knowledge, which is ignorance of the truth, and misguidance in action, which is acting contrary to what is obligatory. Allah protected His Messenger from this kind of misguidance just as He protected him from misguidance in deeds. He informed that their scheme and deception would return upon themselves, as is the case with every schemer, saying: ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves﴾, because that scheming and contrivance did not achieve their aim, and they gained nothing but failure, deprivation, sin and loss. That is: He sent down to you this great Qur'an and wise Reminder, in which is the clarification of everything and the knowledge of the earlier and later generations.

Wisdom (al-hikmah) is either the Sunnah, concerning which some of the early scholars (al-salaf, the righteous predecessors) said: the Sunnah was sent down upon him just as the Qur'an was sent down. This includes everything Allah taught him. Indeed, he (ﷺ), as Allah described him before prophethood, ﴿did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾, and ﴿He found you lost and guided you﴾. Then Allah continued to reveal to him, to teach him and to perfect him, until he attained a station of knowledge that the earlier and later generations could not reach. So he was the most knowledgeable of creation in every respect, the most comprehensive of the attributes of perfection, and the most perfect in them. For this reason He said: ﴿And ever has the favour of Allah upon you been great﴾. His favour upon the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is greater than His favour upon all creation, and the kinds of favour that Allah bestowed upon him cannot be enumerated nor fully counted.

(105) He, exalted is He, informs that He sent down to His servant and messenger the Book with truth, meaning preserved in its revelation from the devils, so that falsehood cannot reach it from them. Rather, it descended with truth and also contains truth. Its reports are true, and its commands and prohibitions are just. ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾. He also informs that He sent it down so that you might judge between the people. In another verse: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them﴾. It is possible that this verse refers to judging between people in matters of dispute and disagreement, and that verse refers to clarifying the whole religion, its roots and its branches. It is also possible that both verses have one meaning, so that judging between people here includes judging between them concerning blood, honour, property and all other rights, as well as in matters of belief and all matters of rulings. His words ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ mean: not by your own desire, but by what Allah has taught you and inspired in you, as in His saying, ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾. In this is evidence of his infallibility (ﷺ) in what he conveys from Allah of all rulings and other matters, and that a judge must have knowledge and justice, as shown by His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾, and He did not say "by what you have seen." He also made judging between people dependent on knowledge of the Book.

When Allah commanded judging between people in a way that includes justice and equity, He forbade oppression and injustice, which are the opposite of justice, saying: ﴿And do not be a pleader for the treacherous﴾. That is, do not argue on behalf of one whose treachery you know, whether he is a claimant to what is not his or a denier of a right owed by him, whether you know this or only suppose it. In this is evidence for the prohibition of disputing for falsehood, and of representing the wrongdoer in religious disputes and worldly rights. The implication of the verse permits taking on representation in a dispute for one who is not known for wrongdoing.

(106) ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what has proceeded from you, if anything did proceed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is, He forgives a great sin for whoever seeks His forgiveness and repents and turns back to Him, and He grants him success in righteous deeds afterward, which bring reward and remove punishment.

(107) ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾. Ikhtiyan (betraying) and khiyanah (betrayal) have the same meaning as wrongdoing, injustice and sin. This includes the prohibition of arguing on behalf of one who has committed a wrong and upon whom a punishment is due, whether a hadd (fixed penalty) or ta'zir (discretionary penalty). He must not be defended by denying what he did as treachery, or by averting the legal punishment that resulted from it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾. That is, one who is much given to treachery and sin. When love is negated, its opposite is established, which is hatred. This is like a reason for the prohibition mentioned earlier.

(108) Then He mentioned about these treacherous people that ﴿they conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him﴾. This is from weakness of faith and deficiency of certainty, when fear of creatures is greater in their hearts than fear of Allah. So they strive, by permissible and forbidden means, to avoid disgrace before people. Yet they have openly defied Allah with grave deeds and have not cared that He sees them and is aware of them. He is with them in knowledge in all their circumstances, especially when they plot what does not please Him in speech, such as clearing the guilty and accusing the innocent of the crime, and striving for this with the Messenger (ﷺ) so that he would do what they had plotted. They combined several crimes and did not watch over the Lord of the earth and the heavens, who knows their secrets and inner thoughts. For this reason He threatened them, saying: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what they do, Encompassing﴾. That is, He has encompassed that in knowledge. Yet He did not hasten punishment upon them. Rather He gave them respite, offered them repentance, and warned them against persisting in their sin, which brings severe punishment.

(109) ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their advocate?﴾ That is: suppose you argued on their behalf in this worldly life, and your argument averted from them some of what they feared of shame and disgrace before people; what good does that bring them or benefit them? Who will argue for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, when the proof is directed against them, and their tongues, hands and feet testify against them for what they used to do? On that Day Allah will pay them their true due, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth. So who will argue for them, when He knows the secret and what is more hidden, and who will set up witnesses against them against which denial is impossible?

This verse contains guidance to compare what is supposed to be worldly benefit resulting from abandoning Allah's commands or committing His prohibitions, with what is lost of the reward of the Hereafter or what is gained of its punishments. {114} That is: there is no good in much of what people confide to one another and discuss. Then the Exalted made an exception, saying: ﴿except for one who orders charity﴾: whether of wealth, knowledge, or any kind of benefit. Indeed, it may even include the purely personal acts of worship, such as glorifying God (tasbih), praising Him (tahmid) and the like, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, for every tasbih there is a charity, for every takbir a charity, for every tahlil a charity, enjoining good is a charity, forbidding evil is a charity, and in the intimate relations of one of you there is a charity..." (the hadith). ﴿Or a good deed﴾: this means kindness, obedience, and everything whose goodness is known by the Sharia and by reason. When enjoining good is mentioned without being coupled with forbidding evil, it includes forbidding evil, because abandoning what is forbidden is part of good, and also good deeds are not complete except by abandoning evil. But when the two are coupled, "good" is interpreted as doing what is commanded, and "evil" as abandoning what is forbidden. ﴿Or reconciliation between people﴾: reconciliation (islah) only takes place between parties who are in dispute and enmity, and dispute, quarrel and resentment bring about an incalculable amount of evil and division. For this reason the Lawgiver urged reconciliation between people concerning blood, property and honour, and even in matters of religion, as the Exalted said: ﴿And hold fast to the rope of God all together and do not divide﴾, and He said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God...﴾ [the verse], and He said: ﴿And reconciliation is best﴾. The one who strives for reconciliation between people is better than the one who stands in prayer, fasts and gives charity. The one who reconciles must have God set right his striving and his deed, just as the one who strives for corruption will not have God set right his deed, nor will his aim be accomplished, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, God does not set right the work of the corrupters﴾. So these things, wherever they are done, are good, as the exception indicates. But the completeness and perfection of the reward depends on the intention and sincerity. Hence He said: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God, We will give him a great reward﴾. Therefore a servant should intend the face of God, make his deed sincerely for God at every time and in every part of good, so that he obtains the great reward, and so that he becomes accustomed to sincerity and becomes one of the sincere. And the reward is complete for him whether or not his aim is achieved, because the intention has been formed and accompanied by what is possible of action.

{115} That is: whoever opposes the Messenger (ﷺ) and defies him in what he has brought, {after the guidance has become clear to him} through the Qur'anic proofs and the prophetic evidences, {and follows other than the way of the believers}, and their way is their path in their creed and their deeds, {We shall leave him to what he has turned to}; that is, We shall leave him to what he has chosen for himself and forsake him, so We will not grant him success in goodness, because he saw the truth and knew it and abandoned it. His recompense from Allah, by way of justice, is that He leaves him in his misguidance, bewildered, and increases his misguidance upon his misguidance, as Allah the Exalted says: {So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate} [al-Saff: 5], and Allah the Exalted says: {And We turn about their hearts and their sights, just as they did not believe in it the first time} [al-An'am: 110].

Its implication (mafhum) indicates that whoever does not oppose the Messenger {and follows other than the way of the believers} (by intending the face of Allah, following His Messenger, and adhering to the community of the Muslims), and then there proceeds from him some sins or the inclination toward them, which are among the requirements of the souls and the overpowering of natures, then Allah does not entrust him to his own self and his Satan, but rather He rectifies him with His kindness, bestows upon him His protection, and preserves him from evil, as Allah the Exalted says concerning Yusuf (peace be upon him): {Thus [it was], that We might avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was among Our sincere servants} [Yusuf: 24]; that is, because of his sincerity, We averted from him evil, and likewise every sincere person, as indicated by the generality of the reason given and by His saying {And We will cause him to enter Hell}; that is, We will punish him therein with a great punishment. {And evil is the destination}; that is, the place of return and final abode.

{116} This threat that follows from opposition and defiance of the believers has degrees that none can enumerate except Allah, according to the state of the sin, minor or major. Among it is what results in eternal abiding in the Fire and entails complete abandonment, and among it is what is less than that. So perhaps the second verse is like an elaboration of this general statement, namely that shirk, Allah the Exalted does not forgive, because it includes disparagement of the Lord of the worlds and of His oneness, and equating a created being who possesses for himself neither harm nor benefit with the One who owns benefit and harm, from whom alone is every blessing and who alone averts calamities, who has absolute perfection in every respect and complete independence in every aspect of consideration. Thus, among the greatest injustice and the most distant error is failing to devote worship sincerely to the One of such status and greatness, and directing any part of it to a created being who has no share of the attributes of perfection and no share of the attributes of independence, rather who has nothing but nonexistence: nonexistence of being, nonexistence of perfection, nonexistence of independence, and poverty in every respect. As for what is below shirk of sins and disobediences, it is subject to the Will: if Allah wills, He forgives it by His mercy and His wisdom, and if He wills, He punishes for it and requites by His justice and His wisdom.

This noble verse has been cited as evidence that the consensus (ijma') of this Ummah is a proof (hujjah), and that it is protected from error. The basis of this is that Allah threatened whoever opposes the way of the believers with abandonment and the Fire, and "the way of the believers" is a singular noun in the construct form which encompasses all that the believers hold to in creed and deeds. So when they agree on the obligation of something, or its recommendation, or its prohibition, or its disapproval, or its permissibility, then this is their way, and whoever opposes them in any of that after their consensus has been established upon it, then he has followed other than their way.

This is also indicated by the saying of Allah the Exalted: {You are the best nation brought forth for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong} [Al 'Imran: 110]. The indication from it is that Allah the Exalted informed that the believers of this Ummah only enjoin what is right. So when they agree on the obligation of something or its recommendation, then it is among what they have commanded, and it is thereby necessarily ruled by the text of the verse to be right (ma'ruf), and there is nothing after the right except the wrong (munkar). Likewise, when they agree on prohibiting something, then it is among what they have forbidden, so it cannot be other than wrong.

Similar to this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over mankind} [al-Baqarah: 143]. Allah the Exalted informed that He made this Ummah a median (wasat), that is, just and excellent, so that they would be witnesses over mankind, that is, in everything. So when they bear witness regarding a ruling that Allah has commanded it, or forbidden it, or permitted it, their testimony is protected, because they know what they testify to and are just in their testimony. Had the matter been otherwise, they would not have been just in their testimony nor knowing of it.

Similar to this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger} [al-Nisa': 59]. It is understood from it that what they do not dispute but rather agree upon, they are not commanded to refer back to the Book and the Sunnah, and that can only be in accordance with the Book and the Sunnah, not in opposition to it.

These proofs and the like establish with certainty that the consensus of this Ummah is a decisive proof.

Thus Allah has made clear the ugliness of the error of the polytheists in His saying:

{117–118} He means: these polytheists do not call upon anything besides Allah except females, that is, idols and statues named with female names, such as al-'Uzza, Manat and the like. It is well known that a name indicates the thing named. So when their names are feminine and deficient, this indicates the deficiency of what is named by them and their lack of the attributes of perfection, as Allah the Exalted has informed in more than one place of His Book that they do not create, do not provide sustenance, do not repel from their worshippers any benefit or harm, not even from themselves, and do not help themselves against one who intends them harm; and they have no hearing, no sight, and no hearts. How, then, is one of this description worshipped, while the sincere devotion is abandoned to the One to whom belong the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna), the Supreme Attributes, all praise, perfection, glory, majesty, might, beauty, mercy, goodness and benevolence, the sole creation and governance, and great wisdom in command and decree? Is this not among the most hideous ugliness, indicating the deficiency of its possessor and his reaching the utmost baseness and vileness that any imagining mind could conceive or any describer could depict? And despite this, their worship of these deficient idols is merely in form, and in reality they worship none but Satan, who is their enemy, who wants their destruction and strives in that with all that he can, and who is at the furthest distance from Allah, may Allah curse him and remove him far from His mercy. Just as Allah has removed him from His mercy, he strives to remove the servants from the mercy of Allah; he only calls his party so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.

This is why Allah informed of his effort to mislead the servants, to adorn evil and corruption for them, and that he said to his Lord, swearing: {I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion} (Qur'an 4:118); that is, a determined share. The accursed one knew that he could not mislead all of Allah's servants, and that the sincere servants of Allah have no authority over them; his authority is only over those who take him as ally and prefer his obedience over the obedience of their Master. And he swore in another place that he would surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them (Qur'an 15:39–40). So this which the wicked one assumed and was certain of, Allah the Exalted informed of its occurrence in His saying: {And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers} (Qur'an 34:20).

{119} This appointed portion which he swore he would take from them, he mentioned what he intends for them and what he aims for them in His saying: {and I will surely mislead them} (Qur'an 4:119); that is, from the straight path, misguidance in knowledge and misguidance in action. {And I will surely lead them into false hopes}; that is, along with misguidance, I will surely lead them to hope that they will attain what the guided attain. This is delusion itself. He did not limit himself to merely misguiding them, but adorned for them the misguidance they were in. This is an increase of evil upon their evil, for they perform the deeds of the people of the Fire that necessitate punishment, while they reckon that these deeds necessitate Paradise. Consider this with regard to the Jews, the Christians and the like; for Allah related of them: {And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." Those are their wishful thinkings} (Qur'an 2:111), {Thus We have made attractive to every nation its deeds} (Qur'an 6:108), {Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? They are those whose effort is lost in the worldly life while they think they are doing well in work"} (Qur'an 18:103–104), and the verse. And Allah the Exalted said of the hypocrites that they will say on the Day of Resurrection to the believers: {Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah"} (Qur'an 57:14).

And His saying: {And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of livestock} (Qur'an 4:119); that is, by slitting their ears, such as the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham; so He alerted to some of that to cover all of it. This is a kind of misguidance that entails making lawful what Allah has forbidden, or making forbidden what Allah has made lawful. Attached to this are corrupt beliefs and unjust rulings, which are among the greatest forms of misguidance. {And I will surely command them, and they will surely change the creation of Allah} (Qur'an 4:119). This encompasses changing the outward creation by tattooing, filing the teeth, plucking the facial hair and making gaps between the teeth for beauty, and the like, which Satan has led them astray with; so they changed the creation of the Merciful. This includes discontent with His creation, disparagement of His wisdom, the belief that what they make with their hands is better than the creation of the Merciful, and non-acceptance of His decree and governance. It also encompasses changing the inner creation; for Allah the Exalted created His servants upright (hanif), inclined by nature to accept the truth and prefer it. Then the devils came to them and diverted them from this beautiful creation, and adorned for them evil, polytheism, disbelief, wickedness and disobedience. Indeed, every child is born upon the fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, and the like, changing what Allah instilled in the servants of His oneness, love of Him and knowledge of Him. So the devils have seized them at this point as a wolf seizes lone sheep, were it not for Allah's kindness and generosity toward His sincere servants; what befell these deluded ones would have befallen them. What befell them is their turning away from their Lord and Creator and their turning to their enemy, who wishes them evil in every way; so they lost this world and the Hereafter, and returned with disappointment and a losing bargain. This is why He said: {And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss} (Qur'an 4:119). And what loss is clearer and greater than that of one who has lost his religion and his worldly life, whose sins and wrongdoings have destroyed him, so that he has gained everlasting wretchedness and lost everlasting bliss? Just as whoever turns to his Master and prefers His pleasure gains every gain, achieves every success, wins the happiness of both abodes, and becomes content of eye. There is no preventer of what You give, and no giver of what You withhold. O Allah! Make us allies of those You have made allies, and grant us well-being among those You have granted well-being.

{120} Then He said: {He promises them and gives them false hopes} (Qur'an 4:120); that is, Satan promises whoever strives to mislead them, and the promise includes the threat as well, as Allah the Exalted said: {Satan threatens you with poverty} (Qur'an 2:268). He promises them that if they spend in the way of Allah they will become poor, and frightens them if they strive, with killing and other things, as Allah the Exalted said: {That is only Satan frightening his allies...} (Qur'an 3:175), and he frightens them when they prefer the pleasure of Allah with everything possible and impossible that enters their minds, until they grow lazy in doing good. Likewise he gives them vain hopes, which upon examination are like a mirage with no reality. This is why He said: {And Satan promises them nothing but delusion} (Qur'an 4:120).

{121} {Those, their refuge is Hell} (Qur'an 4:121); that is, whoever submits to Satan, turns away from his Lord and becomes one of Iblis's followers and party, his abode is the Fire. {And they will not find for themselves a place of escape therefrom} (Qur'an 4:121); that is, no escape or refuge, but they will abide therein forever and ever.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 122:

{122} That is: {Those who believe} in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree (al-qadar), its good and its bad, in the manner they were commanded: with knowledge, affirmation, and acknowledgment. {And do righteous deeds}: those arising from faith. This includes all that is commanded, obligatory and recommended, that of the heart, that of the tongue, and that of the remaining limbs. Each one has the reward that is prescribed for it, according to its state, its rank, and its perfecting of faith and righteous deeds, and he forfeits what is prescribed for it according to what he has neglected of faith and deeds. This is in accordance with what is known of Allah's wisdom and mercy, and likewise His true promise, which is known from following the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. For this reason He mentioned the reward prescribed for that in His words: {We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow}: therein is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived: of kinds of delicious food and drink, wondrous sights, fine spouses, palaces and decorated chambers, drooping trees, marvelous fruits, sweet voices, abundant blessings, and the mutual visiting of brothers and their remembrance of what passed between them in the gardens of Paradise. Higher than all of that [and greater] is: Allah's good pleasure with them, the spirits' enjoyment of His nearness, the eyes' beholding of Him, and the ears' hearing of His address, which makes them forget every bounty and joy. Had Allah not steadied them, they would have flown away and died of joy and delight. How sweet is that bliss! How lofty is what the Generous Lord has bestowed upon them! And what they have attained of every good and delight is beyond the power of describers to portray! The completion and perfection of that is eternal abiding in those lofty abodes.
For this reason He said: {Abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful in speech than Allah?}: So Allah the Mighty spoke truly, whose word and discourse reach the highest degree of truthfulness. For this reason, since His speech is true and His report is true, what it indicates by correspondence, inclusion, and necessary implication is all intended by His speech. Likewise the speech of His Messenger (ﷺ), because he reports only by His command and speaks only from His revelation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 123–124:

{123} That is: {It is not} the matter, nor salvation, nor purification {by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book}. Amani (wishful thinking) are the bare musings of the soul, unaccompanied by the action that should go with them; they are mere claims which, if one were to oppose them with their like, would be of the same kind. This applies to every matter, so how much more to the matter of faith and eternal felicity. The wishful thinking of the People of the Book is one that God has informed us of, when they {said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians. Those are their wishful thinkings}. As for others who do not belong to a Book or a messenger, it applies even more so and more fittingly. Likewise, God includes in this those who attribute themselves to Islam, out of perfect justice and fairness; for mere affiliation with any religion whatsoever benefits nothing if a person does not bring proof of the soundness of his claim. Deeds confirm the claim or refute it. For this reason, the Exalted said: {Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it}. This is comprehensive of all doers, because evil encompasses every sin, whether minor or major, and it also encompasses every recompense, whether little or much, worldly or otherworldly. People in this station are of varying degrees, known only to God: some are light in their sins and some are heavy in them. Whoever's entire deed is evil, and that is not possible except for a disbeliever, then if he dies without repentance, he is recompensed with abiding in the painful punishment. Whoever's deed is righteous, and he is upright in most of his states, and only some minor sins occasionally proceed from him, then what afflicts him of worry, grief, harm, and some pains in his body, his heart, his beloved, or his wealth, and the like, these are expiators for sins; they are also recompense for his deeds, which God ordains out of kindness to His servants.
Between these two states lie many degrees. This recompense for general evil deeds is restricted to other than those who repent, for the one who repents from sin is as one who has no sin, as the texts indicate.
And His saying: {And he will not find for himself besides God any ally or helper}: this removes what one might suppose, namely that the one who deserves recompense for his deed may have an ally, helper, or intercessor who repels from him what he deserves. So God informs that this is negated: there is no ally who obtains for him what he seeks, nor helper who repels from him what he dreads, except his Lord and Sovereign.

{124} {And whoever does righteous deeds}: this includes all deeds of the heart and of the body, and it also includes every doer, whether jinn or human, young or old, male or female. For this reason He said: {whether male or female while being a believer}. This is a condition for all deeds: they are not righteous, nor accepted, nor is reward bestowed upon them, nor is punishment averted by them, except with faith. Deeds without faith are like the branches of a tree whose root has been cut, or like a building erected upon the surface of water. Faith is the root, the foundation, and the base upon which everything is built. This condition should be noted in every unrestricted deed, for it is restricted by it. {Those}: that is, those who combine faith and righteous deeds, {will enter Paradise}, which comprises what souls desire and what eyes delight in, {and they will not be wronged the least bit}: that is, not a little nor a lot of the good they did, but they will find it complete, full, and multiplied many times over.
