Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 125:

{125} That is: there is no one better in religion than the one who combines sincerity (ikhlas) toward the One worshipped, which is submitting one's face to Allah, indicating the submission of the heart, its turning, its returning (inabah), its sincerity, and the turning of the face and all the other limbs toward Allah. {And he}: with this sincerity and submission, {is a doer of good (muhsin)}; that is, one who follows the Shari'ah of Allah with which Allah sent His messengers, revealed His books, and made it a path for the elite of His creation and their followers. {And follows the religion (millah) of Ibrahim}; that is, his religion and law. {Hanif}; that is, inclining away from polytheism (shirk) toward monotheism (tawhid), and away from turning toward creation toward turning to the Creator. {And Allah took Ibrahim as a intimate friend (khalil)}: and khullah (intimate friendship) is the highest type of love. This rank was attained by the two intimate friends, Muhammad and Ibrahim, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them. As for love from Allah, it is for all the believers in general. Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil only because he fulfilled what he was commanded and carried out what he was tested with, so Allah made him an imam for the people, took him as a khalil, and raised his mention among all the worlds.

{126} This noble verse demonstrates God's encompassing of all things. He informs that to Him belongs {whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth}; that is, all of them are His dominion and His servants. They are the owned, and He is the Owner, the one who alone manages them. His knowledge encompasses all known things, His sight all visible things, and His hearing all audible things. His will and power have taken effect on all existing things, and His mercy has embraced the people of the earth and the heavens. By His might and dominance He has subdued every creature, and all things are subservient to Him.

The inquiry (al-istifta') is the questioner's request from the one asked that he explain the sacred ruling concerning the matter asked about. He reports concerning the believers that they sought a ruling (yastaftunna) from the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the rights of women that pertain to them. So God Himself gave this ruling, saying: ﴿Say: "God gives you a ruling concerning them."﴾ Therefore, act upon what He has ruled for you in all matters concerning women, by fulfilling their rights and refraining from wronging them, in general and in particular. This is a general command that encompasses everything God has legislated, in commands and prohibitions, regarding women, whether wives or others, young or old. Then, after the general statement, He specified the counsel concerning the weak among orphans and young children, out of concern for them and as a deterrent against neglecting their rights. He said: ﴿And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women﴾; that is, He also gives you a ruling by what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women ﴿to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them﴾. This is a report about the situation existing and occurring at that time: when an orphan girl was under a man's guardianship, he would deprive her of her right and wrong her, either by consuming her property, or part of it, or by preventing her from marrying, so that he could benefit from her wealth, out of fear that it would be taken out of his hands if he married her off; or by taking from the bridegroom she would marry, by condition or otherwise. This applies if he was averse to her; or if he desired her while she possessed beauty and wealth, and he did not act justly regarding her dowry, but gave her less than she deserved. All of this is wrongdoing that falls under this text. For this reason He said: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾; that is, you desire to refrain from marrying them, or to marry them, as we have mentioned in its illustration. ﴿And [concerning] the weak among the children﴾; that is, He gives you a ruling concerning the weak among the young children: that you give them their rights of inheritance and other things, and that you not seize their property in a manner of injustice and arbitrary control. ﴿And that you stand firmly for the orphans in justice﴾; that is, with complete justice. This includes standing over them by compelling them to obey God's command and what He has obligated upon His servants, so the guardians are charged with this and oblige them to what God has obligated. It also includes standing over them in their worldly interests, by developing their wealth and seeking what is best for them in it, and not approaching it except in the best manner. Likewise, they should not show favoritism toward any friend or other in matters of marriage or otherwise, in a way that diminishes their rights. This is from the mercy of the Exalted toward His servants, since He urged in the utmost degree the upholding of the interests of one who cannot look after his own interests due to his weakness and the loss of his father.
Then He urged goodness in general, saying: ﴿And whatever good you do﴾, for the orphans and for others, whether the good is transitive or intransitive, ﴿indeed, God is ever Knowing of it﴾; that is, His knowledge has encompassed the deeds of those who do good, whether little or much, good or its opposite, and He will reward each according to his deed.

{128} That is: if a woman fears the ill-treatment (nushuz) of her husband, meaning his aloofness from her, his lack of desire for her, and his turning away from her, then the best course in this situation is that the two of them make peace (sulh) between them. This is done by the woman forgoing some of her lawful rights owed to her by her husband, in a way that allows her to remain with her husband. She may be content with less than what is due to her in maintenance, clothing, housing or equal division (qasm), by waiving her right to it, or by giving up her day and night to her husband or to her co-wife. When the two agree upon this state, there is no sin or fault upon either of them in it, neither upon her nor upon the husband. It is then permissible for the husband to remain with her in this condition, and it is better than separation. For this reason He said: ﴿And reconciliation is best﴾.

It may be taken from the generality of this wording and meaning that reconciliation between those who have a right or a dispute over all matters is better than each of them insisting on the full extent of his right, because of what it contains of setting things right, the preservation of harmony, and the attribute of forbearance. It is permissible in all matters, except when it makes lawful what is unlawful or makes unlawful what is lawful; then it is not reconciliation but injustice. Know that every ruling among the rulings does not become complete or perfect except with the presence of its requirements and the absence of its impediments. Among these is this great ruling, which is reconciliation. He, exalted is He, mentioned its requirement and drew attention to the fact that it is good, and good is what every intelligent person seeks and desires. If, in addition to that, Allah has commanded it and urged it, the believer's seeking and desire for it increases. He mentioned the impediment in His words: ﴿And souls are presented with stinginess﴾; that is, souls have been created with stinginess, which is the lack of willingness to give what is owed by a person and eagerness to obtain the right that is due to him. Souls are naturally disposed to this. Therefore, it is incumbent upon you to strive to uproot this base character from your souls and to replace it with its opposite, which is generosity (samahah), namely giving up the right that is owed by you and being content with part of the right that is yours. Whenever a person is granted this good character, reconciliation between him and his opponent or his dealer becomes easy for him, and the path to attaining what is sought is made smooth. By contrast, the one who does not strive to remove stinginess from his soul finds reconciliation and agreement difficult, because he is not satisfied except with all that is his, and he does not agree to discharge what is upon him. If his opponent is like him, the matter becomes severe.

Then He said: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah﴾; that is, do good in the worship of the Creator, by worshipping the servant of his Lord as if he sees Him, and if he does not see Him, then He sees him; and do good to the created beings by all means of goodness, whether by benefit with wealth, knowledge, standing, or otherwise. And fear Allah by doing all that is commanded and abandoning all that is forbidden. Or: do good by doing what is commanded and fear Allah by abandoning what is forbidden. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾: He has encompassed it with knowledge and awareness of its outward and inward aspects, so He will preserve it for you and reward you for it in the most complete reward.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 129:

{129} He, the Exalted, informs that husbands cannot and do not have the ability to be perfectly just among their wives. This is because justice requires equal love, equal inclination, equal feeling in the heart toward them, and then acting in accordance with that. This is impossible and not attainable. Therefore Allah pardoned what cannot be done and forbade what is within one's ability, by His saying: ﴿So do not incline completely [toward one], leaving her as if suspended﴾. That is: do not incline with a great inclination such that you fail to fulfill her obligatory rights. Rather, do what is within your capacity of justice. Regarding maintenance, clothing, the turn-taking (al-qasm) and the like, you must be just among them in these matters. This is unlike love, intimacy and the like, for when a husband neglects what is owed to his wife, she becomes like one suspended, who has no husband, so she is at rest and prepares herself for marriage, yet she is not one who has a husband who fulfills her rights. ﴿And if you amend﴾ what is between you and your wives by compelling yourselves to do what the soul does not desire, seeking reward and standing up for the wife's right; and also amend what is between you and other people, and amend between people in what they dispute. This requires encouraging every path that leads to reconciliation in every way, as mentioned earlier. ﴿And fear [Allah]﴾: by performing what is commanded, avoiding what is forbidden, and patiently bearing what is decreed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He forgives what has proceeded from you of sins and shortcoming in the obligatory right, and He will show you mercy as you showed compassion and mercy to your wives.

This is the third case between spouses, when agreement cannot be reached. In that case there is no harm in separation, so He says: ﴿And if they separate﴾; that is, by divorce (talaq), annulment (faskh), khul' (divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for compensation), or otherwise. ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾: each of the spouses, from His bounty, that is, from His vast and all-encompassing grace and kindness. He will enrich the husband with a wife better for him than her, and will enrich her from His bounty, even if her share from her husband has ceased, for her provision rests with the One who undertakes the provision of all creation and who maintains their welfare. Perhaps Allah will grant her a husband better than him. ﴿And Allah is ever Expansive﴾; that is, abundant in bounty and vast in mercy. His mercy and kindness reach as far as His knowledge reaches. ﴿And Allah is ever Wise﴾; that is, He gives according to His wisdom and withholds according to His wisdom. When His wisdom requires withholding some of His servants from His kindness, because of a matter on the servant's part that makes him undeserving of kindness, He deprives him out of justice and wisdom.

{131–132} Almighty God informs us of the all-encompassing scope of His great and vast dominion, which necessarily entails His management in every kind of management and His disposing of affairs in every kind of disposition, both by decree (qadar) and by law (shar'). His legal disposition is that He enjoined the former and the latter peoples, the followers of the earlier and later scriptures, to observe taqwa (God-consciousness), which includes the commands and prohibitions, the legislation of rulings, and the recompense: reward for those who fulfil this injunction, and painful punishment for those who neglect and waste it. For this reason He says: ﴿And if you disbelieve﴾, by abandoning the taqwa of God and associating with God that for which He has sent down no authority. Indeed, you harm only yourselves by that, and you do not harm God at all, nor do you diminish His dominion. He has servants better than you, greater and more numerous, who obey Him and submit to His command. For this reason He follows that with His saying: ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is ever Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾ To Him belongs perfect generosity and comprehensive benevolence, issuing from the treasuries of His mercy, which spending does not diminish and which the giving of any portion does not deplete, pouring forth night and day. Even if the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, the first and the last of them, were to gather and each one asked for whatever his wishes reached, this would not diminish His dominion in the least. That is because He is Generous, Abounding in wealth, Glorious; His giving is speech, and His punishment is speech. His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.

And among the completeness of His independence is that He possesses every attribute of perfection; for if there were any deficiency in Him in any respect, there would be in Him some kind of need for that perfection. Rather, every attribute of perfection belongs to Him, and among those attributes is the perfection of this attribute itself.

And among the completeness of His independence is that He has not taken a consort, nor a son, nor a partner in His dominion, nor a helper, nor an aide to Him in any of the management of His kingdom. And among the completeness of His independence is that the higher and lower worlds, in all their conditions and affairs, are in need of Him, and they ask Him for all their needs, both the subtle and the great. So God, exalted is He, fulfils those requests and demands, makes them independent and content, bestows His favour upon them with His kindness, and guides them.

As for al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), it is one of the glorious names of God, indicating that He alone deserves all praise, love, commendation and honour. This is because of the attributes of praise that He possesses, which are the attributes of beauty and majesty, and because of the abundant blessings He has bestowed upon His creation. So He is praised in every state.

How excellent is the conjunction of these two noble names: al-Ghani (the Independent) and al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy). For He is independent and praised; so He has perfection from His independence, perfection from His being praised, and perfection from the combination of one with the other. Then He repeated the encompassing of His dominion over what is in the heavens and [what is in] the earth, and that He is over all things Wakil (Guardian/Disposer of affairs), that is: the Knower who sustains the management of things in accordance with wisdom. For that is part of the completeness of wakala (trusteeship), since wakala entails knowledge of that over which one is a wakil, the strength and power to execute and manage it, and that this management is in accordance with wisdom and benefit. Whatever deficiency is found in this is due to a deficiency in the wakil, while God, exalted is He, is far above every deficiency.

{133} That is: He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid), who possesses complete power and an executing will over you. {If He wills, He can remove you, O mankind, and bring others} — others who are more obedient to Allah than you and better than you. In this is a warning to people against persisting in their disbelief and turning away from their Lord; for Allah does not care for them in the least if they do not obey Him, but He gives respite and delays, and He does not neglect.

{134} Then He informs that whoever's aspiration and will are base, not reaching beyond the reward of this world, and who has no will for the Hereafter, has indeed confined his striving and his outlook. Along with that, he will obtain from the reward of this world only what Allah has decreed for him from it. For He, exalted is He, is the Owner of everything, in Whose hand is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. So both should be sought from Him, and one should seek His help in attaining them; for what is with Him is not attained except through obedience to Him, and religious and worldly affairs are not achieved except by seeking His help and constantly being in need of Him. He, exalted is He, has wisdom in granting success to whom He grants it, in abandoning whom He abandons, and in His giving and withholding. Therefore He said: {And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing}.

{133} That is: He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid), who possesses complete power and an executing will over you. {If He wills, He can remove you, O mankind, and bring others} — others who are more obedient to Allah than you and better than you. Almighty God commands His believing servants to be "steadfast in upholding justice, bearing witness for God" (﴿قوَّامين بالقسطِ شهداء لله﴾). The word al-qawwām is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālaghah), meaning: be, in all your circumstances, those who firmly stand by justice (al-qist), which is equity in the rights of God and the rights of His servants. Justice regarding the rights of God means that His blessings are not used to disobey Him, but are spent in obedience to Him. Justice regarding the rights of people means that you render all the rights that are upon you just as you seek your own rights: you pay the obligatory maintenance and debts, and you treat people in the way you would like them to treat you, in matters of manners, reciprocity, and so forth.

Among the greatest kinds of justice is justice in statements and in those who make them: one should not rule in favour of one of two sayings or one of two disputing parties because of kinship or inclination toward one of them, but should make his direction the establishment of justice between them. Among justice is also giving the testimony you hold, in whatever manner it is, even against loved ones, and even against yourself. For this reason He said: ﴿bearing witness for God, even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives. Whether he be rich or poor, God is more entitled to both of them﴾. That is: do not show consideration to the rich for his wealth, nor to the poor out of your supposed compassion for him, but bear witness in truth against whoever it may be. Standing firm in justice is among the greatest matters, and it is most indicative of the religiosity, piety, and standing of the one who upholds it in Islam. Therefore, whoever counsels his own soul and desires its salvation must give this matter the utmost attention, make it the object of his sight and the focus of his intention, and remove from himself every obstacle and impediment that hinders him from willing justice or acting upon it. The greatest of such impediments is following desire (al-hawā). For this reason, He, exalted is He, drew attention to the removal of this obstacle by His saying: ﴿So do not follow [your] desire, lest you deviate [from justice]﴾. That is: do not follow the desires of your souls that oppose the truth, for if you follow them, you will deviate from what is correct and will not be granted success in justice. Desire either blinds the insight of its possessor, so that he sees truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth, or he knows the truth and abandons it for the sake of his desire. Whoever is safe from the desire of his own soul is granted success in the truth and guided to the straight path.

When He had made clear that standing firm in justice is obligatory, He forbade what contradicts it, which is distorting the tongue away from the truth in testimonies and other matters, and twisting speech away from the intended correctness in every respect or in some respects. This includes distorting testimony, not completing it, or interpreting a witness's statement as referring to something else, for this is a form of distortion (layy), since it is deviation from the truth. ﴿Or refuse [to testify]﴾: that is, abandon the justice entrusted to you, like a witness abandoning his testimony or a judge abandoning his judgment, which he is obliged to uphold. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾: that is, He encompasses what you have done and knows your deeds, both hidden and apparent. In this there is a severe warning to the one who distorts or refuses, and all the more so to the one who rules by falsehood or bears false witness, since his crime is greater: the first two abandoned the truth, whereas this one abandoned the truth and took up falsehood.

(136) Know that a command is either addressed to one who has not entered into the matter and has not taken on any part of it; this is a command to him to enter into it, such as a command to one who is not a believer to believe, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you...﴾ [the verse]. Or it is addressed to one who has already entered into the matter; then the command is meant to correct what has already come from him and to attain what has not yet been attained. Among this is what Allah mentions in this verse, the command to the believers to believe. That requires commanding them to do what corrects their faith: sincerity, truthfulness, avoiding what spoils it, and repenting from every deficiency. It also requires commanding them to acquire what has not yet come from the believer of the sciences of faith and its deeds. For whenever a text reaches him, he understands its meaning and holds it as true, that is part of the faith he is commanded to have. Likewise all the outward and inward deeds are all part of faith, as many texts indicate and as the righteous predecessors of this Ummah agreed upon. Then comes persistence in this and steadfastness upon it until death, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.﴾ He also commanded here to believe in Him, in His messengers, in the Qur'an, and in the earlier Books. All of this is the obligatory faith without which a servant is not a believer: in summary regarding what has not reached him in detail, and in detail regarding what is known in detail. Whoever has believed this commanded faith has indeed been guided and succeeded.

And whoever disbelieves ﴿in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day, has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ And what straying is farther than the straying of one who abandons the straight path of guidance and takes the road that leads him to the painful punishment? Know that disbelief in any one of these matters mentioned is like disbelief in all of them, because they are mutually linked, and faith in some of them without others is impossible.

{137} That is: whoever repeatedly disbelieves after belief, so that he is guided and then goes astray, sees and then becomes blind, believes and then disbelieves, and persists in his disbelief and increases in it, then he is far from success (tawfiq) and from guidance to the straightest path, and far from forgiveness, because he has brought the greatest barrier that prevents him from attaining it. Indeed his disbelief becomes a punishment and a seal (taba') that does not depart, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ and ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾.

The verse indicates that if they do not increase in disbelief, but return to belief and abandon what they were upon of ingratitude, then Allah will forgive them, even if apostasy was repeated from them. And if this ruling applies to disbelief, then other sins that are less than it are all the more so; for if a servant repeatedly commits them and then returns to repentance, Allah returns to him with forgiveness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 138–139:

{138} Bishara (good news) is used for good, and it is used for evil when qualified, as in this verse. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Give the hypocrites the good news﴾; that is, those who displayed Islam and concealed disbelief, with the most wretched and evil of good news, which is a painful punishment. This is because of their love for the disbelievers, their allegiance to them, their support of them, and their abandonment of allegiance to the believers. So what drove them to this? ﴿Do they seek honor with them?﴾ This is indeed the reality of the condition of the hypocrites: their assumption about Allah was bad, and their certainty in the victory of Allah for His believing servants was weak. They noticed some of the means that the disbelievers possess, and their view fell short of what lies beyond that. So they took the disbelievers as allies, by whom they strengthen themselves and seek victory, while in fact ﴿honor belongs to Allah entirely﴾. The affairs of the servants are in His hand, and His will is executed over them. He has guaranteed the victory of His religion and of His believing servants, even though this may be interspersed with some trial for His believing servants and the enemy gaining the upper hand over them for a temporary period, since the ultimate outcome and stability belong to the believers.

In this verse there is a great warning against allying with the disbelievers and abandoning allegiance to the believers, and that such conduct is among the characteristics of the hypocrites, and that faith necessitates love for the believers and their allegiance, and hatred for the disbelievers and enmity toward them.

{140} That is: Allah has already made clear to you, in what He sent down to you, His legal ruling concerning attendance at gatherings of disbelief and disobedience: ﴿that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked﴾; that is, they are treated with contempt. The obligation upon every responsible person regarding the verses of Allah is to believe in them, to glorify them, to revere them and to exalt them. This is the purpose for which they were sent down, and it is the purpose for which Allah created creation. Thus the opposite of belief is disbelief in them, and the opposite of glorifying them is mocking them and belittling them. This includes arguing with disbelievers and hypocrites in order to nullify the verses of Allah and support their disbelief. Likewise the innovators (ahl al-bid'ah) of all their various kinds are included, for their argumentation for their falsehood contains contempt for the verses of Allah, since these verses indicate only the truth and entail nothing but veracity. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 142–143:

{142} Allah informs about the hypocrites, concerning the ugly qualities and vile traits they possessed, and that their method is deceiving Allah, i.e., by what they displayed of faith and concealed of disbelief. They think it passes over Allah, that He does not know it and does not reveal it to His servants, while in fact Allah is the One who deceives them. The mere existence of this state in them, and their walking upon it, is a deception of their own selves. And what deception is greater than that of one who strives in a way that returns upon him with humiliation, abasement and deprivation, and which by itself indicates the deficiency of his intellect, since he combines disobedience while considering it good, and thinks it to be intelligence and cunning?! How much ignorance and forsaking (khidhlan) does to its possessor! Among His deception of them on the Day of Resurrection is what Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believe, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will be torment from before it. They will call to them, "Were we not with you?"...﴾ until the end of the verses. Among their qualities is that ﴿when they stand up for prayer﴾ if they stand, which is the greatest of the physical acts of worship, ﴿they stand lazily﴾, reluctant to it and resentful of performing it. Laziness only arises from the absence of desire in their hearts. Had their hearts not been empty of desire for Allah and what is with Him, lacking faith, laziness would not have proceeded from them. ﴿They show off to the people﴾; i.e., this which is concealed within their inner selves, and this is the source of their deeds, is showing off to people, seeking to be seen by people and to be honored and respected by them, and they are not sincere to Allah. Therefore ﴿they do not remember Allah except a little﴾, because their hearts are filled with showing off. For the remembrance of Allah and constancy in it can only come from a believer whose heart is filled with love of Allah and His greatness.

{143} ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾; i.e., hesitating between the group of believers and the group of disbelievers, neither truly believers, outwardly and inwardly, nor truly disbelievers, outwardly and inwardly. They give their inner selves to the disbelievers and their outer selves to the believers, and this is the greatest misguidance that can be imagined. Hence He said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾; i.e., you will not find a path to guide him nor a means to turn him away from his error, because the gate of mercy has been closed to him, and in its place is every punishment. These blameworthy attributes, by their mention, indicate that the believers are characterized by their opposites: truthfulness outwardly and inwardly, and sincerity, and that their state is not hidden, and their energy in prayer and worship, and their abundant remembrance of Allah the Exalted, and that Allah has guided them and granted them success to the straight path. So let the intelligent person examine himself against these two matters, and let him choose which of them is more fitting for him. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

In this verse is evidence of the perfect justice of Allah, and that Allah does not punish anyone before the proof has been established against him. And in it is a warning against sins, for their doer gives Allah a clear proof against him.

{145} God, exalted is He, informs us of the final fate of the hypocrites (al-munafiqun): that they will be in the lowest depths of the Fire (al-darakat) and the worst states of punishment. They are beneath all the disbelievers, because they shared with them in disbelief in God and in hostility toward His messengers, and they added to that deceit, treachery, and the ability to carry out many kinds of enmity against the believers in a way that goes unnoticed and unfelt. On top of this they secured the application of the rulings of Islam to themselves and the entitlement to things they did not deserve. For all this and similar reasons they deserve the most severe punishment. They have no rescuer from His punishment and no helper who can ward off any part of His retribution from them.

{146} This applies to every hypocrite, except those whom God grants the grace of repentance from their misdeeds. ﴿And amend﴾: meaning, their outward and inward states. ﴿And hold fast to God﴾: they turn to Him and seek refuge in Him to bring about their benefits and ward off harm from themselves. ﴿And make their religion sincerely for God﴾: the religion, which is Islam, faith, and excellence (ihsan). ﴿For God﴾: they intend the face of God with their outward and inward deeds, and they are free from showing off (riya') and hypocrisy (nifaq). Nothing removes it except intense holding fast to God and constant seeking of refuge and dependence on Him to repel it. Sincerity is also wholly incompatible with hypocrisy. So He mentioned both for their excellence, for the fact that outward and inward deeds depend upon them, and for the intense need for them in this situation.

This is because this noble principle is one that God continually repeats and reiterates whenever the context concerns a particular case, and He intends to attach a reward or punishment to it that is shared between that case and the general category it belongs to. He attaches the reward to the general ruling under which that case and others fall, and so that it is not wrongly thought that the ruling is restricted to the particular matter. He gives abundant reward and vast kindness to those who bear burdens for His sake and persevere in deeds. Whoever leaves something for God, God gives him something better than it. Despite this, He knows your outward and inward states, your deeds, and what proceeds from you of sincerity and truthfulness and their opposite. He desires that you repent, turn back, and return to Him. So when you turn back to Him, what would He do with your punishment? He does not take pleasure in your punishment, nor does He benefit from your penalty. Rather, the disobedient one harms only himself, just as the obedience of the obedient one benefits only himself. Thankfulness is the submission of the heart, its acknowledgment of God's blessing, the praise of the tongue for the One being thanked, the action of the limbs in obedience to Him, and not using His blessings to disobey Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verses 148–149:

{148} He, may He be exalted, informs that He does not love the public utterance of evil speech; that is, He dislikes it, abhors it, and punishes for it. This includes all evil speech that offends and grieves, such as insult, slander, abuse and the like, for all of that is among what is forbidden and which Allah dislikes. Its implication indicates that He loves good speech, such as remembrance of Allah and pleasant, gentle words. As for His saying: ﴿except by one who has been wronged﴾, that is, it is permissible for him to invoke harm upon one who has wronged him, to complain about him, and to speak evil openly to one who has spoken evil to him publicly, provided he does not lie against him, does not exceed his wrong, and does not extend his insult beyond the one who wronged him. Nevertheless, pardoning him and not retaliating is better, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is upon Allah﴾, and ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing﴾.

Since the verse included evil speech, good speech and permissible speech, Allah the Exalted informed that He is Hearing, so He hears your words. Therefore beware of speaking what angers your Lord, lest He punish you [for it]. In this there is also an encouragement toward good speech. ﴿Knowing﴾ of your intentions and the sources of your words.

{149} Then the Exalted said: ﴿If you disclose good or conceal it﴾. This includes every good deed, verbal and physical, apparent and hidden, whether obligatory or recommended. ﴿Or pardon an evil﴾; that is, pardon the one who has harmed you in your bodies, your wealth, or your honor, so that you forgive him. For the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: whoever pardons for Allah's sake, Allah pardons him, and whoever does good, Allah does good to him. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾; that is, He pardons the slips and great sins of His servants, drapes His concealment over them, and then deals with them through His complete pardon, which issues from His power.

In this verse there is guidance toward gaining understanding of the meanings of Allah's names and attributes, and that creation and command proceed from them, and they necessitate them. Therefore He gives the reasons for rulings by the Most Beautiful Names, as in this verse. When He mentioned doing good and pardoning the offender, He linked that to knowledge of His names, referring us to them, and that this suffices us from mentioning their specific reward.

{150} Here there are two categories that have become clear to everyone: a believer in God and in all His messengers and books, and a disbeliever in all of that. A third category remains: one who claims to believe in some of the messengers and not others, and claims that this path will save him from the punishment of God. Whoever opposes any one of His messengers has opposed God and opposed all of His messengers, as He said: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah...﴾ [2:98], and the verses that follow. Likewise, whoever disbelieves in one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers, indeed in the very messenger he claims to believe in.

Nothing remains after that except whim, desire, and mere assertion, which anyone can answer with its equal. This is true faith and certainty founded upon proof. ﴿Those, He will soon give them their rewards﴾; that is, the recompense for their faith and what follows from it of righteous deeds, good speech, and beautiful character, each according to his condition. {153–158} This question that the People of the Book put to the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), out of obstinacy and as a demand, and by making their belief or disbelief depend upon it, was that they asked him to send down the Qur'an to them all at once, just as the Torah and the Gospel were sent down. They killed another and crucified him; their claim that their hearts are uncircumcised, not understanding or comprehending what you say to them; their hindering people from the way of God, so they hindered them from the truth, and called them to the error and deviation in which they themselves were; and their taking of illicit gain and usury, despite God's prohibition of them and His stern warning against it. Since the purpose of enumerating these ugly deeds of theirs that God enumerated was this comparison, He did not expand upon it in this place, but alluded to it and referred to its places; and He has expanded upon it in other places, in the appropriate context for its expansion.

{159} As for His saying: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Him before his death﴾: it may be that the pronoun in His saying "before his death" refers to the People of the Book, so that according to this, every Scripturist who is present at death and witnesses the matter in reality will believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, but it is a faith that will not benefit him; it is faith of compulsion. {159} As for His saying: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Him before his death﴾: it may be that the pronoun in His saying "before his death" refers to the People of the Book, so that according to this, every Scripturist who is present at death and witnesses the matter in reality will believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, but it is a faith that will not benefit him; it is faith of compulsion. Thus the content of this threat and warning to them is that they should not persist in this state, over which they will regret before their death; so how will their condition be on the day of their gathering and standing?! And it may be that the pronoun in His saying: "before his death" refers back to Jesus, peace be upon him, so the meaning is: there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in the Messiah, peace be upon him, before the death of the Messiah, and that will occur when the Hour draws near and its major signs appear; for the sound hadiths have multiplied concerning his descent, peace be upon him, at the end of this Ummah: he will kill the Dajjal, abolish the jizyah, and the People of the Book will believe in him along with the believers. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾: Jesus, peace be upon him, will be a witness against them, testifying to their deeds and whether they conform to the law of God or not. At that time he will bear witness only to the falsity of everything they are upon that opposes the Shari'ah of the Qur'an. And when Muhammad (ﷺ) called them to it, we know this from our knowledge of the perfect justice and truthfulness of the Messiah, peace be upon him, and that he bears witness only to the truth; except that what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought is the truth, and whatever else is error and falsehood.

{160–161} Then God the Exalted informed that He forbade the People of the Book many of the good things that had been lawful to them. This was a prohibition as punishment, because of their wrongdoing, their transgression, their hindering people from the way of God, and their preventing them from guidance, and because of their taking usury when they had been forbidden it, so they withheld from the needy among those they traded with justice. So God punished them in kind with their deed, forbidding them many of the good things they were about to make lawful because they were good. As for the prohibition upon this Ummah, it is a prohibition of purification for them from the wicked things that harm them in their religion and their worldly life.

{162} When he mentioned the faults of the People of the Book, he mentioned those among them who are praised, saying: {But those firm in knowledge}; that is, those in whose hearts knowledge is established and in whose hearts certainty has taken firm root, so that it bore for them complete and comprehensive faith, {and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you}. It also bore for them righteous deeds, such as establishing the prayer and giving the zakah, which are the best of deeds, and both of which encompass sincerity toward the One worshipped and kindness toward His servants. They believed in the Last Day, so they feared the threat and hoped for the promise. {Those We will give them a great reward}; because they combined knowledge, faith, righteous deeds, and belief in the earlier and later books and messengers.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 163–165:

{163} He, exalted is He, informs that He revealed to His servant and messenger the great Law and the true reports, just as He revealed them to those prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. In this there are several benefits. Among them: Muhammad (ﷺ) is not a novelty among the messengers; rather, God sent before him a great number and a vast multitude of messengers. So marveling at his message has no basis except ignorance or obstinacy.

Among them: He revealed to him, as He revealed to them, the fundamentals and the justice upon which they all agreed, and that some of them confirm others and some of them agree with others.

Among them: he is of the same kind as these messengers, so let the one who takes heed consider him alongside his fellow messengers. His call is their call, their characters are in harmony, their source is one, and their goal is one. Thus He did not join him with the unknown, nor with the liars, nor with the oppressive kings.

Among them: in mentioning these messengers and enumerating them there is an honoring of them, a true praise of them, and an explanation of their conditions, by which the believer increases in faith in them, in love for them, in following their guidance, in adopting their way, and in knowing their rights. This is a fulfillment of His saying: ﴿Peace be upon Noah among the worlds﴾ ﴿Peace be upon Abraham﴾ ﴿Peace be upon Moses and Aaron﴾ ﴿Peace be upon Elias. Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾. So every doer of good has a good praise among mankind in accordance with his goodness, and the messengers, especially these named ones, are in the highest rank of goodness.

When He mentioned their sharing in His revelation, He mentioned the specification of some of them. He mentioned that He gave David the Psalms, which is the well-known written book, which God singled out for David, peace be upon him, for his excellence and nobility. And that He spoke to Moses directly (taklim), meaning verbally from Him to him without intermediary, so that this became famous among all the worlds, so it is said: Moses, the one spoken to by the Most Merciful.

{164} And He mentioned that among the messengers are those whom God related to His messenger, and among them are those He did not relate to him. This indicates their great number.

{165} And that God sent them as bearers of good news to whoever obeys God and follows them, with worldly and otherworldly happiness, and as warners to whoever disobeys God and opposes them, with the wretchedness of both abodes; ﴿so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾, who would say: "No bearer of good news nor warner came to us." Say: "There has come to you a bearer of good news and a warner." Thus no argument remains for creation against God, since He sent the messengers in succession, clarifying for them the matter of their religion, what pleases their Lord and what angers Him, and the paths to Paradise and the paths to Hell. Whoever disbelieves after that, let him blame no one but himself. This is from the perfection of His might and wisdom, that He sent messengers to them and sent down books upon them. And this is also from His grace and kindness, since people were in the greatest imaginable need of the prophets, so He removed this need. So to Him belong praise and thanks, and we ask Him, just as He began His blessing upon us by sending them, to complete it by granting success in following their path; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful.

As for His words, {He has sent it down with His knowledge}, it may be that the meaning is: He sent it down containing His knowledge; that is, within it are divine sciences, legislative rulings and unseen reports that belong to the knowledge of God, which He taught to His servants. It may also be that the meaning is: He sent it down proceeding from His knowledge. In that case there is an indication and a reminder of the manner of His testimony: the meaning is that since God sent down this Qur'an, which includes commands and prohibitions, and He knows that, and He knows the condition of the one to whom He sent it down, and that he called people to it, then whoever responds to him and affirms him becomes His ally, and whoever denies him and opposes him becomes His enemy, and his wealth and blood are made lawful; and God empowers him, continually grants him victory, answers his supplications, humiliates his enemies and grants victory to his allies. Is there any testimony greater or more magnificent than this testimony?! Yet this testimony cannot be discredited except after discrediting God's knowledge, power and wisdom. As for His informing of the testimony of the angels to what He sent down to His Messenger, it is due to the perfection of their faith and the greatness of what is witnessed to; for great matters are not testified to except by the elite, as God said regarding the testimony to monotheism: {God bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [bear witness also], [He is] maintaining justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise} and {And sufficient is God as a witness}.

{167} When He informed of the message of the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, and informed of the message of their seal, Muhammad, and bore witness to it, and His angels bore witness, it followed that the established and attested matter was affirmed, and it became obligatory to confirm them, to believe in them, and to follow them. Then He threatened those who disbelieve in them, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah﴾; that is, they combined disbelief in themselves with barring people from the way of Allah. These are the leaders of disbelief and the callers to misguidance. ﴿They have certainly gone far astray﴾. And what misguidance is greater than the misguidance of one who goes astray himself and leads others astray? He bears the burden of two sins, returns with two losses, and is deprived of two guidances!

{168–169} For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit injustice﴾. This injustice is in addition to their disbelief; otherwise, when "injustice" is mentioned absolutely, disbelief is included in it. The intended meaning of injustice here is: the actions of disbelief and immersion in it. These people are far from forgiveness and from being guided to the straight path. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to any path, except the path of Hellfire﴾. Forgiveness and guidance were rendered impossible for them only because they persisted in their transgression and increased in their disbelief; thus a seal was set upon their hearts, and the paths of guidance were closed to them because of what they had earned. ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾; that is, Allah does not concern Himself with them nor care for them, because they are not fit for good, and nothing befits them except the state they chose for themselves.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 170:

{170} He, exalted is He, commands all people to believe in His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and He mentions the reason that necessitates belief in him, the benefit of believing in him, and the harm of not believing in him.

The necessitating reason is His statement that he has come to them with the truth; that is, his coming itself is true, and what he brought of the law (shari'ah) is true. For the intelligent person knows that for creation to remain in its ignorance, wandering blindly, and in its disbelief, hesitating, while the messengership has been cut off from them, is inconsistent with the wisdom and mercy of God. Thus, from His great wisdom and mercy is the very sending of a messenger to them, to make known to them guidance from error and misguidance from rectitude. Merely considering his message is a decisive proof of the soundness of his prophethood. Likewise, considering what he brought of the great law and the straight path, for in it are reports of the unseen past and future, and information about God and the Last Day that no one could know except through revelation and messengership, and in it is the command to every good, righteousness, rectitude, justice, benevolence, truthfulness, piety, maintaining of kinship, and good character, and the prohibition of evil, corruption, oppression, injustice, bad character, lying, and disobedience to parents, by which it is certain that it is from God. Whenever the servant's insight increases through it, his faith and certainty increase. This is the reason that calls to belief.

As for the benefit of belief, He informed that it is good for {you}, and good is the opposite of evil. Belief is good for believers in their bodies, hearts, souls, worldly life, and the Hereafter, because of the benefits and advantages that follow from it. Every reward, immediate and deferred, is among the fruits of belief. Victory, guidance, knowledge, righteous deeds, joy and happiness, and Paradise with its bliss all result from belief, just as worldly and otherworldly misery results from the absence of belief or its deficiency.

As for the harm of not believing in him (ﷺ), it is known by the opposite of what follows from believing in him, and that the servant harms only himself. God, exalted is He, is independent of him; the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm Him. For this reason He said: {Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth}; that is, all of it is His creation, His dominion, and under His management and disposal. {And Allah is ever Knowing}: of everything {Wise}: in His creation and His command. So He is the Knowing of who deserves guidance and error, the Wise in placing guidance and error in their proper places.

This is the commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 171:

{171} Almighty God forbids the People of the Book from ghuluw (exaggeration) in religion, which is going beyond the limit and the lawful measure into what is not lawful. This is like the saying of the Christians in their exaggeration regarding ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon him, and raising him above the station of prophethood and messengership to the station of lordship (rububiyyah), which is not fitting for anyone other than God. Just as falling short and neglecting are forbidden, so too is exaggeration. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not say about God except the truth﴾. This statement contains three things: two matters that are forbidden, namely speaking falsehood about God and speaking without knowledge concerning His names, attributes, actions, legislation and messengers; and a third matter that is commanded, namely speaking the truth about these matters.

Since this is a general and comprehensive principle, and the context concerns the matter of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, He specified the truth about him, which differs from the way of the Jews and the Christians, saying: ﴿The Messiah, ʿIsa son of Maryam, was only a messenger of God﴾; that is, the ultimate attainment of the Messiah, peace be upon him, and the highest level of perfection he reached, is the highest state that created beings can attain, which is the rank of messengership, the highest of ranks and the most glorious of rewards. And that He is ﴿His word which He directed to Maryam﴾; that is, a word by which God spoke, and through it ʿIsa came into being. He was not that word itself; rather, he came into being by it. This is in the category of attributing something to honour and dignify it. Likewise His saying: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾; that is, from the spirits which He created and perfected with virtuous attributes and complete character. God sent His spirit, Jibril, peace be upon him, who breathed into the womb of Maryam, peace be upon her, and she conceived ʿIsa, peace be upon him, by God's permission.

When He clarified the reality of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, He commanded the People of the Book to believe in him and in His messengers, and forbade them from making God the third of three, one of whom is ʿIsa and the second Maryam. This is the saying of the Christians, may God curse them, so He commanded them to desist, and informed that this is better for them, because it is the path that is definitively the way of salvation, and whatever else is other than it is the paths of destruction. Then He declared Himself free of any partner or offspring, saying: ﴿God is only one God﴾; that is, He alone is the one singled out for divinity, to whom alone worship is due. ﴿Glory be to Him﴾; that is, He is exalted and sanctified ﴿above having a son﴾, because ﴿to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾; all are owned by Him and in need of Him, so it is impossible that He should have a partner or a son from among them.

When He informed that He is the owner of the upper and lower worlds, He informed that He sustains their worldly and otherworldly interests, guards them, and recompenses them for them, exalted is He:

{172} When Allah mentioned the exaggeration (ghulluw) of the Christians regarding ʿIsa (peace be upon him), and mentioned that he is His servant and messenger, He here mentioned that he does not disdain (yastankif) worshipping his Lord; that is, he does not refrain from it out of aversion to it. Neither do ﴿the angels brought near﴾. So He declared them free of disdaining, and their freedom from arrogance (istikbar) is by greater priority. The negation of a thing implies the affirmation of its opposite. That is: ʿIsa and the angels brought near have desired the worship of their Lord, loved it, and striven in it in a manner befitting their states, and this earned them that great nobility and great success. So they do not disdain to be servants of His lordship or His divinity; rather, they see their need for that as greater than every need. It should not be thought that elevating ʿIsa or any other creature above the rank in which Allah placed him, and rising above worship, is perfection; rather, it is deficiency itself, and it is the place of blame and punishment. For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself﴾; that is, He will gather all creatures to Himself, those who disdain and are arrogant and His believing servants, and He will judge between them with His just judgment and His decisive recompense.

{173} Then He detailed His judgment concerning them, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾; that is, they combined the faith that was commanded with doing righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended, of the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants. ﴿He will pay them their rewards﴾; that is, the rewards He ordained for deeds, each according to his faith and deed. ﴿And He will increase them from His bounty﴾: of reward that their deeds did not attain, that their actions did not reach, and that did not occur to their hearts. This includes all that is in Paradise of food, drink, spouses, sights, joy, the delight of the heart and soul, and the delight of the body; indeed, it includes every worldly and religious good ordained for faith and righteous deeds. ﴿As for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾; that is, toward the worship of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, which is the wrath and anger of Allah and the kindled Fire that rises over the hearts. ﴿And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾; that is, they will not find any creature who will take charge of them to obtain what they seek, nor anyone who will help them to repel what they fear. Rather, the Most Merciful of the merciful has forsaken them and left them in their punishment, abiding forever. And what Allah has judged is not to be repelled, nor is His decree to be changed.

For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself﴾; that is, He will gather all creatures to Himself, those who disdain and are arrogant and His believing servants, and He will judge between them with His just judgment and His decisive recompense.

{173} Then He detailed His judgment concerning them, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾; that is, they combined the faith that was commanded with doing righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended, of the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants. ﴿He will pay them their rewards﴾; that is, the rewards He ordained for deeds, each according to his faith and deed. ﴿And He will increase them from His bounty﴾: of reward that their deeds did not attain, that their actions did not reach, and that did not occur to their hearts. This includes all that is in Paradise of food, drink, spouses, sights, joy, the delight of the heart and soul, and the delight of the body; indeed, it includes every worldly and religious good ordained for faith and righteous deeds. ﴿As for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾; that is, toward the worship of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, which is the wrath and anger of Allah and the kindled Fire that rises over the hearts. ﴿And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾; that is, they will not find any creature who will take charge of them to obtain what they seek, nor anyone who will help them to repel what they fear. Rather, the Most Merciful of the merciful has forsaken them and left them in their punishment, abiding forever. And what Allah has judged is not to be repelled, nor is His decree to be changed.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 174–175:

{174} He (Exalted is He) bestows favour upon all of mankind by conveying to them decisive proofs and shining lights, establishing the proof against them and making the path clear to them. So He said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord﴾; that is, decisive arguments upon the truth which clarify it and make it evident, and make its opposite clear. This includes both rational and transmitted evidences, and the signs in the horizons and in the selves. ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾. In His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾ there is an indication of the nobility and greatness of this proof, since it comes from your Lord who nurtured you with religious and worldly upbringing. Among His nurturing of you, for which He is to be praised and thanked, is that He conveyed to you the clear signs so that He might guide you by them to the straight path and to attaining the Gardens of Bliss. And He sent down to you ﴿a manifest light﴾, which is this Great Qur'an, which includes the knowledge of the first and the last, true and beneficial reports, and the command to every justice, goodness and good, and the prohibition of every wrong and evil. So people are in darkness if they do not illuminate themselves with its lights, and in great misery if they do not draw from its goodness.

{175} But people divided, according to their faith in the Qur'an and their benefit from it, into two categories: ﴿As for those who believed in Allah﴾; that is, they acknowledged His existence, His being described with every perfect attribute, and His being exalted above every imperfection and defect. ﴿And held fast to Him﴾; that is, they took refuge in Allah, relied upon Him, disavowed their own power and strength, and sought help from their Lord. ﴿Then He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty﴾; that is, He will envelop them with special mercy, granting them success in goodness, bestowing abundant rewards upon them, and repelling from them afflictions and hardships. ﴿And guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾; that is, He will grant them success in knowledge and action, knowing the truth and acting upon it. As for whoever does not believe in Allah, nor holds fast to Him, nor adheres to His Book, He withholds from them His mercy, deprives them of His bounty, and leaves them to themselves, so they are not guided, but rather go astray in manifest error, as a punishment for them for abandoning faith. Thus they incur disappointment and deprivation. We ask Him, exalted is He, for pardon, well-being and security.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 4, verse 176:

{176} He, may He be exalted, informs that the people asked His Messenger (ﷺ) for a ruling (yastaftoona) concerning the kalalah (a person who dies leaving neither a direct descendant nor an ascendant); that is, concerning the kalalah. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾. The kalalah is the deceased who dies leaving no son in the direct line, no son's son, no father, and no grandfather. For this reason He said: ﴿If a man dies leaving no child﴾, that is, neither male nor female, neither a direct son nor a son's son. Likewise, he has no father; the evidence is that He made the brothers (al-ikhwah) heirs in this case, and by consensus (ijma') siblings do not inherit alongside a father. So when he dies leaving neither child nor father, ﴿and he has a sister﴾, that is, a full sister or a paternal sister (from the father only, not the mother), since her ruling has already been mentioned earlier. ﴿She receives half of what he leaves﴾, that is, half of the estate of her brother in money, property, household goods, and other things, after the payment of debts and bequests, as was mentioned previously. ﴿And he inherits from her if she has no child﴾, that is, her full brother or paternal brother inherits from her, and He did not assign him a fixed share because he is a residuary heir ('asib), so he takes all her property if there is no sharer (sahib fard) or residuary heir who shares with him, or what remains after the fixed shares. ﴿If there are two sisters﴾, that is, two or more, ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves.﴾ ﴿And if there are brothers, men and women﴾, that is, if male siblings from the non-uterine line gather together with female siblings, ﴿to the male is the like of the share of two females﴾: thus the fixed share of the females falls away and their brothers make them residuary heirs ('assabahunna).

﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾, that is, He makes clear to you the rulings that you need, explains them, and expounds them to you out of His bounty and kindness, so that you may be guided by His clarification and act by His rulings, and so that you do not stray from the straight path through your ignorance and lack of knowledge. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, that is, He is aware of the unseen and the witnessed, of past and future matters, and He knows your need for His clarification and instruction, so He teaches you from His knowledge that benefits you constantly in all times and places.

End of the commentary on Surah an-Nisa'. So to Allah belongs all praise and thanks.
